2	title: "The cursor in a recording"
3	description: "Choose whether the pointer is kept out of a screen recording for Frame Job to draw, or drawn into the movie by macOS, and how clicks are shown."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A screen recording can keep the pointer out of the movie, so Frame Job draws it on the clip and you can restyle it later, or have macOS draw it into the picture for good. You choose before you record, because the choice is part of the movie.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
12	  keys="⌥⌘N"
13	  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Cursor', 'New Recording panel ▸ Show Clicks']}
14	  tools="record_screen"
15	/>
16	
17	## Choose Separate or In the picture
18	
19	Set **Cursor** on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).
20	
21	| | **Separate** | **In the picture** |
22	| --- | --- | --- |
23	| The pointer | Kept out of the movie. Frame Job draws it on the clip. | Drawn into the movie by macOS. |
24	| Restyle it later | Yes, in the clip's **Cursor** section. | No. It can't be changed or removed. |
25	| **Show Clicks** | Click ripples, drawn by Frame Job. | A ring drawn into the movie. |
26	| The **Cursor** section | Appears on the clip. | Doesn't appear. |
27	| Cursor file | Written | Written |
28	
29	**Separate** is the default for every screen source: displays, windows and picked windows. Your choice is remembered, and once you've made one it holds for every source.
30	
31	Both write a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) beside the movie, so [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), [shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) and [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) work either way.
32	
33	With **Separate**, the pointer appears wherever Frame Job draws the clip, in the preview and in every export. The movie file on its own has no pointer, so opened in another app it shows none.
34	
35	**Cursor** is greyed out, keeping its value, with **Camera** or **Microphone Only** as the source, and while a recording is under way.
36	
37	## Show clicks
38	
39	**Show Clicks** marks each mouse click. It's off by default, and greyed out with **Camera** or **Microphone Only**.
40	
41	- **With In the picture**, macOS draws a ring around each click into the movie. It can't be removed afterwards.
42	- **With Separate**, nothing is drawn into the movie. Frame Job draws the ripples from the cursor file, and you can edit them afterwards.
43	
44	## What a Separate recording lands with
45	
46	The clip gets a **Cursor** section on the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, with the pointer drawn as recorded. See [Style the recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/) for what you can change there.
47	
48	With **Show Clicks** on as well, the clips land with **Clicks** set to **Ripple**, in the same undo step as the recording. In a new project where that's the only other change, the undo step is called **Cursor Clicks**. Undoing it takes the ripples off and keeps the pointer.
49	
50	Nothing else is set. To smooth the pointer's path and hide it when it's idle, choose **Polish** in the same section.
51	
52	## What an In the picture recording lands with
53	
54	The pointer is in the movie and the cursor file says so, so the clip shows no **Cursor** section and nothing is drawn twice.
55	
56	## Good to know
57	
58	If a **Separate** stretch's cursor file couldn't be written, that stretch has no pointer at all: it isn't in the movie and there's nothing to draw it from. It gets no ripples either. The panel's note says so, with "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."
59	
60	## With an agent
61	
62	`record_screen` takes `cursor`, either `separate` or `in_picture`, and leaving it out means `separate`. Its `show_clicks` is `false` unless the agent sets it. Neither can be used with a voice-over or a camera on its own. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#pointer-and-keys).
63	
64	## Related

67	- [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/)
68	- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
69	- [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/)
70	---
71	title: "Style the recorded cursor"
72	description: Change how a recording's pointer looks after you've recorded it, from its size and path to when it hides and a ring on every click.
73	---
74	
75	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
76	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
77	
78	When a screen recording keeps its pointer out of the movie, Frame Job draws the pointer for you, so you can restyle it long after you stopped recording. The **Cursor** section makes it bigger, calms a shaky path, hides it when it rests and puts a ring on every click.
79	
80	<AtAGlance
81	  where="Clip tab ▸ Picture ▸ Cursor"
82	  tools={['set_video', 'paste_attributes', 'get_cursor_events']}
83	  needs="A screen recording made with Cursor set to Separate, the default, so its pointer isn't in the movie."
84	/>
85	
86	## Find the Cursor section
87	
88	<Steps>
89	
90	1. Select a recording's clip on the timeline.
91	
92	2. Open the **Clip** tab's **Picture** sub-tab.
93	
94	3. Open the **Cursor** section, after **Background**. It starts shut.
95	
96	</Steps>
97	
98	The section's header sums up what's set: **off**, **on** or **arrow**, with **+ ripples** when clicks ripple.
99	
100	The section is there only when every selected clip comes from a movie with a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) that the picture doesn't already show:
101	
102	- A recording made with **Cursor:** set to **In the picture** has no section, because the pointer is part of the movie and would otherwise be drawn twice. See [The cursor in a recording](/recording/cursor/).
103	- A movie with no cursor file has no section. If the file exists but didn't come along, [attach it with Locate…](/recording/cursor-files/#attach-or-re-point-a-cursor-file).
104	- A selection that also holds any other kind of clip has no section.
105	
106	A freeze frame of a recording has the section too, with the pointer held where it was on that frame.
107	
108	Each row is its own undo step. If the selected clips disagree about a row, it shows as mixed.
109	
110	## Tidy the pointer in one click
111	
112	Choose **Polish** at the bottom of the section. It sets **Smoothing** to **Medium** and **Hide when idle** to **3 s**, as one undo step called "Polish Cursor". Nothing else changes, and you can adjust either row afterwards.
113	
114	## The controls
115	
116	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
117	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
118	| **Show cursor** | Draws the pointer. | On | On, off |
119	| **Size** | How big the pointer is drawn. | 100 % | 25–800 % |
120	| **Style** | Which pointer is drawn. | As recorded | As recorded, Arrow |
121	| **Smoothing** | Calms a shaky path. | Off | Off, Light, Medium, Strong |
122	| **Hide when idle** | Fades out a resting pointer. | Never | Never, 1, 2, 3, 5 or 10 s |
123	| **Clicks** | Draws a ring out of every click. | None | None, Ripple |
124	| **Ripple color** | The ring's colour, with opacity. | White at 80 % | Any colour |
125	| **Ripple size** | How big the ring grows. | 100 % | 25–400 % |
126	
127	## Show or resize the pointer
128	
129	Untick **Show cursor** to draw no pointer on this clip. Click rings are separate, so with **Clicks** set to **Ripple** the rings still draw without a pointer. That's useful when you want to show where someone clicked and nothing else.
130	
131	**Size** has quick picks at 50, 100, 150, 200 and 400 %. Its slider runs to 400 %, and you can type up to 800 % in the field.
132	
133	## Choose the pointer's style
134	
135	**Style** offers **As recorded** and **Arrow**. Frame Job's recordings don't store pictures of the pointer, so both choices draw Frame Job's arrow, and a pointer that was an I-beam or a hand on screen is drawn as the arrow too. The only difference you'll see is that the section's header reads **arrow** rather than **on**.
136	
137	Frame Job's arrow is a black arrow with a white outline, 14 by 21 points at 100 %. It's drawn at the recording's own pixel density and redrawn for each **Size** rather than stretched, so it stays crisp.
138	
139	## Calm a shaky path
140	
141	**Smoothing** irons out the wobble in the pointer's path, from **Light** through **Medium** to **Strong**. The pointer still reaches every click exactly, at the moment of the click, and a pause stays a pause.
142	
143	## Hide a resting pointer
144	
145	**Hide when idle** fades the pointer out after the time you pick with no movement and no mouse press. Scrolling and typing don't count as activity. The fade takes 0.2 s, and the pointer comes back 0.15 s before it next moves or clicks, so it's already there when it sets off.
146	
147	## Show clicks
148	
149	Set **Clicks** to **Ripple** to draw a ring growing out of every press of a mouse button. A ring lasts 0.45 s, growing quickly at first and fading as it goes, and up to four can show at once. At 100 % it reaches 24 points from the click.
150	
151	**Ripple color** and **Ripple size** are live only while **Clicks** is **Ripple**. **Ripple size** has quick picks at 50, 100, 150 and 200 %.
152	
153	**Clicks** starts at **None**, unless the recording was made with **Show Clicks:** on and **Cursor:** set to **Separate**. Those clips land with **Ripple** already set.
154	
155	## Put everything back
156	
157	**Reset** in the section's header appears once something differs from its default. It sets all eight rows back to the defaults in the table, as one undo step called "Reset Cursor".
158	
159	## Change the pointer part-way through a clip
160	
161	Select an [action](/motion/actions/) on the clip and the section edits that action instead of the whole clip:
162	
163	| Rows | With an action selected |
164	| --- | --- |
165	| **Size**, **Ripple size** | Animate across the action. |
166	| **Show cursor**, **Style**, **Clicks**, **Ripple color** | Switch at the action's end. The row says **at end**. |
167	| **Smoothing**, **Hide when idle** | Always change the clip itself. Their rows show ⊘. |
168	
169	**Polish** also changes the clip itself, whatever is selected. **Reset** isn't offered while an action is selected. Once the action holds a cursor change, the section's header shows **Clear** in its place, which takes every cursor change out of that action as one undo step called "Clear". **Smoothing** and **Hide when idle** stay as they are on the clip.
170	
171	The first time you change one of the action rows on a clip with no cursor settings of its own, Frame Job stores the defaults on the clip in the same step. That's what lets **Size** and **Ripple size** animate from 100 % instead of jumping.
172	
173	## Copy the settings to another clip
174	
175	**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) carries a clip's cursor settings to another clip, along with the rest of its picture settings. The settings are replaced as a whole, so pasting from a clip whose cursor you never changed puts the target's back to the defaults. See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).
176	
177	## Streak a moving pointer
178	
179	With the clip's **Motion Blur** above 0, in the **Transform** section, a moving pointer is streaked along its path across the shutter. That happens even when the clip itself stands still. A still pointer and the click rings stay sharp.
180	
181	The streak shows in the preview, in rendered frames and in every export. A clip that [motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) draws sharp keeps its pointer sharp, and so does a freeze frame.
182	
183	## How the pointer sits in the picture
184	
185	The pointer is drawn inside its clip, as if it were part of the movie. So it follows the clip's zooms, placement and crop, it takes the clip's grade, and the preview, rendered frames and exports all agree. In an HLG project the pointer and its rings are lifted to match the picture.
186	
187	It also follows the clip's time. Change the clip's speed and the pointer speeds up with it. [Reverse the clip](/speed/reverse/) and the pointer plays backwards too.
188	
189	## Good to know
190	
191	- A cursor file loads in the background and never holds up the preview. Until it's ready the frame draws without the pointer, then redraws with it. Changing **Smoothing** can do the same for a moment, because the new path has to be worked out. Rendered frames and exports wait for the file.
192	- **Hide when idle** and the ring's 0.45 s count in the recording's own time, so on a clip at 2× they pass twice as fast.
193	- [Splitting](/editing/splitting/) a clip or making a freeze frame keeps the clip's own **Smoothing** and **Hide when idle**, even from inside an action.
194	- Paste onto a clip with no cursor file and the settings are kept but nothing is drawn.
195	- If a cursor file is missing or can't be read, the clip draws with no pointer. See [When a cursor file has a problem](/recording/cursor-files/#when-a-cursor-file-has-a-problem).
196	
197	## With an agent
198	
199	`set_video`'s `cursor` key sets the same eight values, and it isn't held to the pop-ups' steps. **Smoothing** can be any value from 0 to 1, where **Light** is 0.25, **Medium** 0.5 and **Strong** 1, and **Hide when idle** anything from 0.5 to 30 seconds. **Size** is a scale from 0.25 to 8 and **Ripple size** one from 0.25 to 4.
200	
201	`{cursor: {}}` stores all eight defaults on the clip and `cursor: null` clears them. Frame Job won't accept a value outside its range, and it doesn't round one to fit. See [the `cursor` key](/mcp/tools-set-video/#cursor) for the full list.
202	
203	To see what a recording's pointer did before styling it, an agent reads the [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/#with-an-agent) with `get_cursor_events`.
204

214	title: "Cursor files"
215	description: Understand the file that holds a recording's pointer, clicks and keys, how it follows its movie, and how to fix it when it doesn't.
216	---
217	
218	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
219	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
220	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
221	
222	A cursor file sits beside a screen recording and holds what the pointer did, so Frame Job can draw and restyle the pointer later. You rarely touch one. This page is for when a movie has moved, lost its file or picked up the wrong one.
223	
224	<AtAGlance
225	  where="Media tab ▸ Cursor"
226	  tools={['set_media_cursor', 'get_cursor_events']}
227	/>
228	
229	## What a cursor file holds
230	
231	Every recording of a display, a window or a picked window writes a cursor file, whichever **Cursor:** option you chose. A camera on its own and a voice-over don't, because they have no pointer. The file has the movie's name, ending in `.fjcursor`, and sits in the same folder:
232	
233	```
234	Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov
235	Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.fjcursor
236	```
237	
238	A paused recording has one movie per stretch between pauses, and each movie gets its own file.
239	
240	The file is plain text and records:
241	
242	- Where the pointer was, about 120 times a second.
243	- Every click and every scroll.
244	- How the recorded area sat on the screen, so a window that moved mid-recording still lines up.
245	- With [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on, the shortcuts you pressed and when you typed. A typed key is stored as a time only, never as a character.
246	
247	It holds no pictures of the pointer, so the pointer you see drawn is [Frame Job's arrow](/recording/cursor-settings/#choose-the-pointers-style).
248	
249	With **Cursor:** set to **In the picture**, the pointer is drawn into the movie as well and the file says so. Frame Job then draws nothing over the clip, and the clip has no **Cursor** section. The file is still used for its clicks and keys.
250	
251	[Style the recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/), [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) and [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) all read this file.
252	
253	## How the file follows its movie
254	
255	Frame Job keeps a movie and its cursor file together wherever it can. Keep them in the same folder with the same name when you move them by hand, and an import will find the file.
256	
257	### When a recording lands
258	
259	Each stretch's movie gets its own cursor file attached as it lands. You don't need to do anything.
260	
261	### When you import a movie
262	
263	When you import a movie, whether with **File ▸ Add Media…**, by dropping it on the window or by opening it, Frame Job looks beside the movie for a file with the same name ending in `.fjcursor`. It takes that file only if it reads as a cursor file and was made for a movie of exactly this size.
264	
265	A file that's missing, damaged or made for another size is left alone and the movie imports without it. Frame Job says nothing about it, so if a recording arrives with no **Cursor** section, check the [Media tab](#see-a-movies-cursor-file).
266	
267	A WebM or Matroska file is copied into a movie as it imports, and that copy isn't looked beside.
268	
269	### When you relink a movie
270	
271	[Relinking](/projects/relink-media/) takes the cursor file beside the new movie. If there's none, the media keeps the cursor file it already had, as long as that file is still there and the new movie is the same size. Otherwise the media has no cursor file after the relink, and you can attach one with **Locate…**.
272	
273	### When you consolidate
274	
275	[Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies each cursor file into the package beside its movie, and a moved package finds it there again when you open it.
276	
277	If a cursor file is missing, Consolidate leaves it alone and its report says so, for example "1 cursor file was missing and left alone." If a copy fails, the media goes on pointing at the original file. A movie that's missing is left alone along with its cursor file.
278	
279	## See a movie's cursor file
280	
281	Select a video in the **Media** tab's list and read its **Cursor** section. The section appears once the project has a video with a picture.
282	
283	<Shot
284	  name="10b-media-tab.inspector"
285	  alt="The Media tab with three files in its list and nothing selected. Below the list, the Camera Log section reads Select a video in the list, and the Cursor section at the bottom has a File row with dimmed Locate… and Remove buttons."
286	/>
287	
288	| The section says | What it means |
289	| --- | --- |
290	| "Select a video in the list" | Nothing that can carry a cursor file is selected. |
291	| "No cursor file" | This video has none attached. |
292	| The file's name | The file is attached and on disk. |
293	| The file's name, then "— missing" | The file is attached but has gone from where it was. |
294	
295	## Attach or re-point a cursor file
296	
297	Use **Locate…** to give a video its cursor file, or to point it at one that has moved.
298	
299	<Steps>
300	
301	1. Select the video in the **Media** tab's list.
302	
303	2. In the **Cursor** section, choose **Locate…**.
304	
305	3. Choose the `.fjcursor` file recorded with this movie.
306	
307	</Steps>
308	
309	Frame Job runs the same check as an import: the file must read as a cursor file made for a movie of exactly this size. If it passes, that's one undo step called "Locate Cursor File". If it doesn't, an alert titled "The cursor file was not attached" gives the reason and nothing changes. For example:
310	
311	- "The cursor file *name* was not attached: its movie_size is 3024 × 1964 and the movie is 1920 × 1080."
312	- "The cursor file *name* was not attached: this is not a Frame Job cursor file…"
313	
314	A cursor file from a newer version of Frame Job gets the same alert, which says which version the file is.
315	
316	## Forget a cursor file
317	
318	Choose **Remove** in the **Cursor** section. The video stops using the file, as one undo step called "Remove Cursor File". The file itself stays on disk, so you can choose **Locate…** to bring it back. **Remove** is dimmed for a video with no cursor file.
319	
320	## When a cursor file has a problem
321	
322	A cursor problem never fails a recording or an export. You always get the movie, and Frame Job tells you what's missing.
323	
324	### While recording
325	
326	If a stretch's cursor file can't be written, the recording still lands and the panel's note says why, naming the file:
327	
328	| The note says | What it means |
329	| --- | --- |
330	| "The cursor file *name* could not be written…", "…was not kept…", "…could not be put in place…" | The file couldn't be saved, or it failed the check Frame Job makes once it's written. No file was left behind. |
331	| "The cursor file for *name* was not written: no cursor was captured for it." | Nothing was captured for this stretch. |
332	| "The cursor file for *name* was not written: the screen never reported its start, so its times have nothing to count from." | Without a start time, the pointer can't be matched to the picture. |
333	| "The cursor file for *name* has only the geometry the screen had when it began…" | A file exists, but a move or resize of what was recorded after the start isn't in it, so the pointer can sit in the wrong place after that. |
334	
335	A stretch recorded **Separate** with no cursor file has no pointer at all, because it isn't in the movie and there's nothing to draw it from. The note ends "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."
336	
337	### While exporting
338	
339	If a cursor file can't be drawn, because it's missing or damaged, the clip exports without a pointer and the export finishes as normal. The export's finish line counts the problem, for example "1 cursor warning (hover for details).", and hovering lists each one. The [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) shows the count on the job's row, with the same list in its tooltip:
340	
341	> The cursor of media 3 is not drawn: …
342	
343	### In the preview
344	
345	A missing or damaged cursor file draws no pointer, and the preview says nothing. Check the **Media** tab, and use **Locate…** if the name reads "— missing".
346	
347	## Good to know
348	
349	- Moving a cursor file away doesn't take the clip's **Cursor** section with it. The section stays, and nothing is drawn until the file is back.
350	- Removing or re-pointing a cursor file doesn't touch the [settings on its clips](/recording/cursor-settings/). They wait for the next file.
351	
352	## With an agent
353	
354	An agent can read what a cursor file holds, which the app doesn't show you as a list. `get_cursor_events` returns a recording's clicks, scrolls, shortcuts and stretches of typing and, if asked, the pointer's path, ten times a second. Give it a media to read in the file's own time, or a clip to read in the clip's time, where each click and scroll also comes with its place in the clip's picture, ready for a zoom. It returns at most 5,000 rows at a time and says where to carry on. It edits nothing, runs on your Mac and needs no key.
355	
356	It won't read a clip that plays reversed, though it can read that clip's media, and it needs a media with a cursor file that's still on disk.
357	
358	`set_media_cursor` attaches, moves or removes a file as **Locate…** and **Remove** do, under the same check, and its `in_picture` value must match the file's. A cursor file belongs to the project's media, so the tool won't work from inside a nest.
359	
360	`record_screen` names each stretch's cursor file as `cursor_path` and any problem with it as `cursor_problem`. `export_status` lists a pointer it couldn't draw under `cursor_warnings`, and `render_frame` says so in its reply. See [Tools: recording and screencasts](/mcp/tools-recording/).
361

370	title: "Auto Zoom"
371	description: "Zoom a screen recording in where things happen, planned from its cursor file, with every zoom left as an ordinary action you can change."

373	
374	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
375	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
376	
377	Auto Zoom moves a screen recording in where things happen. It reads the recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/), arrives at each click as it happens, stays while you keep working there, and zooms back out once you stop, so a viewer can see what you clicked without you zooming each moment by hand.
378	
379	<AtAGlance
380	  menu="Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…"
381	  where="Zoom in on clicks, under When it lands: in the recorder panel"
382	  tools="auto_zoom"
383	  needs="A recording with a cursor file. Nothing else: it plans from that file on your Mac, with no picture analysis and no key."
384	/>
385	
386	## Zoom a recording
387	
388	<Steps>
389	
390	1. Select one or more clips of a screen recording. **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** is available when every selected clip is a movie with a cursor file, and no sheet is up. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/) too.
391	
392	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. The sheet reads "Reading cursor files…" and **Zoom** is dimmed until they're read and there's a plan.
393	
394	3. Adjust the [controls](#the-controls). The line under them [says what you'd get](#what-the-sheet-tells-you).
395	
396	4. Choose **Zoom**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.
397	
398	</Steps>
399	
400	The whole plan is one undo step, **Auto Zoom**.
401	
402	## The controls
403	
404	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
405	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
406	| **Zoom:** | How far in, as a multiple of the clip's own size. | 2× | 1.25 to 4× |
407	| **Arrive:** | How long the zoom takes, in seconds. It starts this long before the click and is fully in on the click. | 0.6 s | 0.2 to 2 s |
408	| **Stay:** | How long the zoom holds after the last click or typing before it starts back out. | 2.5 s | 0.5 to 10 s |
409	| **Follow the cursor while zoomed** | Pans along when the pointer stays near the edge of the zoomed view. | On | |
410	| **Zoom on typing** | Zooms in on stretches of typing as well as clicks. | On when the recording holds typing | |
411	| **Replace existing zooms** | Removes the clips' existing zooms first. | Off | |
412	| **Motion blur** | Gives each zoomed clip a 50 % motion blur. | On | |
413	
414	The number fields take up to two decimal places, and each value is held to its range.
415	
416	### Follow the cursor while zoomed
417	
418	When the pointer stays outside the middle 70 % of the zoomed view for 0.3 s, the view makes a half-second pan to it. It makes at most one of these pans a second, and none that would run into the zoom back out or a pan to a coming click.
419	
420	### Zoom on typing
421	
422	A stretch of typing is at least three typed keys, each less than a second after the last. The zoom arrives at the first key and aims at the last click before the stretch, because the typing marks say when you typed, not where. With no click before it, the zoom aims at where the pointer was.
423	
424	**Zoom on typing** is greyed out when the recording holds no such stretch. A recording only holds typing if it was made with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on, which needs macOS's **Input Monitoring** permission.
425	
426	### Replace existing zooms
427	
428	Off, your own zooms stay, and a planned zoom that would meet one is [left out](#the-zooms-are-ordinary-actions). On, the selected clips' zooms go first. A zoom here is any action that changes only a clip's scale and position, so it takes hand-made zooms from [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) as well as Auto Zoom's own. A speed change, a fade or any other action stays.
429	
430	### Motion blur
431	
432	The zoomed clips get a 180° shutter in the same undo step, so the zooms and pans blur along their movement. Only clips that actually get a zoom are touched. A clip that already has a [Motion blur](/motion/motion-blur/) keeps its own, and unticking the box doesn't take one away.
433	
434	## What the sheet tells you
435	
436	The line under the controls says what **Zoom** would do, or why it can't. It updates when you tick a box or leave a number field.
437	
438	| The sheet says | What it means |
439	| --- | --- |
440	| "5 zooms in 2 visits." | What **Zoom** would make. A [visit](#how-a-visit-is-planned) is one trip in and back out. Each zoom in, pan and zoom back out counts as one zoom, so a click with nothing after it is two. |
441	| "1 dropped where an action is already set." | Follows the line above: that many planned zooms [met an action](#the-zooms-are-ordinary-actions) already on the clip and were left out. |
442	| "0 zooms in 0 visits." | Nothing in the clips' played part calls for a zoom. **Zoom** closes the sheet and changes nothing, unless **Replace existing zooms** is on, when it still removes the clips' zooms. |
443	| "Clip 12 is placed smaller than the canvas…" | See [A clip placed smaller than the canvas](#a-clip-placed-smaller-than-the-canvas). |
444	| "Clip 12 plays reversed; Auto Zoom plans only clips that play forward." | Auto Zoom only works on clips that play forward. Take the clip out of the selection, or untick [Reverse](/speed/reverse/). |
445	| "Clip 12 has no picture." | The selection includes a clip with sound only. Select the picture. |
446	| "Media 3's cursor file … is missing…" | The file has moved or gone. Use **Locate…** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section to point at it. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |
447	| "The cursor file … could not be read…" | Frame Job couldn't read the file, and the sentence gives the reason. |
448	
449	With any of the last five, **Zoom** stays dimmed.
450	
451	### A clip placed smaller than the canvas
452	
453	Auto Zoom won't plan a clip that sits smaller than the canvas, such as a screen beside a camera or a picture in picture, because a zoom would fill the canvas. The sheet says "Clip 12 is placed smaller than the canvas; a zoom would fill the canvas. Nest it (Clip ▸ Nest) and run Auto Zoom inside the nest."
454	
455	The way round this is to zoom inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), then place the nest:
456	
457	<Steps>
458	
459	1. Select the clip and choose **Clip ▸ Nest**.
460	
461	2. Open the nest. The clip keeps its small placement in there, so Auto Zoom gives the same message until you make the clip fill the nest again. Set its [scale and position](/canvas/transform/) back.
462	
463	3. Run Auto Zoom inside the nest. The zooms fill the nest.
464	
465	4. Leave the nest, and place the nest clip where the screen was.
466	
467	</Steps>
468	
469	Nest the screen before you shrink it and there's nothing to set back in step 2.
470	
471	## How a visit is planned
472	
473	Auto Zoom groups the recording's activity into visits, and each visit becomes a run of moves.
474	
475	- **A visit starts** at a click with any button, or at a stretch of typing when **Zoom on typing** is on.
476	- **The zoom in** ends on that first click or key, and starts **Arrive:** seconds before it.
477	- **A later click or stretch of typing** within **Stay:** of the last activity joins the visit. If it falls outside the middle 60 % of the view, the view pans to it, arriving on the click or first key.
478	- **The zoom back out** starts **Stay:** seconds after the last click or the last key of a typing stretch, and takes 0.8 s.
479	- **Scrolling ends a visit.** Three or more wheel events under a second apart count as scrolling, and the zoom back out starts where they start. A click after that begins a new visit.
480	- **Visits close together run on.** When one visit would finish zooming out less than a second before the next starts zooming in, the view pans across instead.
481	
482	The view keeps the canvas's shape and never shows past the edge of the picture, or of a crop on the clip. Near a corner it stops at the corner, so the click sits off centre.
483	
484	Only what plays counts. A click in a part you've trimmed away is ignored, and everything is placed through the clip's speed and any speed ramp.
485	
486	## The zooms are ordinary actions
487	
488	Each zoom in, pan and zoom back out is a normal [action](/motion/actions/) on the clip's [action lane](/motion/action-lane/), the same kind [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/) makes. Each is snapped to the frame grid and eases in and out. You can [move, resize or remove](/motion/change-an-action/) any of them, or [change what it animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
489	
490	Actions on a clip can't overlap, so a planned zoom that would meet one already there is left out and counted in the sheet. This goes piece by piece, so a visit can lose its zoom in and keep its zoom back out. Check those visits by eye.
491	
492	To try different settings after you've applied a plan, undo it, or run Auto Zoom again with **Replace existing zooms** on. Run again without it and the new plan meets the old one, and most of it is dropped.
493	
494	## Across a split
495	
496	The halves of a split clip are planned as one recording: clips side by side on one track, from the same file, each carrying on where the last stopped.
497	
498	- Every zoom back out returns to the first half's placement.
499	- No zoom crosses a cut. One that would is moved to one side of it.
500	- A zoom held across a cut carries into the next half, which starts already zoomed. Frame Job does this by setting that half's own scale and position.
501	- If that half wasn't selected, or has an action of its own during the zoom, the zoom goes back out at the cut instead.
502	
503	With **Replace existing zooms** on, a later selected half left zoomed by an earlier run goes back to the first half's placement, unless an action you've kept moves it.
504	
505	## What Auto Zoom remembers
506	
507	Frame Job remembers **Zoom:**, **Arrive:**, **Stay:**, **Follow the cursor while zoomed**, **Replace existing zooms** and **Motion blur** from one use to the next. A value is kept only if you changed it and then chose **Zoom**. **Cancel** keeps nothing.
508	
509	**Zoom on typing** is never remembered. It's ticked whenever the recording holds typing.
510	
511	## Zoom when a recording lands
512	
513	**Zoom in on clicks**, under **When it lands:** in the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), runs Auto Zoom by itself on a finished screen recording, with the values the sheet last used and no sheet. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).
514	
515	## Good to know
516	
517	- A click right at the start of a clip has no room before it. The zoom in starts on the clip's first frame and takes its full **Arrive:** time, so it finishes after the click.
518	- **Zoom:** multiplies the size the clip is placed at, so a clip already scaled up goes further in than the number suggests.
519	- If the menu item is dimmed, check the selection. Recordings of a display or a window made in Frame Job have a cursor file. A camera on its own, a voice-over, a title and a movie from elsewhere don't, and one such clip in the selection is enough to dim it.
520	
521	## With an agent
522	
523	`auto_zoom` plans and applies the same zooms, with the sheet's settings as arguments. An agent can also limit the plan to a stretch of the timeline, in which case replacing removes only the zooms in that stretch, and set a motion blur other than 50 %. See [Tools: recording and screencasts](/mcp/tools-recording/).

558	## Turn it on
559	
560	<Steps>
561	
562	1. Choose **File ▸ New Recording…**.
563	
564	2. Set **Source:** to a display or a window.
565	
566	3. Tick **Record shortcuts**. It's off to begin with, and the panel remembers your choice for the next recording.
567	
568	4. Press **Record**. The first time, you'll need to [grant Input Monitoring](#grant-input-monitoring).
569	
570	</Steps>
571	
572	A note under the box says what it records. The box is greyed out for **Camera** and **Microphone Only**, which have no screen to go with the keys. It keeps its tick for when you go back to a screen source.
573	
574	While keys are being recorded, the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) shows a keyboard mark before the time, and its menu opens with a dimmed "Recording keyboard shortcuts" row. Everything lands in the recording's [cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/).
575	
576	## Grant Input Monitoring
577	
578	Recording keys needs macOS's **Input Monitoring** permission. macOS shows no prompt for it, and Frame Job isn't in that pane's list until you add it, so pressing **Record** without the permission stops the recording from starting and opens System Settings for you.
579	
580	<Steps>
581	
582	1. Press **Record**. System Settings opens at **Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring**, and the panel's note says what to do.
583	
584	2. Turn Frame Job on. If it isn't in the list, add it with **+**.
585	
586	3. Back in the panel, press **Record** again. You don't need to relaunch.
587	
588	</Steps>
589	
590	Frame Job asks for this after Screen Recording, and before the camera and the microphone. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/) for all of them, and for what changes if you started Frame Job from a terminal.
591	
592	## What counts as a shortcut
593	
594	A key press is a shortcut when you hold:
595	
596	- <kbd>⌘</kbd> or <kbd>⌃</kbd> with any key.
597	- <kbd>⌥</kbd> with an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc.
598	
599	<kbd>⇧</kbd> on its own never makes a shortcut, and neither does <kbd>⌥</kbd> with any other key, because that types a character: <kbd>⌥E</kbd> starts an é.
600	
601	A shortcut is stored with its keys spelled out, such as `cmd+shift+4`. The modifiers come first, in the order `cmd`, `ctrl`, `opt`, `shift`. The key comes last: a named key such as `return`, `tab`, `space`, `left` or `f5`, or otherwise the character the key types with no modifier, in lower case. `+` itself is spelled `plus`.
602	
603	## What happens to everything else
604	
605	Every other key press is stored as a typing mark, which is a moment in time and nothing more. It doesn't say which key it was. Frame Job doesn't read the character of a typed key at all, and there's no mode that records what you type.
606	
607	A key held down until it repeats gives typing marks too, even if it began as a shortcut. Holding <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> is one shortcut and then a run of typing marks.
608	
609	## When nothing is recorded
610	
611	Nothing at all is recorded while any app holds secure input, as a password field does: no shortcut, and not even a typing mark.
612	
613	A password field that doesn't turn on secure input is different, such as a Terminal `sudo` prompt with Secure Keyboard Entry off. Its keys are recorded as typing marks only, with no characters.
614	
615	Keys you press while the recording is [paused](/recording/pause-and-stop/) aren't recorded.
616	
617	:::caution
618	The keys stay out of the file, but the movie is still a picture of your screen. A password that shows on screen as you type it is in the recording.
619	:::
620	
621	## What you can do with the keys
622	
623	| Feature | What it uses | Where |
624	| --- | --- | --- |
625	| [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) | The shortcuts, shown on screen as you pressed them. | **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays**, or **Show shortcuts** in the panel |
626	| [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) | The typing marks, to find the stretches to speed up. | **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**, or **Speed up typing** in the panel |
627	| [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/) | The typing marks, to zoom in where you typed. | **Zoom on typing** in **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** |
628	
629	**Show shortcuts** and **Speed up typing** are in the panel's **When it lands:** rows, and they're greyed out unless **Record shortcuts** is ticked, because the cursor file would have no keys for them to use.
630	
631	## With an agent
632	
633	`record_screen` records keys when it's given `keys: "shortcuts"`. The default is `off`. It never asks macOS for the permission. Without Input Monitoring it won't start, and it names the System Settings pane, so someone has to grant it in the panel first. It won't record keys from a voice-over or a camera on its own. `get_cursor_events` reads the shortcuts and stretches of typing back. See [Tools: recording and screencasts](/mcp/tools-recording/).
634

644	title: "Shortcut overlays"
645	description: "Show each keyboard shortcut you pressed while recording as animated keycaps on screen, at the moment you pressed it."
646	---
647	
648	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
649	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
650	
651	Shortcut overlays show a viewer what you pressed. Each keyboard shortcut in a screen recording appears as keycaps on screen at the moment you pressed it, so nobody has to guess how you did that.
652	
653	<AtAGlance
654	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays"
655	  where="Show shortcuts, under When it lands: in the recorder panel"
656	  tools="add_shortcut_overlays"
657	  needs="A recording made with Record shortcuts on, which needs macOS's Input Monitoring permission. No key: it runs on your Mac."
658	/>
659	
660	## Add the overlays
661	
662	<Steps>
663	
664	1. Make the recording with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on. Only shortcuts are recorded, never what you typed.
665	
666	2. Select one or more clips of the recording. The menu item is available when every selected clip is a movie with a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) and no sheet is up. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/) too.
667	
668	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays**.
669	
670	</Steps>
671	
672	There's no sheet. Frame Job reads the cursor files, with the item dimmed while it does, and places one **Keyboard keys** graphic clip per shortcut on a [Shortcuts track](#the-shortcuts-track). Each sits at the bottom of the picture in the dark theme and shows for 1.5 s.
673	
674	The whole change is one undo step, **Add Shortcut Overlays**. If some shortcuts couldn't be shown, or nothing could be added, a [sheet says so](#what-the-sheet-tells-you).
675	
676	## What an overlay shows
677	
678	The keycaps pop in one after another, each is pressed in turn, and the group fades out at the end of the clip. ⌘, ⇧, ⌥, ⌃ and the arrow keys are drawn as symbols, a single character as its capital, and a named key such as `return` or `f5` as its word.
679	
680	## How overlays are timed
681	
682	**Where it starts.** An overlay starts on the frame where the press plays, following the clip's speed and any speed ramp. Only the part of a clip that plays counts, so a shortcut in a part you've trimmed away gets no overlay.
683	
684	**How long it lasts.** Each overlay lasts 1.5 s, and never less than the keycaps need to press in turn and fade out. That minimum is (10 × keycaps + 25) frames at the project's frame rate:
685	
686	| Keycaps | Minimum at 30 fps | Minimum at 60 fps |
687	| --- | --- | --- |
688	| 2 | 45 frames, 1.5 s | 45 frames, 0.75 s, so the overlay lasts 1.5 s |
689	| 3 | 55 frames, about 1.83 s | 55 frames, about 0.92 s, so the overlay lasts 1.5 s |
690	| 4 | 65 frames, about 2.17 s | 65 frames, about 1.08 s, so the overlay lasts 1.5 s |
691	
692	**When you repeat a shortcut.** Pressing the same shortcut again before its overlay ends doesn't make a second overlay. The first stays up until at least 1.5 s after the last press and carries a label under the keycaps: "×2", "×3" and so on.
693	
694	**When shortcuts come close together.** Overlays never overlap. A different shortcut pressed while one is showing takes over as soon as the first has had its minimum, and the first ends there. If that would show the new shortcut more than half a second late, it's left out, and a sheet says how many were.
695	
696	## The Shortcuts track
697	
698	Overlays go on the front-most track named **Shortcuts** when that track is usable, and otherwise on a new **Shortcuts** track at the front. To be usable, the track must:
699	
700	- be in front of every selected clip's track
701	- be [unlocked and shown](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)
702	- not be a [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/)
703	- have nothing on it from the first overlay's start to the last overlay's end
704	
705	Inside an open nest, the track and the overlays go in the nest.
706	
707	## Change an overlay
708	
709	Each overlay is an ordinary graphic clip. Move, trim or delete it on the timeline, and change its keys, label, theme, position or accent colour in its [Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/). To change them all at once, select them first.
710	
711	The overlays are drawn by the project's own copy of the bundled [Keyboard keys template](/graphics/templates/). Frame Job writes that copy into the project's graphics the first time something is placed, and reuses it after. If you've [edited that copy](/graphics/edit-a-module/), it leaves your version alone and writes a fresh one beside it for new overlays.
712	
713	Undo takes the clips away but not the copy, which stays in the project's graphics for next time.
714	
715	## What the sheet tells you
716	
717	An informational sheet comes up when something didn't go as asked. Only the "too close" sheet comes with a change to the project.
718	
719	| The sheet says | What it means |
720	| --- | --- |
721	| "No shortcut was recorded in the selected clips' played windows, so nothing was added." | The part of the recording that plays holds no shortcut. Check that the recording was made with **Record shortcuts** on. |
722	| "1 shortcut came too close to show." | The overlays were added, without that many. With more it reads "3 shortcuts came too close to show." |
723	| "Clip 12 plays reversed; Add Shortcut Overlays places only clips that play forward." | Overlays only work on clips that play forward. Take the clip out of the selection, or untick [Reverse](/speed/reverse/). |
724	| "Media 3's cursor file … is missing…" | The file has moved or gone. Use **Locate…** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section to point at it. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |
725	| "The cursor file … could not be read…" | Frame Job couldn't read the file, and the sentence gives the reason. |
726	| "The project changed while the cursor files were read, so no overlay was added. Choose Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays again." | You edited the project, or opened or left a nest, while the files were being read. Nothing was added. |
727	
728	## Show shortcuts when a recording lands
729	
730	**Show shortcuts**, under **When it lands:** in the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), adds the overlays by itself on a finished screen recording, at the bottom in the dark theme. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).
731	
732	## Good to know
733	
734	- Add the overlays before you run [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/). It keeps each overlay on a Shortcuts track at normal speed.
735	- Running the command again on the same clips doesn't replace the overlays. The Shortcuts track isn't free any more, so you get a second Shortcuts track with the same overlays on it. Undo first if you want to start over.
736	
737	## With an agent
738	
739	`add_shortcut_overlays` places the same overlays. An agent can also choose how long each one shows, from 0.5 to 10 s, put them at the centre or top of the picture, use the light theme, and limit them to a stretch of the timeline. See [Tools: recording and screencasts](/mcp/tools-recording/).

750	title: "Speed Up Typing"
751	description: "Play the typing in a screen recording faster, while speech and shortcuts stay at normal speed, as one undo step."
752	---
753	
754	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
755	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
756	
757	Speed Up Typing plays the typing in a screen recording faster, so a viewer doesn't sit through every keystroke. Frame Job finds the typing from the recording's cursor file, leaves anything spoken or any shortcut at normal speed, and makes the whole change one undo step.
758	
759	<AtAGlance
760	  menu="Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…"
761	  where="New Recording panel ▸ When it lands ▸ Speed up typing"
762	  tools={['speed_up_typing', 'get_cursor_events']}
763	  needs="A screen recording made with Record shortcuts on. Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
764	/>
765	
766	## Speed up the typing
767	
768	<Steps>
769	
770	1. Select the clip. Select both halves if you've split the recording, and any other recordings you want done at the same time.
771	
772	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**. It has no keyboard shortcut. The sheet reads "Reading cursor files…" for a moment, with **Apply** dimmed.
773	
774	3. Set [**Rate**, **Shortest stretch** and **Keep pitch**](#the-settings).
775	
776	4. Read the summary under the settings, for example "2 typing stretches sped up ×4, saving 9.3 s."
777	
778	5. Choose **Apply**, or **Cancel** to leave the timeline as it was.
779	
780	</Steps>
781	
782	The menu item is dimmed unless every selected clip is a movie with a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). It's also dimmed while another sheet is open. It works inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), on the nest's own clips and tracks.
783	
784	The edit is one undo step, **Speed Up Typing**.
785	
786	To do this for every recording as it arrives, tick **Speed up typing** in the recorder panel. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/#speed-up-typing).
787	
788	## What counts as typing
789	
790	A typing stretch is a run of at least 3 typed keys, each less than 1 s after the last. It lasts from the first key to the last.
791	
792	The keys come from the recording's cursor file, which only holds them if the recording was made with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) on. Without it the menu item still works, but the sheet finds no typing. The file holds when you typed, never what you typed, and nothing is noted while an app holds secure input, such as a password field.
793	
794	Only typing in the part of the clip you've kept counts. Typing you've trimmed away is ignored.
795	
796	### Split recordings
797	
798	The halves of a recording you split are treated as one when you select them both and they touch, so typing across the cut is one stretch. With one half selected, Frame Job only looks at that half.
799	
800	## The settings
801	
802	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
803	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
804	| **Rate:** | How much faster the typing plays. | ×4 | ×2 to ×8 |
805	| **Shortest stretch:** | Typing shorter than this is left alone. | 3 s | 1 to 30 s |
806	| **Keep pitch** | Keeps the sped-up sound at its own pitch. Off, it rises like a fast tape. See [Keep pitch](/speed/keep-pitch/). | On | |
807	
808	The two number fields take up to two decimal places, and their values stay inside the range. The summary updates when you leave a field or change **Keep pitch**.
809	
810	Frame Job remembers these from one use to the next. It saves a setting when you apply the edit, and only if you changed it, so **Cancel** saves nothing.
811	
812	## What the sheet tells you
813	
814	The sheet says what **Apply** would do before you press it, or why nothing would happen.
815	
816	| The sheet says | What it means |
817	| --- | --- |
818	| "2 typing stretches sped up ×4, saving 9.3 s." | What **Apply** will do. |
819	| "No typing stretch without speech or a shortcut lasts 3 s or more in the selected clips, so nothing would change." | There's nothing to speed. **Apply** stays dimmed. Try a lower **Shortest stretch**. The figure in the sentence follows that setting. |
820	| "Waiting for speech detection on …" | Frame Job is still finding the speech in the files it names. **Apply** is dimmed, and the sheet updates by itself. |
821	| "Speech detection has not finished for … Close this sheet and try again." | It waited 5 minutes and stopped. |
822	| "… is offline, so its speech cannot be read." | A file under a stretch is missing, so nothing changes. [Relink it](/projects/relink-media/) first. |
823	| "Speech detection is unavailable on this Mac, so Speed Up Typing cannot tell typing from talking." | Speech detection can't run here, so nothing changes. |
824	| "The typing from … cannot be sped up: …" | One stretch can't be sped. See [When it can't speed up](#when-it-cant-speed-up). |
825	
826	## What stays at normal speed
827	
828	Within each stretch, Frame Job sets aside every moment of speech and every shortcut, and leaves them at normal speed. What's left is sped up, if it still lasts as long as **Shortest stretch**.
829	
830	### Speech
831	
832	Any part of a stretch with speech under it stays at normal speed. That goes for every clip of a file with sound under the stretch, on any track, even if the clip is muted. So a voice on the Microphone track holds the typing back the same way sound in the movie does.
833	
834	The speech comes from the same on-device detection [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/#where-the-speech-comes-from) uses. If a file has no saved speech, Frame Job saves it with the project in the same undo step. If detection hasn't finished, the sheet starts it and waits.
835	
836	### Shortcuts
837	
838	A recorded shortcut and its overlay are never sped up. What stays at normal speed is the overlay's whole clip on a track named **Shortcuts**, or 1.5 s from the press when there's no overlay.
839	
840	[Add the overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) first, so that each one's full length stays at normal speed.
841	
842	### The edges
843	
844	Each sped stretch keeps 0.3 s at normal speed at both ends. **Shortest stretch** is measured before those edges come off. A 3 s stretch at ×4 speeds its middle 2.4 s down to 0.6 s, which saves 1.8 s. Cuts then land on frames, so the figures can differ slightly.
845	
846	## What the edit does to the timeline
847	
848	Each stretch is sped with [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) on every unlocked track, so the camera and the microphone stay in sync with the screen and everything after moves up. A title or a graphic over a stretch is squeezed by the same amount, as Retime Range does it.
849	
850	The sound in a sped stretch is sped too, because it's cut and retimed with the picture.
851	
852	
853	## If a clip would go silent
854	
855	Rates multiply, so a clip already playing at ×2 goes to ×16 at a **Rate** of ×8. Frame Job leaves a clip's sound out above ×12, so when **Apply** would take a clip with sound past that, an alert asks first.
856	
857	**Set Speed** goes ahead. **Cancel** leaves the sheet open with nothing changed, so you can lower the **Rate**. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
858	
859	## When it can't speed up
860	
861	Speed Up Typing is all or nothing. If any stretch can't be sped, nothing changes, **Apply** is dimmed, and the sheet names the stretch and the reason in place of the summary.
862	
863	| What stops it | What to do |
864	| --- | --- |
865	| A locked track has a clip that ends after the stretch begins. | [Unlock the track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). |
866	| A transition touches the stretch. | Remove the [transition](/motion/add-a-transition/). |
867	| Half of a detached pair is in the stretch. | Use [Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) first. |
868	| A selected clip plays reversed. The sheet reads "Clip … plays reversed; Speed Up Typing speeds only clips that play forward." | Leave that clip out, or [turn off Reverse](/speed/reverse/). |
869	| The cursor file is missing or won't read. | Use **Locate…** in the **Cursor** section of the Media tab. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/). |
870	
871	A stretch can also be stopped by anything else that stops Retime Range, such as a nest clip or a caption page with timed words. See [When a range can't be retimed](/speed/retime-range/#when-a-range-cant-be-retimed).
872	
873	## With an agent
874	
875	`speed_up_typing` makes the same edit, with these differences:
876	
877	- It takes one clip or a list of clips, not both, rather than reading the selection.
878	- It can limit the edit to part of the timeline, which the sheet can't.
879	- It doesn't remember anything. It starts from ×4, 3 s and pitch kept unless told otherwise.
880	- It doesn't wait for speech detection. It says the speech hasn't been detected yet, and to try again in a moment.
881	- It never asks about ×12. The clip's sound is left out, and it reports that when it finishes.
882	
883	`get_cursor_events` reads a recording's typing stretches and changes nothing. See [Tools: recording and screencasts](/mcp/tools-recording/#speed_up_typing).

7	
8	`record_screen` is **File ▸ New Recording…** without the panel. An agent says how many seconds to record, the call runs for that long, and the recording lands in the project the way one made with the panel does. There's no countdown, and the tool never asks for a permission.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
12	  tools="record_screen"
13	  needs={[
14	    'Screen Recording permission, for a screen recording',
15	    'Microphone, Camera or Input Monitoring, only when the call uses them',
16	    'A person has to give each permission first',
17	  ]}
