504	
505	## Record the screen and the camera
506	
507	<Steps>
508	
509	1. Choose **File ▸ New Recording…**, and set **Source** to a display or **Window…**.
510	
511	2. Tick **Record the camera too**. **Camera**, **Format**, **Layout** and **Remove the camera's background when it lands** go live, and a live preview of the camera appears under **Format**.
512	
513	3. Choose the camera in **Camera**, and its size and frame rate in **Format**. [Record a camera](/recording/record-a-camera/) explains both lists.
514	
515	4. Choose a [layout](#choose-a-layout).
516	
517	5. Choose a **Microphone** if you want your voice. The camera's movie has no sound of its own.
518	
519	6. Press **Record**. Frame Job checks its permissions, then counts down from 3.
520	
521	7. The panel leaves the screen. Pause and stop from the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or the **File** menu.
522	
523	</Steps>
524	
525	**Record the camera too** is off until you tick it, and Frame Job remembers it between launches. It's live only with a display or **Window…** as the source. **Camera** and **Microphone Only** grey it out, keeping its value.
526	
527	**System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows** and **Rate** stay live and apply to the screen, and the note under **Size** describes the screen. The camera records at the frame rate of its **Format**.
528	
529	### What Record checks
530	
531	Pressing **Record** stops at the first thing missing, in this order:
532	
533	1. A window, when **Source** reads **Window…** with none picked. The panel says "Choose a window with Window… first, or pick a display."
534	2. A camera. With none connected, the panel says "No camera is connected."
535	3. The Screen Recording permission.
536	4. The Input Monitoring permission, only with [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) ticked.
537	5. The Camera permission.
538	6. The Microphone permission, only with a microphone chosen.
539	
540	[Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/) says what each one asks of you.
541	
542	### The preview
543	
544	The camera starts as soon as you tick the box, so it has usually settled at its frame rate by the time recording begins. Unticking the box, choosing **Microphone Only** or closing the panel turns it off.
545	
546	The preview shows the chosen camera at the chosen format. When it can't, it says why:
547	
548	| The preview says | What it means |
549	| --- | --- |
550	| "No camera is connected." | There's no camera to show. |
551	| "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera." | You haven't allowed the Camera permission yet. Showing the panel never asks for it. Pressing **Record** does, or opens System Settings if you've turned it down. |
552	| "The camera is recording." | An agent is recording a camera right now. The picture comes back when it ends. |
553	| Another sentence | The reason the camera couldn't start. Untick and tick the box, or reopen the panel, to try again. |
554	
555	## Choose a layout
556	
557	**Layout** sets how the camera sits with the screen when the recording lands.
558	
559	| Layout | What it does |
560	| --- | --- |
561	| **Corner** | The default. The camera sits in the bottom-right corner, scaled to fit a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % guide of [**View ▸ Safe Areas**](/canvas/safe-areas/). |
562	| **Rounded Corner** | The same corner with rounded edges. |
563	| **Circle** | The same corner as a circle. |
564	| **Side by Side** | The screen and the camera next to each other. |
565	| **Camera Full** | The camera fills the canvas. |
566	
567	**Layout** is live only with **Record the camera too** ticked. Otherwise, and while a recording is under way, it's greyed out and keeps its value. Frame Job remembers it between launches.
568	
569	The panel offers no other corner, and no **Stacked** or **Screen Only**. [**Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**](/framing/camera-layouts/) has those once the clip has landed. Neither offers a scale or an inset. Any crop the panel's layout makes centres on the camera's picture, not on the person.
570	
571	## The Camera track
572	
573	When the recording lands, each stretch's camera movie goes on one new track named **Camera**, in front of everything, lined up with that stretch's screen clip. A recording you never paused has one stretch. A paused one has [several](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches).
574	
575	Frame Job measures how far apart the camera and the screen started, for each stretch. The camera usually starts a moment first, so the clip's first frames are trimmed off rather than the clip starting early. A camera clip never starts before its screen clip, and never overlaps the camera clip before it.
576	
577	The camera files land in the same undo step as the screen:
578	
579	| Recording into | The undo step |
580	| --- | --- |
581	| An open project | **Add Recording**, for the screen, the camera and any microphone |
582	| A new project, one stretch | **Add Camera**, or **Add Camera and Microphone** with a microphone. The screen movie is the project itself. |
583	| A new project, several stretches | **Add Recording Segments** |
584	
585	[Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) covers the rest of the landing. Each camera file is named after its screen movie with ` (Camera)` added, for example `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov`.
586	
587	## How far the layout reaches
588	
589	The layout is one layout switch at the camera clip's first frame, the same kind **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸** makes, so the screen keeps its full picture until the camera arrives. It ends with that stretch's screen clip or its camera clip, whichever is later.
590	
591	That keeps it to this recording. A clip that was already in the project never moves, and another stretch's screen with no camera of its own stays full.
592	
593	If a stretch's screen clip is missing, or isn't playing where its camera starts, that camera goes in the bottom-right corner instead, whichever layout you chose.
594	
595	## Remove the camera's background
596	
597	Tick **Remove the camera's background when it lands** and Frame Job runs [**Clip ▸ Remove Background**](/effects/remove-background/) on the camera's clips as soon as they land. It works on your Mac, with no key.
598	
599	The box is off until you tick it, and Frame Job remembers it. It's greyed out, keeping its value, whenever **Layout** is.
600	
601	It's its own undo step, **Remove Background**, after the landing's and before any [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/) and the **When it lands:** boxes. **Edit ▸ Undo** takes it off and keeps the recording. If no camera clip landed, it does nothing and says nothing.
602	
603	## Change a camera clip afterwards
604	
605	Each camera clip stays an ordinary clip. You can move it, or give it another layout from [**Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**](/framing/camera-layouts/) or the [Layout section](/framing/layout-section/).
606	
607	## Good to know
608	
609	- If the camera stops on its own during the recording, for example because it's unplugged, the screen keeps recording. What the camera wrote lands, later stretches have no camera, and the panel's note gives the reason. If it stops while the recording is starting, the recording doesn't start.
610	- A camera file that would keep less than a frame after its trim stays in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) without a clip, and a note says so. If no camera clip can be placed, no **Camera** track is added.
611	- If a stretch is left out because its movie can't be read, its camera file stays on disk and the note names it, but it isn't added to the project.
612	
613	## With an agent
614	
615	`record_screen` makes the same recording when it names a camera, and it can choose any of the five layouts and remove the camera's background. If no camera clip landed, the agent is told so. Landing in an open project, an agent can also leave the recording's files in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) with no clips, which the panel doesn't offer. In that case no **Camera** track is added, and it can't ask for a layout or a removed background. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#record-a-camera-beside-the-screen).
616

631	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
632	
633	A recording can carry two sounds: what your Mac plays, and your voice. Frame Job keeps them apart, so you can set the level of each on its own after the recording lands.
634	
635	<AtAGlance
636	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
637	  keys="⌥⌘N"
638	  where={['New Recording panel ▸ System Audio', 'New Recording panel ▸ Microphone']}
639	  tools="record_screen"
640	  needs={['System Audio: the Screen Recording permission', 'Microphone: the Microphone permission']}
641	/>
642	
643	<Shot
644	  name="16-recorder-panel.panel"
645	  alt="The New Recording panel. Microphone is set to Off with a level meter beside it, and the System Audio switch below it is on."
646	/>
647	
648	## Record what your Mac plays
649	
650	**System Audio** records the sound from every app but Frame Job, as the movie's own stereo 48 kHz sound track. It's on until you turn it off, and Frame Job remembers your choice.
651	
652	With it off, the movie has no sound track at all. The switch applies to the screen, so **Camera** and **Microphone Only** in **Source** grey it out, keeping its value.
653	
654	## Play the timeline while you record
655	
656	Frame Job's own sound is never recorded, whether or not **Include Frame Job windows** is on. You can play your timeline during a recording and its sound won't be in the file.
657	
658	## Record your voice
659	
660	Choose a microphone in **Microphone**. **Off** comes first and is the default, then every connected microphone by name. Frame Job remembers your choice, and falls back to **Off** if that microphone isn't connected.
661	
662	It works with every source. With a picture, the voice goes into a second file beside the movie, named after it with ` (Microphone)` added, and never into the movie. With a microphone chosen, pressing **Record** also checks the [Microphone permission](/recording/permissions/).
663	
664	To clean your voice up as it lands, tick [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/). To record your voice with no picture, see [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/).
665	
666	## Check your level
667	
668	A meter sits beside **Microphone**. It starts moving at the countdown, not when you choose the microphone, so the 3, 2, 1 is your chance to check your level before the recording starts.
669	
670	It stays live through the recording, and goes silent while paused. For a display or a window the panel leaves the screen once recording begins, so you only see the meter during the countdown. For a camera on its own or a voice-over, the panel stays up and so does the meter.
671	
672	## Your first words are kept
673	
674	The microphone starts during the countdown, not when the recording does, so your first words are in the file. A camera's capture starts early the same way. Both are let go if you cancel the countdown, close the panel, or the start fails.
675	
676	## How the microphone lands
677	
678	Each file lands on one new track at the back, named **Microphone**, lined up with its picture, so your voice and the computer's sound have separate volumes.
679	
680	Frame Job measures how far apart the two files started, for each stretch of a [paused recording](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches) separately, and places the clip to match. The alignment is exact to half a frame.
681	
682	If your voice started before its clip could, at the very start of the timeline or right after the previous microphone clip, the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip being placed late.
683	
684	If no voice can be placed, no empty track is added. [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) covers the undo steps.
685	
686	## If the microphone stops
687	
688	A microphone that fails doesn't stop a screen or camera recording. The picture keeps going, the meter goes silent, and the panel's note reads "The microphone stopped: … The picture is still recording." That stretch's microphone file isn't added to the project. It stays on disk, and the note names it when the recording lands.
689	
690	A [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/#good-to-know) is different. With nothing else recording, it ends there.
691	
692	## Plug devices in and take them out
693	
694	The **Camera**, **Format** and **Microphone** lists follow the devices you plug in or take away.
695	
696	- Changes apply only while the panel is idle, so nothing moves during a countdown, a recording or a landing. A change that waited applies when the panel goes idle.
697	- A change made while the panel was closed is picked up when it next shows.
698	- A microphone you take away falls back to **Off**. A camera falls back to the default camera, or to **None connected** when there's no camera left.
699	- When a device comes back it's chosen again, and a camera comes back with its stored format.
700	- Plugging in or removing a device doesn't change what the panel remembers. The next control you change saves whatever the lists show at that moment, so a device that's away at that point is forgotten. The one exception is **None connected**, which leaves the remembered camera alone.
701	- A list is rebuilt only when its own devices changed, so a menu you have open isn't disturbed by an unrelated device.
702	
703	## With an agent
704	
705	An agent turns each sound on or off rather than choosing a device. Its microphone is your Mac's default microphone, off unless it asks. It can't ask for the Microphone permission either: that takes one press of **Record** in the panel. A microphone that fails doesn't fail an agent's recording, and the result says why. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#sound).
706

719	
720	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
721	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
722	
723	Press **Record**, count down from 3, pause when you need a break, and stop from wherever you're working. Frame Job then adds the recording to your project, which it calls landing. This page also says what happens if you close the panel or quit along the way.
724	
725	<AtAGlance
726	  menu={['File ▸ New Recording…', 'File ▸ Pause Recording', 'File ▸ Stop Recording']}
727	  keys="⌥⌘N"
728	  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Record', 'The menu-bar item while recording']}
729	  tools="record_screen"
730	/>
731	
732	## Start a recording
733	
734	<Steps>
735	
736	1. Set up the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) and press **Record**.
737	
738	2. Frame Job checks the [permissions](/recording/permissions/) it needs.
739	
740	3. The panel counts 3, 2, 1, a second each. **Record** reads **Cancel** meanwhile, and the [microphone meter](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/#check-your-level) already moves. Press **Cancel** or close the panel to stop, and nothing is recorded.
741	
742	4. The recording starts. For a display or a window, the panel leaves the screen and the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) takes over. With **Source** set to **Camera** or **Microphone Only**, nothing on screen is filmed, so the panel stays up.
743	
744	</Steps>
745	
746	## What the button says
747	
748	The panel's main button tells you where the recording has got to.
749	
750	| The button reads | What's happening | Pressing it |
751	| --- | --- | --- |
752	| **Record** | Nothing yet. | Starts the permission checks and the countdown. |
753	| **Cancel** | The countdown is running. | Ends it with nothing recorded. |
754	| **Starting…** | The recording is starting. | It's dimmed. |
755	| **Stop** | A recording runs or is paused. | Stops it and adds it to the project. |
756	| **Stopping…** | The files are being written. | It's dimmed. |
757	| **Adding…** | The files are being added to the project. | It's dimmed. |
758	
759	## If a recording doesn't start
760	
761	A recording that hasn't started within 20 seconds fails rather than hanging. The panel says "The recording did not start within 20 s." and goes back to **Record**. Any other failed start puts its reason in the same note.
762	
763	While the button reads **Starting…**, you can still stop with <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>, or by closing the panel. The **File** item may still read **New Recording…** at that moment. If Frame Job hadn't begun yet, the note reads "Stopped before the recording began; nothing was recorded." A moment later, it's too late to abandon: the recording ends as soon as it begins, and whatever it caught lands as usual.
764	
765	## One recording at a time
766	
767	Only one recording runs at a time. If you press **Record** while another runs or is paused, including one an agent started, the countdown runs and the panel then says "A recording is already in progress."
768	
769	## Pause and resume
770	
771	You can pause from any of these:
772	
773	- the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/)'s **Pause Recording**
774	- **File ▸ Pause Recording**, directly under **New Recording…**
775	- the panel's **Pause** button, for a [camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/) or a [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/)
776	
777	While paused, each of these reads **Resume Recording** or **Resume**. The **File** item is available only while a recording runs or is paused. Pausing has no keyboard shortcut.
778	
779	If Frame Job can't pause a recording you started, it beeps and the recording carries on. A resume that fails leaves it paused, with the reason in the panel's note: at once if the panel is up, otherwise when it comes back after you stop. Try again, or stop and land what you have.
780	
781	## Paused recordings are stretches
782	
783	A pause ends the current file and a resume starts a new one, so a paused recording is several stretches. Each stretch has its own movie, and its own microphone, camera and [cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/) when the recording has them.
784	
785	- Each file is named by the moment its stretch began.
786	- Each stretch keeps its own width, height and frame rate.
787	- The paused time is in no file, and the elapsed time counts only what was recorded.
788	
789	When the recording lands, the stretches sit end to end on one track, touching, with no transition between them. Each stretch's microphone goes on the **Microphone** track, lined up with its own picture.
790	
791	## Stop a recording
792	
793	You can stop a running or paused recording from any of these:
794	
795	- the menu-bar item's **Stop Recording**
796	- **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>). While any recording runs, **File ▸ New Recording…** reads **Stop Recording**, paused included.
797	- the panel's **Stop** button, for a camera on its own or a voice-over
798	
799	Frame Job writes the files and [adds the recording to your project](/recording/where-it-lands/). If it lands with nothing to report, a hidden panel [stays hidden](/recording/where-it-lands/#when-the-panel-comes-back). Press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> when you want it again.
800	
801	:::caution
802	There's no global shortcut to stop. <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> works in Frame Job's own menus, so it does nothing while another app is in front. Use the menu-bar item.
803	:::
804	
805	## Stop from macOS's indicator
806	
807	macOS shows its own indicator in the menu bar during a screen recording, and it can end the recording too. Frame Job keeps what was captured and adds it. The panel's note reads "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added." An agent's result says it was stopped this way.
808	
809	## The Welcome window during a recording
810	
811	The **New Recording…** button on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/) never stops a recording.
812	
813	- During a screen recording you started in the panel, it only beeps. Use **File ▸ Stop Recording** or the menu-bar item.
814	- During a camera recording, a voice-over or an agent's recording, it shows the panel.
815	
816	## If the panel closes
817	
818	A recording carries on if the panel closes, under the menu-bar item and **File ▸ Stop Recording**. You can only do this with a camera on its own or a voice-over, because the panel is off screen for anything else.
819	
820	Closing it at other moments is different:
821	
822	- During the countdown, it cancels the countdown and nothing is recorded.
823	- While the button reads **Starting…**, it counts as a Stop.
824	- Closing also lets go of a microphone or camera that was warming up for a recording.
825	
826	## Quit during a recording
827	
828	Choosing **Quit Frame Job** (<kbd>⌘Q</kbd>) during a recording doesn't quit. It puts the recording's controls in front of you, so you can stop or resume first:
829	
830	- With the panel hidden for a screen recording, it opens the menu-bar item's menu.
831	- For a camera recording, a voice-over or an agent's recording, it shows the panel.
832	
833	Frame Job reviews your unsaved projects before this. If that review closes the project you were recording into, the recording opens as a new project when it lands, and the note says so.
834	
835	## Stop an agent's recording
836	
837	A recording an agent starts shows the same menu-bar item, so you can pause, resume or stop it from there or from the **File** menu.
838	
839	Your Stop ends the agent's recording early, and what was recorded still lands. The agent's result shows the shorter length, and lists each stretch with the number of pauses. An agent asks for a length of real time, so a pause shortens what gets recorded rather than extending it. An agent has no way to pause or resume, and it has no countdown. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#a-person-can-pause-or-stop-it).
840

1	---
2	title: "When a recording stops on its own"
3	description: "What Frame Job keeps when a camera, a microphone or the system stops a recording, and what to do when a recording can't be added."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A recording can lose a device or end without you pressing Stop. Frame Job keeps what it captured, adds it to your project, and tells you what happened. This page calls that adding "landing". It says what lands in each case, and what to do about what doesn't.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where={["The recorder panel's note", 'The menu-bar item']}
12	  tools="record_screen"
13	/>
14	
15	## Where you'll read about it
16	
17	Unless a section says otherwise, each case here is reported in the note on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/). A recording that lands cleanly doesn't bring the panel back, but one with something to say does, as long as the panel was on screen when the recording began.
18	
19	If the panel wasn't on screen, press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> to open it and read the note.
20	
21	While a display or a window records, the panel is hidden, so the note only appears when the recording lands. While a camera on its own or a voice-over records, the panel stays up, so the note appears as it happens.
22	
23	## What's kept
24	
25	| What happened | Does the recording go on? | What lands |
26	| --- | --- | --- |
27	| [A camera on its own stops](#a-camera-stops) | No | What was captured |
28	| [A camera beside the screen stops](#a-camera-stops) | Yes | The screen, and the camera up to the stop |
29	| [The microphone stops](#a-microphone-stops) | Yes | The picture, and the microphone's file only if [it can be used](#a-microphone-stops) |
30	| [A voice-over's microphone stops](#a-voice-overs-microphone-stops) | No | What was recorded |
31	| [The display sleeps or goes away](#the-display-sleeps-or-the-system-stops-the-recording) | No | What was captured |
32	| [A stretch's movie won't read](#a-stretch-wont-read) | It has already ended | Every other stretch, and that stretch's voice if it reads |
33	| [A file is too short for a frame](#a-file-is-too-short-for-one-frame) | It has already ended | That file in the media list, and the rest as usual |
34	| [The recording can't be added](#the-recording-cant-be-added) | It has already ended | Nothing, but the files stay on disk |
35	
36	## A camera stops
37	
38	If a camera recording's camera stops, for example because it's unplugged, the recording ends there and what was captured lands. The note gives the reason, then "What was captured was added.":
39	
40	> The camera FaceTime HD Camera stopped on its own: it was disconnected. What was captured was added.
41	
42	It can also read "its session was interrupted", or give a reason from macOS.
43	
44	Beside the screen, a camera that stops doesn't end the recording. The screen keeps recording, what the camera wrote up to then lands, and the note gives the same reason. Anything you record after a later pause and resume has no camera. The one exception is a camera that fails while the recording is still starting. That stops the recording from starting, and the note gives the reason.
45	
46	If a camera hasn't settled at its rate when the recording begins, the recording begins anyway and the note says what it ran at:
47	
48	> The camera ran at 24.0 fps, not its 30, in the 1 s it was given to settle; the recording began anyway.
49	
50	## A microphone stops
51	
52	A microphone that stops partway through a screen or camera recording doesn't end it. The picture keeps recording and the panel's level meter goes silent. With the panel on screen, its note says so at once:
53	
54	> The microphone stopped: … The picture is still recording.
55	
56	The picture lands either way. If the microphone's file didn't finish properly or won't read, it isn't added, and the note says why and where the file is, so you can [import it](/projects/import-media/) yourself. In a camera recording, a microphone that stopped on its own isn't added even if its file is whole. The same goes for a microphone that never started, which reads "The microphone never started recording, so the picture was recorded without it."
57	
58	## A voice-over's microphone stops
59	
60	A voice-over has nothing else to record, so if its microphone stops on its own, for example because it's unplugged, the voice-over ends there. What was recorded lands, with a note:
61	
62	> The microphone stopped recording on its own: … The voice-over ends where it stopped.
63	
64	## The display sleeps or the system stops the recording
65	
66	If the display sleeps or goes away, or the system stops the recording, what was captured lands, with the note:
67	
68	> The system stopped the recording (the display slept or went away); what was captured was added.
69	
70	Stopping from macOS's own screen-recording indicator in the menu bar also lands the recording. The note reads "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added."
71	
72	## The screen is locked
73	
74	If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, no display can be shared, so a screen recording can't start until one wakes. The panel's note reads "No display with id … is shareable…", or "No window with id … is shareable." for a window. Wake or unlock the Mac and press **Record** again.
75	
76	## Resume doesn't work
77	
78	If **Resume Recording** fails, the recording stays paused and nothing already recorded is lost. Nothing new is recorded until a resume works, so you can try again, or stop and land what you have.
79	
80	The reason goes in the panel's note, for example "The recording could not be resumed: …". During a voice-over or a camera recording it appears there at once. During a screen recording it appears when the recording lands, and the panel comes back to show it.
81	
82	A **Pause Recording** that fails only beeps, because the recording is still running.
83	
84	## A stretch won't read
85	
86	Each stretch between pauses has its own movie. If one won't read, for example an empty file from a pause right after a resume, it's left out, and the stretches that do read land. The note gives the reason and names everything it left on disk:
87	
88	> A segment was left out. … Its files are kept at …
89	
90	Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and its note names every file.
91	
92	### Its voice still lands
93	
94	If a left-out stretch's microphone file reads, it lands without its picture, on the Microphone track in the slot the picture would have had. The picture track keeps a gap there, and the next picture starts after it. The note reads "The left-out segment's microphone, …, was added to the project without its picture."
95	
96	That stretch's camera file stays on disk and the note names it, but it isn't added.
97	
98	In a new project, a left-out voice from before the first picture has no timeline to sit on, so it lands in the media list without a clip, and the note says so.
99	
100	## A file is too short for one frame
101	
102	A file too short for one frame can't become a clip. It lands in the media list, the rest of the recording lands as usual, and the note says so:
103	
104	> … is too short for a frame (12 ms) and was added to the media list without a clip.
105	
106	## The recording can't be added
107	
108	If a recording can't be added, nothing goes on the timeline, but the files are safe. The note names every one, so you can [import them](/projects/import-media/):
109	
110	> The recording was saved at … but could not be added: …
111	
112	These are the usual reasons:
113	
114	| What happened | What to do |
115	| --- | --- |
116	| The project is at its limit of 64 tracks, counting the tracks inside nests, and the recording needs a new one. If the picture would fit but the microphone wouldn't, none of it is added. | [Remove a track](/timeline/manage-tracks/) you don't need, then import the files. |
117	| You were still dragging on the timeline. Frame Job waits for a drag to end, for up to 20 s, then reads "A drag was still in progress after 20 s." | Import the files. |
118	
119	If a file still hasn't finished writing 10 s after Stop, Frame Job tries to read it anyway. If it won't read, the note reads "The recording did not finish writing within 10 s." and names the files kept on disk.
120	
121	## Very long recordings
122	
123	A recording longer than 9:59:59 carries on as usual, but the menu-bar item's label gets wider than the item was sized for.
124	
125	## With an agent
126	
127	`record_screen` reports all of this when it finishes, so an agent can tell what stopped and what landed: `camera.problem` and `mic_problem` say why a device stopped, `stopped_by` says what ended the recording, and `unreadable` lists any stretch left out, with the files kept and the reason. With the screen locked, it stops before recording and says that no display is shareable. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

142	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
143	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
144	
145	The boxes on the recorder panel run the clean-up you'd otherwise do by hand. The recording [lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) exactly as it would without them, and then each ticked box runs its command on what landed, each as its own undo step.
146	
147	<AtAGlance
148	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
149	  keys="⌥⌘N"
150	  where="New Recording panel ▸ When it lands:"
151	  tools={['record_screen', 'enhance_voice', 'auto_zoom', 'add_shortcut_overlays', 'speed_up_typing']}
152	  needs="Show shortcuts and Speed up typing need Record shortcuts, which needs macOS's Input Monitoring permission."
153	/>
154	
155	<Shot
156	  name="16-recorder-panel.panel"
157	  alt="The New Recording panel. Under the Layout row, Remove the camera's background when it lands is greyed out. Under Microphone, Enhance the microphone when it lands is greyed out. Under When it lands, Zoom in on clicks is ticked, Show shortcuts is ticked and greyed out, and Speed up typing is unticked and greyed out."
158	/>
159	
160	## Choose what runs
161	
162	Tick the boxes on the panel before you press Record.
163	
164	| Box | Runs | On | Default | Available when |
165	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
166	| **Remove the camera's background when it lands** | **Clip ▸ Remove Background** | The camera's clips | Off | **Record the camera too** is ticked beside a display or a window |
167	| **Enhance the microphone when it lands** | **Clip ▸ Enhance Voice** | The microphone's clips | Off | A microphone is chosen, on any source |
168	| **Zoom in on clicks** | **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…** | The screen clips | On | The source is a display or a window |
169	| **Show shortcuts** | **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays** | The screen clips | On | The source is a display or a window, with **Record shortcuts** ticked |
170	| **Speed up typing** | **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** | The screen clips | Off | The source is a display or a window, with **Record shortcuts** ticked |
171	
172	A greyed box keeps its value for next time, and every box is greyed while a recording is under way. The panel remembers all five between uses.
173	
174	The screen clips are the clips of each stretch's movie that has a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). No other clip is touched, and a voice-over or a camera on its own has none.
175	
176	:::note
177	**Zoom in on clicks** is on from the start, so a display or window recording lands with zooms unless you untick it. **Show shortcuts** is on too, but it does nothing until you tick [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/), which is off.
178	:::
179	
180	## The order they run in
181	
182	The steps always run in this order, whichever you tick:
183	
184	1. **Remove Background**, straight after the landing.
185	2. **Enhance Voice**, once the sound has been analysed.
186	3. **Auto Zoom**.
187	4. **Add Shortcut Overlays**.
188	5. **Speed Up Typing**, once the speech has been detected.
189	
190	Each is its own undo step, named as in this list, and they all come after the landing's. **Edit ▸ Undo** takes them off one at a time, last first, and keeps the recording.
191	
192	The order matters. Zooms are planned on whole clips before the speed-up splits them, and the speed-up leaves each overlay at its pace.
193	
194	Each command uses the settings its own menu command would, and only Enhance Voice shows a sheet. Nothing asks you a question.
195	
196	## Remove the camera's background
197	
198	**Remove the camera's background when it lands** runs [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) on the camera's clips straight after the landing, with nothing to wait for. If no camera clip landed, it does nothing and says nothing. [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/#remove-the-cameras-background) has the rest.
199	
200	## Enhance the microphone
201	
202	**Enhance the microphone when it lands** runs [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) on each stretch's microphone file, or on a voice-over's files. It never touches the picture, a camera or the system audio.
203	
204	Enhance Voice needs the sound's loudness and speech analysed first, so it waits for that after the files land. It then runs under the **Measuring Sound** sheet, at the target loudness of the [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) row, and its settings appear in the clip's [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
205	
206	Choosing **Cancel** on the sheet leaves the clips as they landed.
207	
208	**Edit ▸ Undo Enhance Voice** takes the processing off and keeps the recording. The next undo is **Remove Background** if that ran, then the landing's own step: **Add Recording** in an open project, and in a new project a step such as **Add Microphone**, or nothing when the recording is a single file.
209	
210	If a second recording lands in the same project while the first is still waiting, its clips join the wait and the wait starts again.
211	
212	## Zoom in on clicks
213	
214	**Zoom in on clicks** runs [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/) with the values the Auto Zoom sheet last used. **Zoom on typing** is turned on when the recording has typing, and off when it hasn't.
215	
216	## Show shortcuts
217	
218	**Show shortcuts** runs [Add Shortcut Overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) with its usual settings: at the bottom of the picture, in the dark theme.
219	
220	## Speed up typing
221	
222	**Speed up typing** runs [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) with the values its sheet last used. It waits until the speech has been detected, so typing you talk over keeps its pace.
223	
224	A speed-up that would leave a clip silent above ×12 is never applied here, because the panel can't ask you first. The foot of the inspector says so instead. Choose **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…** yourself to be asked. See [Sound at high speed](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
225	
226	## What the steps wait for
227	
228	Enhance Voice, Auto Zoom, Add Shortcut Overlays and Speed Up Typing each hold off while:
229	
230	- you're dragging in the project
231	- a sheet is up on its window
232	- you're inside a different nest from the one the recording landed in
233	
234	They carry on by themselves once that's over. Each waits for up to 5 minutes. The clock starts at the landing or when the step before it ran. For the first step after Enhance Voice, it starts when Enhance Voice stops waiting.
235	
236	## When a step can't run
237	
238	A problem shows at the foot of the [inspector](/getting-started/inspector/), with no beep and no sheet. A step with nothing to do says nothing at all: a recording with no cursor file, a recording with no microphone clip, or no click, shortcut or typing stretch long enough changes nothing and shows no message.
239	
240	| The inspector says | What happened | What runs next |
241	| --- | --- | --- |
242	| "Enhance Voice did not run on the recording: its microphone was not ready to measure within 5 minutes. Select its clip and choose Clip ▸ Enhance Voice." | The sound wasn't analysed in time, or the project stayed busy. | The other steps |
243	| "Nothing could be enhanced. …" | There was nothing to measure, for example a silent microphone. The sentence gives the reason. | The other steps |
244	| "… did not run on the recording: the project was busy for 5 minutes. Select its clips and choose Clip ▸ …" | You were dragging, a sheet was up, or you were in another nest for the whole wait. | Nothing. Run the rest yourself. |
245	| "Speed Up Typing did not run on the recording: its speech was not detected within 5 minutes. Select its clips and choose Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…." | Speech detection didn't finish in time, or the project stayed busy. | It's the last step. |
246	| "Clip … now plays above ×12, so its audio is left out: it is silent in the preview and the export." | The speed-up would do this, so it was left off. Despite the wording, nothing changed. | It's the last step. |
247	| Any other sentence | The command wouldn't run. This is the sentence it would show from its own menu item. | The next step |
248	
249	A cursor file that can't be read is reported the same way, and none of the steps that use it runs after that.
250	
251	## With an agent
252	
253	`record_screen` can run the same steps, through its `camera_cutout`, `enhance`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` arguments, with some differences:
254	
255	- Every step is off unless the agent asks for it, **Zoom in on clicks** included.
256	- Every step needs the recording placed on the timeline, so none works with `place: false`.
257	- `enhance` needs `microphone: true` or a voice-over.
258	- `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` need `keys: "shortcuts"`.
259	- `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` can't be used with a voice-over or a camera on its own.
260	- Enhance Voice runs at −16 LUFS, not at the Normalize row's target. The agent can call `enhance_voice` afterwards for another target.
261	- The other steps use the tools' own defaults, never the values a sheet remembers.
262	- A speed-up that leaves a clip silent above ×12 is applied, and the agent is told.
263	
264	The call's answer holds each step's own answer, or a sentence under `enhance_error`, `auto_zoom_error` and so on when the step couldn't run. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#run-steps-after-it-lands).
265

277	title: "Where a recording lands"
278	description: "Where a finished recording goes, into an open project at the playhead or as a new project of its own, what undo takes back, and when the panel comes back."
279	---
280	
281	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
282	
283	When you stop, Frame Job adds the recording to your work without asking anything: into the project you chose, at its playhead, or as a new project. A recording is ordinary media from then on, so you can cut, move and delete its clips like any others.
284	
285	<AtAGlance
286	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
287	  keys="⌥⌘N"
288	  where="New Recording panel ▸ Record Into"
289	  tools={['record_screen', 'undo']}
290	/>
291	
292	## Choose where it goes
293	
294	Before you press Record, set **Record Into** on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/). It lists **New Project** and every open project. It follows whichever project is in front until you pick a row yourself, and it's fixed once you press Record, so switching windows during a recording doesn't change where it goes.
295	
296	While the files are written and imported, the panel's button reads **Stopping…** and then **Adding…**.
297	
298	## Into an open project
299	
300	The recording goes in at the chosen project's playhead, in whatever is open there. If you're working inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), it lands inside the nest.
301	
302	| What was recorded | Where it lands |
303	| --- | --- |
304	| The picture, from a screen or a camera on its own | On the front track, when all of it fits there. Otherwise all of it goes on a new track in front of everything. |
305	| The microphone | On a new back track named **Microphone**. |
306	| A [camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) | On a new track named **Camera**, in front of everything, in the panel's **Layout**. |
307	| A [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/) | On a new back track named **Microphone**, from the playhead. |
308	
309	A recording's picture is never split across two tracks. An existing Microphone track is never reused: each recording makes its own.
310	
311	The microphone file and the movie don't start at quite the same moment, so Frame Job measures how far apart they began and places the microphone clip to match. When that would start it before the beginning of the timeline, or on top of the stretch before it, its head is trimmed instead.
312	
313	Every clip that landed is selected afterwards, microphone and camera clips included.
314	
315	## Land a paused recording
316	
317	Each [pause](/recording/pause-and-stop/) ends a file, so a paused recording is several files, one for each stretch. They land as one clip per stretch, back to back on one track. They touch, they never overlap, and no transition joins them. Each stretch's microphone file goes on the Microphone track, lined up with its own picture.
318	
319	At an uneven project frame rate, such as 24.981 fps, a gap of less than a frame can remain between two stretches.
320	
321	## Undo a landing
322	
323	Everything that lands in an open project is one undo step, **Add Recording**. **Edit ▸ Undo Add Recording** removes the clips and their media entries and leaves the files on disk, as undoing **Add Media…** does.
324	
325	Anything set up in [When it lands](/recording/when-it-lands/) runs after the landing as its own undo steps, so those come off first.
326	
327	## As a new project
328	
329	With **Record Into** set to **New Project**, the recording opens in a new, untitled project named after its file, such as `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22`. That's the name Save offers.
330	
331	The canvas takes the movie's size and the frame rate you chose in **Rate**, while the media keeps the file's own frame rate. Two sources differ:
332	
333	- A [camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/) sets the canvas to the file's size at the camera format's frame rate.
334	- A voice-over has no picture, so the canvas is 1920×1080 at **Rate**, and later stretches follow the first on its one track.
335	
336	The project is unsaved, and it asks before it closes.
337	
338	The first stretch's picture is the project itself, so it has no undo step. Everything else that landed with it is one step, named for what it holds:
339	
340	| What landed beside the first picture | Undo step |
341	| --- | --- |
342	| A microphone | **Add Microphone** |
343	| A camera | **Add Camera** |
344	| A camera and a microphone | **Add Camera and Microphone** |
345	| Later stretches, with or without a microphone or camera | **Add Recording Segments** |
346	| Only [click ripples](/recording/cursor/#show-clicks) | **Cursor Clicks** |
347	| Nothing | No step |
348	
349	Undoing that step keeps the first picture, leaves the files on disk, and leaves the project unsaved.
350	
351	## If you're dragging when it ends
352	
353	If you're in the middle of a drag in the chosen project when the recording ends, the landing waits for the drag to finish, for up to 20 seconds. After that it gives up, and the panel's note reads "The recording was saved at … but could not be added: A drag was still in progress after 20 s." The files are on disk either way, and you can bring them in with [**Add Media…**](/projects/import-media/).
354	
355	## If the chosen project closed
356	
357	If the project you chose closes while you're recording, the recording opens as a new project instead, and the panel's note says "The document you chose was closed, so the recording opened as a new project."
358	
359	## When the panel comes back
360	
361	A recording that lands cleanly doesn't bring the panel back. Once it has landed, press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> to open it. While a recording runs, the same keys stop it.
362	
363	The panel returns on its own, with a note, only if it was on screen when the recording began and there's something to report. The note can hold several of these at once.
364	
365	| The note says | What happened |
366	| --- | --- |
367	| "Stopped from the system's screen-recording indicator; the recording was added." | You stopped it from macOS's own indicator, not from Frame Job. |
368	| "The system stopped the recording (the display slept or went away); what was captured was added." | The display slept or went away. See [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/). |
369	| "The camera stopped on its own. What was captured was added." | A camera recording ended because the camera stopped. The first sentence can give the camera's own reason instead. |
370	| "A segment was left out. … Its files are kept at …" | One stretch's movie couldn't be read, for example an empty file from a pause right after a resume. The other stretches landed. |
371	| "The left-out segment's microphone, …, was added to the project without its picture." | That stretch's microphone file was readable, so it's on the Microphone track where the picture would have been. The next picture starts after that gap. |
372	| A sentence about the microphone | It stopped or failed. The picture still landed. |
373	| A sentence about a [camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) | It stopped or failed. The screen recording still landed. |
374	| "The camera ran at … fps, not its …, in the … s it was given to settle; the recording began anyway." | The camera didn't reach its format's frame rate before the recording began. "The camera delivered no steady frames…" is the same note when it sent none. |
375	| A sentence about resuming | Resuming after a [pause](/recording/pause-and-stop/) failed, and the sentence says why. |
376	| "… is too short for a frame (… ms) and was added to the media list without a clip." | The file is in the Media tab, with nothing on the timeline. |
377	| "… was added to the media list without a clip: …" | The file couldn't be placed, and the sentence says why. |
378	| "The cursor file for … was not written: …" | That stretch has no [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/). |
379	| "The recording did not finish writing within 10 s." | The files didn't close within 10 seconds of the stop. The note names the files kept on disk. |
380	| "The recording was saved at … but could not be added: …" | Nothing landed. The note names every file, which are all on disk. |
381	
382	## Good to know
383	
384	- A project already at its limit of 64 tracks can't take a recording that needs a new track. The picture and the microphone land together or not at all, so if the picture would fit and the microphone wouldn't, nothing lands. The files stay on disk and the note names them.
385	- A recording fails outright only when no movie could be read at all, or when the capture failed while the movie was being written. Its note names every file on disk.
386	- When a stretch is left out, its camera file stays on disk and is named with its kept files, but it isn't added to the project.
387	- In a new project, a left-out first stretch's microphone goes to the media list with no clip, because the first readable picture starts the project at 0.
388	
389	## With an agent
390	
391	`record_screen` lands a recording the same way, with two differences:
392	
393	- With no project open, it always opens a new project. Whenever a recording opens as a new project, including when the chosen project closed, the answer says `landed: new_project`, and later calls reach that project with `project` set to the recording's path.
394	- With `place: false` it adds the recording to the media list with no clip, which the panel can't, and the note says to place it with `add_clip`. A new project's picture is on the timeline whatever `place` says. `camera_layout` and the [steps after landing](/recording/when-it-lands/#with-an-agent) can't be used with it.
395	
396	See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).

406	title: "Recording files and formats"
407	description: "Where recordings are saved, how their files are named, what format each one is, and why a still screen gives a low frame rate."
408	---
409	
410	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
411	
412	Every recording is a set of ordinary files in one folder, so they outlast any project they land in. This page lists what each recording writes and in what format.
413	
414	<AtAGlance
415	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
416	  keys="⌥⌘N"
417	  tools="record_screen"
418	/>
419	
420	## Where recordings are saved
421	
422	Recordings go in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, which Frame Job creates the first time it needs it. The panel's footnote shows the folder before you start.
423	
424	They're never stored inside the project package. A recording is original footage, so it survives even if you never save the project it opened in, and undoing a landing leaves its files on disk. To carry recordings into the package, use [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).
425	
426	## What each recording writes
427	
428	| File | Example name | Format |
429	| --- | --- | --- |
430	| [Screen movie](#the-screen-movie) | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC or H.264 |
431	| [Its microphone](#the-microphone-file) | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22 (Microphone).m4a` | AAC audio |
432	| [Its cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) | `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.fjcursor` | Frame Job's own |
433	| [Voice-over](#voice-over-files) | `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a` | AAC audio |
434	| [Camera on its own](#camera-files) | `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33.mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC or H.264 |
435	| [Camera beside the screen](#camera-files) | `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov` | QuickTime movie, HEVC or H.264 |
436	
437	## How files are named
438	
439	A file is named by the date and time it began, on a 24-hour clock in your Mac's time zone.
440	
441	A [pause](/recording/pause-and-stop/) ends a file and a resume starts a new one, so each stretch of a paused recording is its own set of files, named by the time that stretch began.
442	
443	When a name is already taken, Frame Job adds ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.
444	
445	## The screen movie
446	
447	A screen recording is a QuickTime `.mov` in HEVC where your Mac offers it, otherwise H.264. Its size comes from the panel's **Size** row, **Nominal (points)** or **Best (pixels)**, measured on the display or on a picked window's own size.
448	
449	With **System Audio** on, the movie has one stereo 48 kHz sound track of what your Mac plays. Frame Job's own sound is left out, so playing your timeline during a recording doesn't get into it.
450	
451	The microphone is never a track of the movie.
452	
453	## The microphone file
454	
455	The microphone is written beside the movie, named after it with ` (Microphone)` added, as an AAC `.m4a` file.
456	
457	Keeping it apart from the system sound means you can set the level of your voice and your computer's sound separately. See [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/).
458	
459	## Voice-over files
460	
461	A [voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/) is an AAC `.m4a` named `Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a`, one file for each stretch between pauses.
462	
463	## Camera files
464	
465	A camera recording is a QuickTime `.mov` at the camera's format, in HEVC where that can be used at the format's size, otherwise H.264. It has no sound of its own.
466	
467	- A [camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/) is named `Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov`.
468	- A [camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) is named after the screen movie with ` (Camera)` added, one for each stretch.
469	
470	Any microphone file sits beside the movie, named as for a screen recording.
471	
472	## Why a still screen gives a low frame rate
473	
474	macOS delivers a new frame only when something on screen changes, so a mostly still screen gives a file with a low, uneven frame rate. That rate comes from the file itself and isn't a fault. The picture holds until the next change.
475	
476	**Rate**, 30 or 60 fps, is the most frames per second the file can hold. A new project uses it as its frame rate, while the media in the project keeps the file's real rate.
477	
478	Where the picture stops changing before the sound ends, the last frame is held to the end of the clip.
479	
480	## With an agent
481	
482	An agent can record into another folder, created if it's missing, which the panel can't. It names the folder only: the file always takes its dated name.
483	
484	The call's answer gives the files it wrote, as `path`, `mic_path` and `camera_path`. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#what-it-answers).
485

499	
500	While a recording runs, Frame Job puts an item in the menu bar. For a display or a window the panel is off screen, so this item is the recording's control, wherever you're working.
501	
502	<AtAGlance
503	  where="The menu bar, while a recording runs"
504	  tools="record_screen"
505	/>
506	
507	## What it shows
508	
509	The item appears when the recording starts, and shows the elapsed time as `m:ss`, then `h:mm:ss` past an hour. Hover over it and its tooltip says which state it's in.
510	
511	| State | The menu bar shows | Tooltip | Its menu |
512	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
513	| Recording | A coral ● and the running time | "Frame Job is recording" | **Pause Recording**, **Stop Recording** |
514	| Paused | ❚❚ and the time, held still | "Frame Job's recording is paused" | **Resume Recording**, **Stop Recording** |
515	
516	It needs no permission. It appears for an agent's recording too, so you can [pause or stop one](/recording/pause-and-stop/#stop-an-agents-recording). It comes down the moment the recording ends, before the recording has landed.
517	
518	## Pause, resume and stop
519	
520	Click the item for its menu.
521	
522	- **Pause Recording** pauses. The row then reads **Resume Recording**.
523	- **Stop Recording** stops the recording, running or paused, and adds it to your project.
524	
525	The time keeps ticking while the menu is open, so you can read it before you decide. [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/) has the other places to do this. If you choose **Quit Frame Job** while the panel is hidden for a screen recording, Frame Job opens this menu instead of quitting.
526	
527	## The keyboard mark
528	
529	While a recording [records shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/), a ⌨︎ mark follows the ● or ❚❚, and the menu starts with a greyed-out **Recording keyboard shortcuts** row. Both show whether the recording is running or paused, and they hold for a recording an agent started with shortcuts on.
530	
531	## A fixed width
532	
533	The item is sized once, so the other items in your menu bar don't shift as the seconds tick, when the hours appear, or at a pause. It's sized for times up to 9:59:59, and a little wider when it shows the keyboard mark. Past 9:59:59 the label is wider than that.
534	
535	## If macOS hides the item
536	
537	macOS can drop the item from a crowded menu bar or behind the notch. **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **File ▸ Pause Recording** still work once you switch to Frame Job.
538

546	title: "Recording permissions"
547	description: "Which macOS permissions a recording needs, when Frame Job asks for each one, and what to do when one is missing."
548	---
549	
550	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
551	
552	A recording can need up to four macOS permissions, depending on what you record. Frame Job asks for them only when you press **Record** in the recorder panel, and never during a countdown.
553	
554	<AtAGlance
555	  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Record', 'System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security']}
556	  tools="record_screen"
557	  needs="macOS's Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Camera and Microphone permissions, as the table below says."
558	/>
559	
560	## Which permissions you need
561	
562	| Permission | Needed when | Where it lives in **System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security** | Relaunch afterwards? |
563	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
564	| **Screen Recording** | You record a display or a window. | **Screen & System Audio Recording** | Yes |
565	| **Input Monitoring** | **Record shortcuts** is ticked and you record a display or a window. | **Input Monitoring** | No |
566	| **Camera** | **Source** is **Camera**, or **Record the camera too** is ticked. | **Camera** | Yes, after a denial |
567	| **Microphone** | A microphone is chosen, which every voice-over needs. | **Microphone** | Yes, after a denial |
568	
569	A camera on its own or a voice-over doesn't need Screen Recording.
570	
571	## When Frame Job asks
572	
573	A press of **Record** checks every permission it needs before the countdown begins, so a countdown never ends in a prompt. If one is missing, that press stops there, and the panel's note says what to do. The recorder panel is the only place Frame Job asks for these or opens System Settings for them.
574	
575	The checks run in a fixed order, and stop at the first one missing:
576	
577	| You're recording | The order |
578	| --- | --- |
579	| A display or a window | Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Camera, Microphone |
580	| A camera on its own | Camera, Microphone |
581	| A voice-over (**Source** is **Microphone Only**) | Microphone |
582	
583	Frame Job skips any that the recording doesn't need. Before any of them, it checks that you've picked what to record: a window, a camera, or a microphone for a voice-over.
584	
585	## Screen Recording
586	
587	The first press of **Record** without the permission shows macOS's prompt. The panel's note reads:
588	
589	> Screen Recording is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then relaunch.
590	
591	Turn it on, relaunch Frame Job, and press **Record** again.
592	
593	macOS shows that prompt only once, and Frame Job remembers it has asked. Every later press without the permission opens System Settings at the right pane instead, and the note adds "System Settings is open at that pane."
594	
595	## Input Monitoring
596	
597	**Record shortcuts** needs Input Monitoring to see key presses. macOS shows no prompt for it, and Frame Job isn't in that pane's list until you add it. So a press of **Record** without it opens System Settings at the pane, and the note reads:
598	
599	> Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring. If Frame Job is not in its list, add it with +. System Settings is open at that pane.
600	
601	Turn Frame Job on there, adding it with **+** if it isn't listed, and press **Record** again. No relaunch is needed, and **Record shortcuts** doesn't need Accessibility.
602	
603	## Camera
604	
605	If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears. It reads "Frame Job records the camera you choose, into a file of its own. Nothing is sent anywhere."
606	
607	- Allowing it carries on to the microphone check and the countdown.
608	- Denying it leaves the panel idle, with a note saying the camera isn't granted.
609	
610	If you've denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Camera pane instead, and the note says so. Turn it on there and relaunch Frame Job.
611	
612	## Microphone
613	
614	If you've never answered, macOS's prompt appears. It reads "Frame Job records the microphone you choose alongside a screen recording, into a file of its own beside the movie. Nothing is sent anywhere."
615	
616	- Allowing it starts the countdown straight away, as long as the panel is still open.
617	- Denying it leaves the panel idle, with a note saying the microphone isn't granted.
618	
619	If you've denied it before, the press opens System Settings at the Microphone pane instead, and the note says so. Turn it on there and relaunch Frame Job.
620	
621	## If you started Frame Job from a terminal
622	
623	A Frame Job started from a terminal or another app runs under that app's permissions, not its own. Turning on Frame Job in System Settings then makes no difference.
624	
625	The panel's note says so, and names the process that launched it by its process number (pid):
626	
627	> This Frame Job was launched by another process (pid 4182), so the grant that counts is that application's — the terminal's, for a shell launch; or relaunch with open -a "Frame Job".
628	
629	Either give the permission to that app, or quit Frame Job and start it from the Finder, the Dock or `open -a "Frame Job"`.
630	
631	In a launch like this, Frame Job doesn't remember having asked. Each press without Screen Recording asks macOS again rather than opening System Settings.
632	
633	## The panel steps aside
634	
635	The recorder panel usually floats above other windows. While a macOS prompt or System Settings is up, it stops floating so that it doesn't cover them. It floats again when you allow a camera or microphone prompt, on your next press of **Record**, or when you open the panel again.
636	
637	## macOS's recurring alert
638	
639	macOS periodically asks whether to keep letting Frame Job record the screen. Frame Job can't see this alert, and the permission still reads as granted, so a capture waiting behind it looks like a recording that won't start.
640	
641	If the panel stays on **Starting…** and then says "The recording did not start within 20 s.", look for the alert on the screen. Answer it and press **Record** again.
642	
643	## With an agent
644	
645	`record_screen` never asks for a permission and never opens System Settings, because a prompt needs a person in front of it. It checks each permission it needs and, if one is missing, stops with a sentence that names it and says where to turn it on. Grant it once from the panel.
646	
647	If the recording doesn't start or finish in time, it reports that a macOS alert may be waiting. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).
648

658	title: "Record a voice-over"
659	description: "Record narration from your microphone with no picture, at the playhead of the project you're editing or as a new project."
660	---
661	
662	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
663	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
664	
665	A voice-over is the microphone alone, with no picture. Use it to record narration over your edit: it lands at the playhead, on a new track of its own.
666	
667	<AtAGlance
668	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
669	  keys="⌥⌘N"
670	  where="New Recording panel ▸ Source ▸ Microphone Only"
671	  tools="record_screen"
672	  needs="The Microphone permission. Screen Recording isn't needed."
673	/>
674	
675	## Record a voice-over
676	
677	<Steps>
678	
679	1. Move the playhead to where the narration should start.
680	
681	2. Choose **File ▸ New Recording…**, and set **Source** to **Microphone Only**.
682	
683	3. Choose your microphone in **Microphone**.
684	
685	4. Check **Record Into**: the project to land in, or **New Project**.
686	
687	5. Press **Record**. Frame Job checks the Microphone permission, then counts down from 3.
688	
689	6. Speak. The panel stays up while you do.
690	
691	7. Press **Stop**. The button reads **Stopping…** and then **Adding…**, and the voice-over lands. The panel stays up, back on **Record**, ready for another take.
692	
693	</Steps>
694	
695	With **Microphone** set to **Off**, **Record** starts nothing and the panel says "Microphone Only records the microphone alone — choose a microphone first."
696	
697	The controls that only make sense for a picture grey out, keeping their values for next time: **System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows**, **Record the camera too**, **Cursor**, **Record shortcuts** and the **When it lands:** boxes. The note under **Size** reads "no picture — the microphone alone". **Rate** stays live, because it sets the frame rate of a new project.
698	
699	Frame Job keeps **Microphone Only** in **Source** until you quit, then goes back to your display.
700	
701	## While it records
702	
703	Nothing on screen is being filmed, so the panel stays up:
704	
705	- Its rows are locked.
706	- The [level meter](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/#check-your-level) stays live.
707	- The footnote at the bottom left shows ● and the elapsed time, or ❚❚ and the time held still while paused.
708	- **Record** reads **Stop**, and a **Pause** button stands beside it, reading **Resume** while paused.
709	
710	The countdown and the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) work as they do for a screen recording, so you can also pause and stop from the menu bar, or from **File ▸ Pause Recording** and **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>).
711	
712	**Close** takes the panel away and the voice-over carries on. To bring the panel back, click **New Recording…** on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/). <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> won't do it, because it stops the recording.
713	
714	## Where a voice-over lands
715	
716	**In an open project,** each [stretch](/recording/pause-and-stop/#paused-recordings-are-stretches) between pauses is its own file, and they land end to end from the playhead on one new track at the back, named **Microphone**. It's all one undo step, **Add Recording**. If a [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/) is open, they land inside it.
717	
718	A voice-over always gets a new track. It never goes on an existing one, even one already named **Microphone**.
719	
720	**As a new project,** the first file is the project itself, audio only at 1920×1080 and the frame rate in **Rate**. Later files follow it on its one track, as one undo step named **Add Recording Segments**.
721	
722	Either way they're ordinary audio clips, with everything in the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). To clean your voice up as it lands, tick [**Enhance the microphone when it lands**](/recording/when-it-lands/).
723	
724	## The files
725	
726	Each stretch is an `.m4a` file in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by the moment it began, for example `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04.m4a`. See [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/).
727	
728	## Good to know
729	
730	- If the microphone stops on its own, for example because it's unplugged, the voice-over ends there. What was recorded lands, and the note reads "The microphone stopped recording on its own: … The voice-over ends where it stopped."
731	- A file too short to fill one frame stays in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) without a clip, and a note says so. If that's every file, no **Microphone** track is added.
732	- A project already at its track limit can't take the new track. The files stay on disk and the note names them. See [Limits](/reference/limits/).
733	
734	## With an agent
735	
736	`record_screen` records a voice-over too. An agent gets your Mac's default microphone rather than a chosen one, and there's no countdown. It can't pass any of the screen settings with a voice-over. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/).
737

2	title: "The cursor in a recording"
3	description: "Choose whether the pointer is kept out of a screen recording for Frame Job to draw, or drawn into the movie by macOS, and how clicks are shown."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A screen recording can keep the pointer out of the movie, so Frame Job draws it on the clip and you can restyle it later, or have macOS draw it into the picture for good. You choose before you record, because the choice is part of the movie.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
12	  keys="⌥⌘N"
13	  where={['New Recording panel ▸ Cursor', 'New Recording panel ▸ Show Clicks']}
14	  tools="record_screen"
15	/>
16	
17	## Choose Separate or In the picture
18	
19	Set **Cursor** on the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).
20	
21	| | **Separate** | **In the picture** |
22	| --- | --- | --- |
23	| The pointer | Kept out of the movie. Frame Job draws it on the clip. | Drawn into the movie by macOS. |
24	| Restyle it later | Yes, in the clip's **Cursor** section. | No. It can't be changed or removed. |
25	| **Show Clicks** | Click ripples, drawn by Frame Job. | A ring drawn into the movie. |
26	| The **Cursor** section | Appears on the clip. | Doesn't appear. |
27	| Cursor file | Written | Written |
28	
29	**Separate** is the default for every screen source: displays, windows and picked windows. Your choice is remembered, and once you've made one it holds for every source.
30	
31	Both write a [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/) beside the movie, so [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), [shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/) and [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) work either way.
32	
33	With **Separate**, the pointer appears wherever Frame Job draws the clip, in the preview and in every export. The movie file on its own has no pointer, so opened in another app it shows none.
34	
35	**Cursor** is greyed out, keeping its value, with **Camera** or **Microphone Only** as the source, and while a recording is under way.
36	
37	## Show clicks
38	
39	**Show Clicks** marks each mouse click. It's off by default, and greyed out with **Camera** or **Microphone Only**.
40	
41	- **With In the picture**, macOS draws a ring around each click into the movie. It can't be removed afterwards.
42	- **With Separate**, nothing is drawn into the movie. Frame Job draws the ripples from the cursor file, and you can edit them afterwards.
43	
44	## What a Separate recording lands with
45	
46	The clip gets a **Cursor** section on the Clip tab's **Picture** sub-tab, with the pointer drawn as recorded. See [Style the recorded cursor](/recording/cursor-settings/) for what you can change there.
47	
48	With **Show Clicks** on as well, the clips land with **Clicks** set to **Ripple**, in the same undo step as the recording. In a new project where that's the only other change, the undo step is called **Cursor Clicks**. Undoing it takes the ripples off and keeps the pointer.
49	
50	Nothing else is set. To smooth the pointer's path and hide it when it's idle, choose **Polish** in the same section.
51	
52	## What an In the picture recording lands with
53	
54	The pointer is in the movie and the cursor file says so, so the clip shows no **Cursor** section and nothing is drawn twice.
55	
56	## Good to know
57	
58	If a **Separate** stretch's cursor file couldn't be written, that stretch has no pointer at all: it isn't in the movie and there's nothing to draw it from. It gets no ripples either. The panel's note says so, with "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."
59	
60	## With an agent
61	
62	`record_screen` takes `cursor`, either `separate` or `in_picture`, and leaving it out means `separate`. Its `show_clicks` is `false` unless the agent sets it. Neither can be used with a voice-over or a camera on its own. See [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/#pointer-and-keys).
63	
64	## Related
