7	
8	`record_screen` is **File ▸ New Recording…** without the panel. An agent says how many seconds to record, the call runs for that long, and the recording lands in the project the way one made with the panel does. There's no countdown, and the tool never asks for a permission.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
12	  tools="record_screen"
13	  needs={[
14	    'Screen Recording permission, for a screen recording',
15	    'Microphone, Camera or Input Monitoring, only when the call uses them',
16	    'A person has to give each permission first',
17	  ]}
18	/>
19	
20	## Record the screen
21	
22	The smallest call names only `seconds`:
23	
24	```json
25	{ "seconds": 30 }
26	```
27	
28	That records the main display for 30 seconds with its system sound, leaves Frame Job's own windows out of the picture, and lands the movie at the playhead of the front project. A recording then goes through these stages:
29	
30	- **It starts at once.** There's no countdown and no panel.
31	- **It writes to disk.** The file goes to `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, named for example `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov`, and it's never stored inside the project. A name that's already taken gets ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.
32	- **It lands.** The movie becomes ordinary media, and a clip goes at the playhead on the front track of whatever is open, a [nest](/mcp/nests/) included. When that track has no room there, Frame Job adds a new track in front of everything. This is one undo step, **Add Recording**.
33	- **It returns.** The call comes back once the recording is finished, imported and placed. See [What it answers](#what-it-answers).
34	
35	With no project open, the recording opens as a new untitled project instead, and `landed` reads `new_project`. Its canvas takes the movie's size and `rate`. Later calls address that project with `project` set to the recording's path, which is the path `get_project` reports for it. If the target project closes while the recording runs, the same thing happens and the answer's `note` says so.
36	
37	Only one recording runs at a time, whoever started it. A second call stops with "A recording is already in progress."
38	
39	A recording that a person pauses is written in stretches, one file for each run between pauses. This page uses that word throughout, and a recording never paused is a single stretch. See [A person can pause or stop it](#a-person-can-pause-or-stop-it).
40	
41	:::note
42	The built-in [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) can't call `record_screen`. Recording stays with a person at the Record button, or an agent connected from outside.
43	:::
44	
45	[Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) has the landing in full, and it's the same for both.
46	
47	## Choose a source
48	
49	`source` says what's recorded.
50	
51	| `source` | What it records | Files |
52	| --- | --- | --- |
53	| `screen` | A display or a window. The default. | `Screen Recording <date> at <time>.mov` |
54	| `voice_over` | The default microphone alone, with no picture. | `Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a` |
55	| `camera` | A camera alone, with no screen. | `Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov` |
56	
57	An argument the source can't use isn't ignored. The call stops with a message naming it, and nothing is recorded. A JSON null counts as not given. This is what each source takes:
58	
59	| Argument | `screen` | `voice_over` | `camera` |
60	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
61	| `seconds`, `project`, `path`, `place`, `enhance` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
62	| `microphone` | Yes | Implied, and `false` stops the call | Yes |
63	| `rate` | Yes | Yes, for a new project's canvas | No |
64	| `camera`, `camera_format` | Yes, [beside the screen](#record-a-camera-beside-the-screen) | No | Yes |
65	| `camera_layout`, `camera_cutout` | Yes, with `camera` | No | No |
66	| `display`, `window`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows` | Yes | No | No |
67	| `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `cursor`, `keys` | Yes | No | No |
68	| `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` | Yes | No | No |
69	
70	## The arguments
71	
72	Only `seconds` is required. The sections further down cover the arguments for [voice-overs](#record-a-voice-over), [cameras](#record-a-camera-alone) and the [steps after landing](#run-steps-after-it-lands).
73	
74	### Length and source
75	
76	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
77	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
78	| `seconds` | number | Required | How long to record, from 1 to 600 seconds. It's wall-clock time, so a [pause](#a-person-can-pause-or-stop-it) shortens what's recorded. |
79	| `source` | `screen`, `voice_over` or `camera` | `screen` | What's recorded. See [Choose a source](#choose-a-source). |
80	
81	### Display or window
82	
83	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
84	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
85	| `display` | whole number, 0 or more | `0` | Which display, as an index into the displays that can be shared, 0 being the main one. Can't be used with `window`. |
86	| `window` | whole number | None | The system window id (`CGWindowID`) of one window to record on its own, at that window's own size, instead of a display. Can't be used with `display`. |
87	| `include_framejob_windows` | boolean | `false` | Puts Frame Job's own windows, the editor and the preview, in a display recording. By default they're left out. With `window` it changes nothing. Frame Job's own sound stays out either way. |
88	| `size` | `nominal` or `best`, in any case | `nominal` | `nominal` records a display's point size, and `best` its pixel size, twice the points on a Retina display. An odd dimension is rounded up to even. |
89	| `rate` | `30` or `60` | `60` | The most frames a second the file may hold, and the canvas rate of a new project the recording opens as. A camera alone records at its format's rate instead. |
90	
91	A screen recording's frame rate is whatever the screen did, because a frame arrives only when something changes. A mostly still screen reports a low, fractional rate. That's the file and not a fault, and the picture holds its last frame to the end of the sound.
92	
93	### Sound
94	
95	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
96	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
97	| `system_audio` | boolean | `true` | Records what the Mac plays as the movie's one stereo 48 kHz track. It takes in every app but Frame Job, so the timeline can play meanwhile and stay out of it. `false` writes a movie with no audio track, and `has_audio` reads false. |
98	| `microphone` | boolean | `false` | Also records the default microphone, to a second file beside the movie named `<movie name> (Microphone).m4a`. |
99	
100	The microphone's file lands as its own clip on a new track at the back named **Microphone**, lined up with the picture by the measured `mic_offset`. When the microphone began first and there's no room for it there, the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip landing late.
101	
102	A microphone that fails doesn't fail the recording. The picture lands, the stretch it failed in has no `mic_path`, and `mic_problem` and the `note` say why. See [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/).
103	
104	### Pointer and keys
105	
106	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
107	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
108	| `cursor` | `separate` or `in_picture` | `separate` | `separate` keeps the pointer out of the movie, and Frame Job draws it on the clip from the cursor file, where you can restyle it. `in_picture` has macOS burn the pointer into the movie. |
109	| `show_clicks` | boolean | `false` | Shows each mouse click. With `in_picture`, a circle is drawn around each click into the movie. With `separate`, the clips land with click ripples on, drawn by Frame Job. |
110	| `keys` | `off` or `shortcuts` | `off` | `shortcuts` writes keyboard shortcuts into the cursor files, and needs the Input Monitoring permission. |
111	
112	Every display or window recording writes a cursor file beside each movie, named `<movie name>.fjcursor`, holding the pointer's path, its clicks and scrolls. A problem with it never fails the recording. `segments` reports it as `cursor_problem`, and the note repeats it. A `separate` stretch with no cursor file has no pointer at all, and the note ends "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."
113	
114	With `keys: "shortcuts"`, the file records each shortcut pressed with ⌘ or ⌃, or with ⌥ and an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc, spelled like `cmd+shift+4`. Every other key is a mark of the time alone, never which key was typed. Nothing is written while an app holds secure input. See [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) and [The cursor in a recording](/recording/cursor/).
115	
116	### Where it goes
117	
118	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
119	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
120	| `path` | string | `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings` | A folder to record into, created if it doesn't exist. It names the folder and never the file, and the answer's `path` is the file that was written. A leading `~` means your home folder, and a blank string means the default folder. |
121	| `project` | string | The front project | The open project to land in, as `get_project` reports its path. One that names nothing open stops the call. It never turns into a new project. |
122	| `place` | boolean | `true` | Puts clips on the timeline, in one undo step with the media. `false` adds the recording to the media list only, and the note says to place it with `add_clip`. |
123	
124	In a new project `place: false` has no effect, because the project is made from the recording's picture. Its clips are on the timeline, one for each stretch and the first at 0, and the `note` says so.
125	
126	## Record a voice-over
127	
128	`source: "voice_over"` records the default microphone alone, as the panel's **Microphone Only** does. `microphone: true` is implied. The only permission it reads is the Microphone one, and it looks nothing up.
129	
130	Each stretch between pauses is its own `.m4a` file. The files land touching, from the playhead, on one new track at the back named **Microphone**, in one undo step, **Add Recording**. In a new project the first file starts the project, on a 1920 × 1080 canvas at `rate`, and later files touch it on its one track.
131	
132	The answer's `path` is the first `.m4a`, its `width` and `height` are 0, and it has no `mic_path`. A microphone that stops on its own ends the voice-over, what it wrote lands, and `mic_problem` and the `note` say so.
133	
134	See [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/).
135	
136	## Record a camera alone
137	
138	`source: "camera"` records one camera, with no screen, and lands it as a screen recording's picture lands. It reads the Camera permission and never the Screen Recording one. `microphone: true` adds the default microphone as a second file, as for a screen.
139	
140	Recording starts once the camera has settled at its frame rate, which takes up to a second, and `seconds` counts from its first frame. While it runs, a recorder panel left open with a camera chosen reads "The camera is recording." in its preview. The movie holds no sound, so `has_audio` is false. In a new project the canvas is the file's size at the format's frame rate, rounded.
141	
142	### Choose the camera and its format
143	
144	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
145	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
146	| `camera` | string | The default camera with `source: "camera"`, none with `source: "screen"` | A camera's unique id, or its name in any case. Blank counts as not given. |
147	| `camera_format` | string | `best` | The format to record at, in any case: `1920x1080@30`, or `1920x1080` for that size's highest frame rate, or `best`. Blank or null means `best`. |
148	
149	The default camera is the Mac's preferred camera, then the first built-in one, then the first connected. `best` is the largest size wider than tall that runs at 30 fps or more, at its highest frame rate.
150	
151	An unknown camera stops the call with a list of every camera connected, by name and id. With none connected the message is "No camera is connected." A format the camera doesn't have stops the call with a list of its formats. With `source: "screen"`, `camera_format` needs `camera`: "With source screen, camera_format needs camera — name the camera to record beside the screen."
152	
153	The answer carries `camera`, with the camera's `name`, `id` and `format`, spelled like `1920x1080@30`. It adds `problem` when the camera stopped on its own, which ends the recording with `stopped_by: "system_stopped"` and lands what it wrote, and `note` when the camera hadn't settled by the time recording began. The top-level `note` repeats both.
154	
155	See [Record a camera](/recording/record-a-camera/).
156	
157	## Record a camera beside the screen
158	
159	`source: "screen"` with `camera` records that camera at the same time as the screen, for a talking head over a screencast. It's the panel's **Record the camera too** box, and `camera_format` works as it does for a camera alone.
160	
161	Each stretch gets a camera movie named after its screen movie, like `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov`. The camera files land in the same undo step as the screen, on one new track named **Camera** in front of the screen's. Each camera clip starts where its screen clip starts, moved by that stretch's measured `camera_offset`. A camera usually starts a little before the screen, and then the clip's first frames are trimmed rather than the clip starting early. A camera clip never starts before its screen clip, and never overlaps the camera clip before it.
162	
163	With `place: false` the camera files are added to the media list only, with no clip and no **Camera** track. In a new project the first movie starts the project, and its camera is one undo step: **Add Camera**, or **Add Camera and Microphone** with a microphone, for a recording that wasn't paused.
164	
165	The Camera permission is checked before the Screen Recording one. See [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/).
166	
167	### Lay the camera out
168	
169	| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
170	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
171	| `camera_layout` | see below | `corner_square` | How each camera clip lands, laid out from its first frame with its stretch's screen clip, as the panel's **Layout** does. |
172	| `camera_cutout` | boolean | `false` | Runs [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) on the camera clips right after the landing, as the panel's **Remove the camera's background when it lands** box does. |
173	
174	| `camera_layout` | Panel's name | What you get |
175	| --- | --- | --- |
176	| `corner_square` | Corner | The bottom-right corner, scaled to fit a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % safe area. |
177	| `corner_rounded` | Rounded Corner | The same corner with rounded edges. |
178	| `corner_circle` | Circle | The same corner as a circle. |
179	| `side_by_side` | Side by Side | The screen and the camera next to each other. |
180	| `camera_full` | Camera Full | The camera fills the canvas. |
181	
182	The layout reaches no further than the later end of the two clips. When a stretch's screen clip is missing, or isn't playing where its camera starts, that camera goes in the bottom-right corner instead. Either way it stays an ordinary clip you can move. [Camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) has the rest.
183	
184	Both arguments need `camera`, and neither works with `source: "voice_over"` or `"camera"`. `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout: true` also need `place: true`. Frame Job checks all of this before it reads any permission, and the message says what's missing. For example: "With source screen, camera_layout needs camera — name the camera to record beside the screen."
185	
186	## Run steps after it lands
187	
188	These arguments run a command over the recording once it has landed. Each is its own undo step, so undoing one keeps the recording, and they run in the order of this table. The landing itself is the same with or without them.
189	
190	| Argument | What it runs | On which clips | Undo step | Needs |
191	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
192	| `camera_cutout` | Remove Background | The camera clips | **Remove Background** | `camera`, `place: true` |
193	| `enhance` | `enhance_voice` at −16 LUFS | The microphone's clips, or a voice-over's | **Enhance Voice** | `microphone: true` or `source: "voice_over"`, `place: true` |
194	| `auto_zoom` | `auto_zoom` | The screen clips | **Auto Zoom** | `place: true` |
195	| `shortcut_overlays` | `add_shortcut_overlays` | The screen clips | **Add Shortcut Overlays** | `place: true`, `keys: "shortcuts"` |
196	| `speed_up_typing` | `speed_up_typing` | The screen clips | **Speed Up Typing** | `place: true`, `keys: "shortcuts"` |
197	
198	All default to `false`. The last three are the panel's **When it lands:** boxes, **Zoom in on clicks**, **Show shortcuts** and **Speed up typing**. `enhance` is its **Enhance the microphone when it lands** box. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).
199	
200	The screen clips are the clips of the recording's movies that have a cursor file. `enhance` never touches the picture, a camera or the system audio.
201	
202	### What they wait for
203	
204	The call stays open while these run, and `project` in the answer is read after them.
205	
206	- `enhance` waits for the microphone's loudness and speech to be analysed, up to 5 minutes.
207	- `speed_up_typing` waits for the clips' speech to be detected, up to 5 minutes.
208	- `enhance`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` also wait while the project is busy, up to 5 minutes: a drag is under way, or a different nest is open from the one the recording landed in.
209	- `camera_cutout` waits for nothing, and runs straight after the landing.
210	
211	### The values they use
212	
213	They run at the tools' own defaults, never at what the sheets last remembered.
214	
215	| Step | Values |
216	| --- | --- |
217	| `enhance` | −16 LUFS. Call [`enhance_voice`](/mcp/tools-audio/#enhance_voice) afterwards for another target. |
218	| `auto_zoom` | Zoom ×2, Arrive 0.6 s, Stay 2.5 s, Follow the cursor while zoomed on, Zoom on typing on, Replace existing zooms off, Motion blur 50 %. |
219	| `shortcut_overlays` | Bottom, dark, 1.5 s. |
220	| `speed_up_typing` | ×4 for stretches of 3 s or more, Keep pitch on. A speed-up that leaves a clip silent above ×12 is applied, and says so in `audio_note`. |
221	
222	### What each one answers
223	
224	Each step adds its own answer to the call's answer, under its name, or a sentence under `<name>_error` saying why it didn't run. The recording stays either way.
225	
226	| Key | Holds |
227	| --- | --- |
228	| `camera_cutout` | `clips`, the clips that were cut out. |
229	| `camera_cutout_error` | "No camera clip landed on the timeline, so Remove Background did not run." |
230	| `enhance` | What `enhance_voice` answers. |
231	| `enhance_error` | That no microphone clip landed, that it wasn't ready to measure within 5 minutes, that the call was stopped first, or `enhance_voice`'s own reason. |
232	| `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` | What each tool answers. |
233	| `auto_zoom_error`, `shortcut_overlays_error`, `speed_up_typing_error` | That no screen clip with a cursor file landed, that the project was busy or the speech wasn't detected within 5 minutes, that the call was stopped first, or the tool's own reason. |
234	
235	If `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` or `speed_up_typing` fails for a reason of its own, the next one still runs. When no screen clip landed, a wait runs out or the call is stopped, none of the remaining ones run, and each gets its own sentence.
236	
237	## It never asks for a permission
238	
239	`record_screen` reads each permission and never requests one. It never shows a system prompt, never opens the window picker and never opens System Settings. A person grants them in the panel, usually by pressing **Record** in **File ▸ New Recording…** once. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).
240	
241	| Permission | When it's read | What the call says when it's missing |
242	| --- | --- | --- |
243	| Screen Recording | Any `screen` recording | "Screen Recording is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then relaunch." |
244	| Microphone | `microphone: true` or `source: "voice_over"` | "The microphone is not granted to Frame Job (status: denied)." and the Microphone pane. With status `notDetermined`, it says to press Record in **File ▸ New Recording…** once. The status may also read `restricted`. |
245	| Camera | `source: "camera"` or `camera` | "The camera is not granted to Frame Job (status: denied)." and the Camera pane. With status `notDetermined`, it says to press Record with the Camera source once. |
246	| Input Monitoring | `keys: "shortcuts"` | "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring." |
247	
248	A Frame Job launched from a shell runs under the terminal's permissions, not its own. Each of these messages then also names the launching process by its pid, and says the permission that counts is that application's, or to relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"`.
249	
250	:::caution
251	macOS periodically asks whether to keep letting Frame Job record, and neither Frame Job nor the tool can see that alert. A capture waiting behind it looks like a hang. When a start or a finish times out, the answer says an alert may be waiting on the screen. Answer it and call again.
252	:::
253	
254	## What's checked first
255	
256	Frame Job checks a call in a fixed order and stops at the first problem. The caller's own mistakes come first, so an agent hears about a mistake even when no permission has been given.
257	
258	1. `seconds` missing or outside 1 to 600.
259	2. `source` unknown, then the arguments that source can't take, including `camera_format`, `camera_layout` or `camera_cutout` on a screen recording without `camera`, then `microphone: false` with a voice-over.
260	3. `display` with `window`, or a `display` or `window` that isn't a valid number.
261	4. `rate` or `size` outside its values.
262	5. `keys` or `cursor` outside its values.
263	6. `enhance` without a microphone, then with `place: false`.
264	7. `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing`, in that order, each with `place: false`, and the last two without `keys: "shortcuts"`.
265	8. `camera_layout` outside its values, then `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout: true` with `place: false`.
266	9. The Microphone permission.
267	10. The Input Monitoring permission.
268	11. A `project` that names nothing open.
269	12. For a camera, the camera lookup, then `camera_format`, then the Camera permission.
270	13. For a screen, the Screen Recording permission.
271	14. The display or window lookup. A window that can't be shared gets "No window with id 123 is shareable." An index past the last display gets "display must be 0…1 (got 3); 2 displays are shareable."
272	
273	When the console is locked or every display is asleep, step 14 says "No display is shareable right now — the console is locked or every display is asleep; nothing can be recorded until one is."
274	
275	After those, a call with a microphone needs a default microphone, or it stops with "No microphone is available." Then the recording starts.
276	
277	## How long the call takes
278	
279	| Stage | How long |
280	| --- | --- |
281	| Starting | Up to 20 seconds, then "The recording did not start within 20 s." |
282	| Recording | `seconds`, plus about a second to start and finish. |
283	| Finishing | Up to about 75 s more if the files are slow to close, and 60 s more for each further stretch of a paused recording. |
284	| Finishing, with a camera beside the screen | Up to about 105 s more, and 90 s more for each further stretch, because each camera file is read too. |
285	| Landing | Up to 20 seconds, while a drag in the target project ends. |
286	| [Steps after landing](#what-they-wait-for) | Up to 5 minutes for each wait. |
287	
288	A finish that times out lists every movie it still holds, then the camera files, because they may yet finish on their own. If a drag outlasts its wait, the message names the files too, which are on disk either way:
289	
290	"The recording was saved at `<path>` but could not be added: …"
291	
292	Calls run one at a time, so a recording holds up the next call until it returns. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).
293	
294	## A person can pause or stop it
295	
296	While an agent records, the same [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) appears as for the panel, so a person at the Mac can pause, resume or stop it. **File ▸ Pause Recording** and **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) work too. An agent has no tool to pause or resume.
297	
298	- **Stop** ends the call early and the recording still lands, with `stopped_by: "stopped"` and a `duration` shorter than `seconds`. That's the same value the tool's own stop gives, so the short `duration` is what tells the two apart.
299	- **Pause** shortens what the call records, because `seconds` keeps running. The paused time is in no file, and `pauses` counts the presses, including a pause with no resume before the stop.
300	
301	A paused recording is a sequence of files, one for each stretch between a start or a resume and a pause or the stop. Each is named by its own start time and, with a microphone, carries its own microphone file. Every stretch lands as its own clip on one track, touching the one before, and each microphone file as its own clip on the **Microphone** track at its own offset.
302	
303	## What it answers
304	
305	Times are ticks, 600,000 to the second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). Most top-level keys describe the first stretch, the recording's own file.
306	
307	| Key | What it holds |
308	| --- | --- |
309	| `path` | The first stretch's file, the one a new project is addressed by. |
310	| `duration` | The total recorded across every stretch. |
311	| `width`, `height`, `fps` | The first stretch's picture size and frame rate, with `fps` as `[num, den]`. |
312	| `has_audio`, `audio_tracks` | What that movie holds. `audio_tracks` is 1 with system audio, else 0. The microphone is never a track of the movie. |
313	| `mic_offset` | Always present, and 0 with no microphone. The measured lead in ticks, positive when the picture began after the microphone. |
314	| `mic_path`, `mic_duration` | The first stretch's microphone file, when it landed. |
315	| `mic_problem` | Every stretch's microphone sentence, joined. It can stand beside a `mic_path` when a later stretch failed. |
316	| `media`, `clip`, `mic_media`, `mic_clip` | The first stretch's ids. There's no `clip` or `mic_clip` with `place: false`. |
317	| `camera` | The camera used, as in [Choose the camera and its format](#choose-the-camera-and-its-format). |
318	| `pauses` | How many times Pause was pressed, 0 when never. |
319	| `segments` | Always present, one entry for each file, in order. Exactly one for a recording never paused. |
320	| `stopped_by` | `stopped` for the tool's own stop and a person's Stop from Frame Job. `user_stopped` for macOS's own screen-recording indicator. `system_stopped` for a display that slept or a camera that stopped on its own. |
321	| `landed` | `document` or `new_project`. |
322	| `unreadable` | Any stretches left out. See below. |
323	| `note` | Present when there's something to say. |
324	| `project` | The usual project summary. |
325	| `new_media`, `new_clips`, `new_tracks` | The ids made, as every edit reports them, when it landed in an open project. `new_tracks` appears when a track was added. `scope` and `document_ops` appear when it landed inside a nest. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/). |
326	
327	Each entry of `segments` carries these keys. A screen recording's frame rate differs between stretches, so each has its own.
328	
329	| Key | What it holds |
330	| --- | --- |
331	| `path`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps` | This stretch's file. |
332	| `started_at` | When this stretch began, in UTC to the millisecond, like `2026-09-12T13:04:22.417Z`. |
333	| `mic_offset`, `mic_path`, `mic_duration`, `mic_problem` | As at the top level, for this stretch. |
334	| `media`, `clip`, `mic_media`, `mic_clip` | This stretch's ids, when known. |
335	| `camera_path`, `camera_duration`, `camera_offset` | This stretch's camera file, when it landed. `camera_offset` is in ticks, positive when the camera began after the screen. |
336	| `camera_problem`, `camera_note` | What went wrong with this stretch's camera, when anything did. The note repeats them. |
337	| `camera_media`, `camera_clip` | The camera's ids, when known. |
338	| `cursor_path`, `cursor_image` | This stretch's cursor file, when one was written. `cursor_image` reads `none` because no cursor image is recorded. |
339	| `cursor_problem` | Why the file wasn't written, or holds only the geometry the screen had when the stretch began. |
340	
341	### When a stretch won't read
342	
343	A stretch whose movie won't read, such as an empty file from a pause straight after a resume, is left out rather than failing the recording. The readable stretches land, and `unreadable` lists each one left out, with its `path`, its `kept_files` still on disk and the `reason`. When its microphone file reads, the entry adds `mic_path` and `mic_duration`, and `mic_media` and `mic_clip` when known, and that microphone lands in the slot the picture would have had. A camera file from such a stretch stays on disk, named in `kept_files`, and doesn't land.
344	
345	Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and it names every file.
346	
347	## Undo a recording
348	
349	In an open project, one undo removes every stretch's media and clips and leaves the files on disk, as undoing Add Media… does.
350	
351	A recording that opened as a new project has no undo step for its first picture, because the project is made from it. Whatever came with it is one undo step, and undoing it leaves that first picture alone in the project:
352	
353	| What came with it | Undo step |
354	| --- | --- |
355	| A microphone, on a recording never paused | **Add Microphone** |
356	| A camera, on a recording never paused | **Add Camera** |
357	| A camera and a microphone, on a recording never paused | **Add Camera and Microphone** |
358	| Only click ripples, on a recording never paused | **Cursor Clicks** |
359	| Later stretches of a paused recording, with all their files | **Add Recording Segments** |
360	
361	[Steps after landing](#run-steps-after-it-lands) undo first, one at a time, last first.

386	/>
387	
388	Every tool here also takes `project`, the path of an open project. Without it the call goes to the frontmost project. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/). Times are in ticks, 600,000 a second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).
389	
390	## The tools that work from a cursor file
391	
392	`auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` share these rules:
393	
394	- Each takes exactly one of `clip` and `clips`.
395	- `from` and `to` are in the time of the timeline or nest that's open, and `to` must be after `from`. The menu commands can't limit themselves this way.
396	- None takes `scope`. Each acts in whatever `set_scope` has open. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/).
397	- None remembers the settings a person last used in a sheet. They start from the defaults below.
398	- With nothing to do, each returns `ok` with a `note` and makes no undo step.
399	
400	Each one won't run when a clip isn't a media clip, its media has no cursor file or the file is missing, or it plays reversed. If the project changes while the cursor files are read, the call changes nothing and says to call again.
401	
402	## `record_screen`
403	
404	Records for a set number of seconds and adds the result to the project as ordinary media, as **File ▸ New Recording…** does without the panel. It records a display or a window, the microphone alone, or a camera alone, and it can record a camera beside the screen. See also [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).
405	
406	This is a summary. [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/) has every argument, its default and what the agent gets back.
407	
408	Only `seconds` is required, 1 to 600. The rest are grouped like this:
409	
410	| To set | Use |
411	| --- | --- |
412	| [The length and the source](/mcp/record-screen/#length-and-source) | `seconds`, and `source`: `screen` (the default), `voice_over` or `camera`. |
413	| [The display or window](/mcp/record-screen/#display-or-window) | `display`, `window`, `size`, `rate` and `include_framejob_windows`. |
414	| [The sound](/mcp/record-screen/#sound) | `system_audio` and `microphone`. |
415	| [The pointer and keys](/mcp/record-screen/#pointer-and-keys) | `cursor`, `show_clicks` and `keys`. |
416	| [Where it goes](/mcp/record-screen/#where-it-goes) | `path`, a folder, and `place`. |
417	| [A camera](/mcp/record-screen/#choose-the-camera-and-its-format) | `camera` and `camera_format`, and beside the screen, [`camera_layout` and `camera_cutout`](/mcp/record-screen/#lay-the-camera-out). |
418	| [Steps after it lands](/mcp/record-screen/#run-steps-after-it-lands) | `enhance`, [`auto_zoom`](#auto_zoom), `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing`. Each runs as its own undo step. The last two need `keys: "shortcuts"`. |
419	
420	Not every argument goes with every source. [Choose a source](/mcp/record-screen/#choose-a-source) has the table, and an argument the source can't use gives an error by name rather than being ignored.
421	
422	The call doesn't return until the recording has finished and been added to the project. [What it returns](/mcp/record-screen/#what-it-answers) lists every key. A person at the Mac can [pause or stop](/mcp/record-screen/#a-person-can-pause-or-stop-it) an agent's recording.
423	
424	**It never asks for a permission.** A person has to give Screen Recording, Microphone, Camera and Input Monitoring first, in the recorder panel, and a missing one gives an error that names it. See [It never asks for a permission](/mcp/record-screen/#it-never-asks-for-a-permission) and [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/). The [Assistant tab](/assistant/what-it-can-do/) can't use this tool, so it's for a client connected over MCP.
425	
426	## `set_media_cursor`
427	
428	Attaches, moves or removes a screen recording's cursor file, the `.fjcursor` Frame Job writes beside each recorded movie. It's **Locate…** and **Remove** in the Media tab's **Cursor** section. See [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/).
429	
430	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
431	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
432	| `media` | integer | Yes | The video media's id. |
433	| `cursor` | object | Yes | `{path, bookmark?, in_picture}`, the media's `cursor` as `get_project` shows it, or null to forget the file. The file itself stays on disk. |
434	| `scope` | integer | No | A nest's id, to make the edit inside that nest. See [Editing inside a nest](/mcp/nests/). |
435	
436	Give `path` in full, because `~` isn't expanded here. `in_picture` says whether the movie's picture already shows the pointer, and it must match the file.
437	
438	It returns what [any edit returns](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/), with `media` added, and it's one undo step, **Locate Cursor File** or **Remove Cursor File**. **Consolidate Media** copies the file into the package beside its movie, and opening a moved package finds it there.
439	
440	It won't attach the file when:
441	
442	- `path` is empty.
443	- The file doesn't open as a cursor file.
444	- The file was made for a movie of a different size.
445	- `in_picture` isn't the file's own.
446	- The media isn't a video with a picture.
447	
448	## `get_cursor_events`
449	
450	Reads what a recording's cursor file holds: its clicks, scrolls, shortcuts, stretches of typing and, if asked, the pointer's path. It runs on your Mac, needs no key, edits nothing and makes no undo step. There's no menu for it. See [What a cursor file holds](/recording/cursor-files/#what-a-cursor-file-holds).
451	
452	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
453	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
454	| `media` | integer | One of these | The recording, read in the file's own source ticks. |
455	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A media clip of a recording, read in ticks from the clip's start, through its speed and ramps. |
456	| `from` | integer | No | Where to start, in ticks, in the same time as the result. Default: 0. |
457	| `to` | integer | No | Where to stop, not included, in ticks. Must be after `from`. Default: the media's or the clip's duration. |
458	| `kinds` | array of strings | No | Any of `clicks`, `scrolls`, `shortcuts`, `typing` and `path`. Default: the first four. |
459	| `smoothing` | number | No | The path's smoothing, 0 to 1. Default: the clip's own **Smoothing** in its Cursor section, else 0, the raw path. |
460	
461	It returns `ok`, `time` (`media` or `clip`), `from`, `to`, `count`, `media`, `clip` when given, `size` as `[w, h]`, `cursor_file`, `in_picture`, a `project` summary, and one key for each kind asked for:
462	
463	| Key | What it holds |
464	| --- | --- |
465	| `clicks` | A list of `{t, button, down, count, x, y}`. `button` is 0 left, 1 right, 2 other. `down` is 1 for a press and 0 for a release. |
466	| `scrolls` | A list of `{t, x, y, dx, dy}`, each a single wheel event, with `dx` and `dy` in points. |
467	| `shortcuts` | A list of `{t, keys, code}`. |
468	| `typing` | A list of `{from, to, marks}`, each stretch that overlaps the window. |
469	| `path` | `{smoothing, t, x, y}`, sampled 10 times a second. |
470	
471	`x` and `y` are the movie's own pixels from its top left.
472	
473	**Zoom on a click.** With `clip`, each click and scroll also has `q`, as `[qx, qy]`: its position as an offset in source pixels from the centre of the clip's cropped picture. That's the frame `add_zoom_action`'s region takes, so a region around a click is `{x: qx, y: qy, width, height}`. See [Zoom to Region](/motion/zoom-to-region/).
474	
475	**Long recordings.** Rows of every kind and path samples count together, and one result holds at most 5,000. `next` is then the first time left out, so call again with `from: next`.
476	
477	It won't read when:
478	
479	- It doesn't get exactly one of `media` and `clip`.
480	- `kinds` is empty or names something else, or `smoothing` is outside 0 to 1.
481	- `to` isn't after `from`.
482	- The clip isn't a media clip, or it plays reversed. Ask with its media instead.
483	- The media has no cursor file, or the file is missing.
484	
485	## `auto_zoom`
486	
487	Plans screencast zooms from the clicks and typing in a recording's cursor file, and applies them as one undo step, **Auto Zoom**. It's **Clip ▸ Auto Zoom…**. See [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/).
488	
489	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
490	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
491	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
492	| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. |
493	| `zoom` | number | No | How far in, times the clip's own scale: 1.25 to 4. Default: 2. |
494	| `lead` | number | No | Arrive this many seconds before the click: 0.2 to 2. Default: 0.6. |
495	| `stay` | number | No | Stay this many seconds after the last activity: 0.5 to 10. Default: 2.5. |
496	| `follow` | boolean | No | Follows the pointer while zoomed. Default: true. |
497	| `typing` | boolean | No | Zooms on stretches of typing too. Default: true. |
498	| `replace` | boolean | No | Removes the clips' existing zooms first. Default: false. |
499	| `motion_blur` | number | No | The shutter given to each zoomed clip whose own `motion_blur` is 0, as a fraction of a frame: 0 to 1. Default: 0.5, a 180° shutter. 0 sets none. |
500	| `from` | integer | No | Plans only clicks and typing at or after this time, in ticks. With `replace`, removes only zooms that meet the `from` to `to` window. |
501	| `to` | integer | No | Plans only before this time, in ticks. |
502	
503	Each zoom is an ordinary action, the shape `add_zoom_action` makes, so it can be edited like any other. A visit starts at a click, or at a stretch of typing aimed at the last click before it. It zooms in `lead` seconds before that and back out over 0.8 seconds, `stay` seconds after the last activity. [How a visit is planned](/recording/auto-zoom/#how-a-visit-is-planned) has the rest.
504	
505	Halves of a split are planned as one, and nothing straddles a cut. See [Across a split](/recording/auto-zoom/#across-a-split). A planned zoom that meets an action already on the clip is dropped. `replace` removes only zooms, never any other action. A clip that already has a shutter keeps it.
506	
507	It returns what any edit returns, and adds:
508	
509	| Key | What it holds |
510	| --- | --- |
511	| `visits` | How many visits were planned. |
512	| `added`, `replaced`, `dropped` | Zooms added, existing zooms removed, and planned zooms dropped because they met an action. |
513	| `closed_at_cut` | Visits closed at a cut, because the later half wasn't named in the call or has an action of its own there. |
514	| `bases_set` | Later halves whose base was set, by a zoom held across a cut or by `replace` putting it back. |
515	| `blurred` | How many clips were given `motion_blur`. |
516	| `actions` | A list of `{clip, at, duration, kind}`, with `at` in clip ticks and `kind` one of `in`, `pan`, `follow` or `back`. |
517	
518	Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run when a number is out of range, a clip has no picture, or a clip is placed smaller than the canvas. For that last one, nest the clip, open the nest with `set_scope` and call `auto_zoom` inside it.
519	
520	## `add_shortcut_overlays`
521	
522	Places one Keyboard keys graphic clip for each keyboard shortcut recorded, at the moment it was pressed, as one undo step, **Add Shortcut Overlays**. It's **Clip ▸ Add Shortcut Overlays**, which has no sheet, so an agent is the only way to choose these settings. See [Shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/).
523	
524	Only shortcuts are recorded, never typed keys, and only when the recording was made with **Record shortcuts** or `keys: "shortcuts"`. See [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/).
525	
526	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
527	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
528	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
529	| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. |
530	| `duration` | number | No | How long each overlay shows, in seconds: 0.5 to 10. Default: 1.5. |
531	| `position` | string | No | Where the keycaps sit: `bottom` (the default), `center` or `top`. |
532	| `theme` | string | No | The keycaps' look: `dark` (the default) or `light`. |
533	| `from` | integer | No | Places only shortcuts at or after this time, in ticks. |
534	| `to` | integer | No | Places only shortcuts before this time, in ticks. |
535	
536	An overlay never lasts less than 10 frames for each keycap plus 25, the time the template needs to press its last key and exit. Overlays never overlap:
537	
538	- The same shortcut pressed again before its overlay ends extends it, labelled ×2, ×3 and so on.
539	- A different shortcut pressed sooner ends the earlier overlay where it starts, once the earlier one has had its minimum. If that puts it more than 0.5 seconds after its press, it's dropped.
540	
541	The clips go on the front-most track named **Shortcuts** when it's in front of every clip's track, unlocked, shown, not a matte and free over their span. Otherwise they go on a new **Shortcuts** track at the front. A module in `graphics/` whose text equals the bundled template is reused, and otherwise the template is copied in once, only when something is placed.
542	
543	The overlays are ordinary graphic clips. See [Change an overlay](/recording/shortcut-overlays/#change-an-overlay).
544	
545	It returns what any edit returns, and adds:
546	
547	| Key | What it holds |
548	| --- | --- |
549	| `added`, `merged`, `dropped` | Overlays placed, repeat presses folded into one, and presses left out. |
550	| `track`, `new_track` | The track used, and whether it's new. |
551	| `module`, `written` | The module drawn, and whether the template was copied in. |
552	| `overlays` | A list of `{at, duration, keys, label}`, with `at` in timeline ticks. |
553	
554	Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run with a `duration`, `position` or `theme` out of range.
555	
556	## `speed_up_typing`
557	
558	Plays the typing in screen recordings faster, keeping speech and shortcuts at normal speed, as one undo step, **Speed Up Typing**. It's **Clip ▸ Speed Up Typing…**. See [Speed Up Typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/).
559	
560	| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
561	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
562	| `clip` | integer | One of these | A screen recording's media clip. |
563	| `clips` | array of integers | One of these | Media clips whose media have cursor files. Halves of a split recording are joined. |
564	| `rate` | number | No | How much faster a stretch plays: 2 to 8. Default: 4. |
565	| `shortest` | number | No | The shortest stretch sped up, in seconds: 1 to 30. Default: 3. |
566	| `keep_pitch` | boolean | No | Keeps the sped sound's pitch. Default: true. |
567	| `from` | integer | No | Speeds only typing at or after this time, in ticks. |
568	| `to` | integer | No | Speeds only typing before this time, in ticks. |
569	
570	A typing stretch is a run of at least 3 typed keys, each under 1 second apart. Taken out of each stretch are every span of speech, in any clip with sound under it on any track, and each recorded shortcut with its overlay, which is 1.5 seconds when it has no clip on a **Shortcuts** track. The pieces of all the clips join where they meet, and a piece shorter than `shortest` is left alone.
571	
572	Each kept piece is sped by `retime_range` at `rate` on every unlocked track, keeping 0.3 seconds at normal speed at each end, so everything after it moves up in step. See [Tools: speed and time](/mcp/tools-speed/).
573	
574	Speech detection runs on your Mac. If a stretch has sound under it and that media's speech hasn't been saved yet, it's detected in the same step.
575	
576	It returns `ok`, a `project` summary and the ids it created, and adds:
577	
578	| Key | What it holds |
579	| --- | --- |
580	| `stretches`, `short` | Stretches sped up, and pieces left alone for being too short. |
581	| `ranges` | A list of `{from, to, sped_to}`, in timeline ticks before the edit. |
582	| `saved` | The time saved, in ticks. |
583	| `speech_saved` | The media whose speech was saved in this step. |
584	| `audio_left_out`, `audio_note` | Only when a clip with sound now plays past ×12, the ceiling for sound. Unlike the menu command, it doesn't ask. See [If a clip would go silent](/recording/speed-up-typing/#if-a-clip-would-go-silent). |
585	
586	Besides [the shared rules](#the-tools-that-work-from-a-cursor-file), it won't run, and nothing changes, when:
587	
588	- `rate` or `shortest` is out of range.
589	- `retime_range` couldn't do one of the ranges, because of a locked track after it, a transition or a linked clip, for example. The error names it.
590	- Speech detection is still running. It doesn't wait, and it says to try again in a moment.
591	
592	## Related
593	
594	- [Record with record_screen](/mcp/record-screen/)
595	- [Cursor files](/recording/cursor-files/)
596	- [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/)
597	- [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/)

import AVFoundation
import AppKit
import ScreenCaptureKit

/// File ▸ New Recording… (⌥⌘N) — the recorder's panel (road map 3, R1c).
/// One instance for the life of the process, `ExportQueueWindowController`'s
/// mould (`shared`, a private init, `isExcludedFromWindowsMenu`,
/// `isReleasedWhenClosed = false`), because a recording outlives documents
/// and the panel must exist with none open. The controls become one
/// `RecordingChoice`; Record hands it to `ScreenRecorder.shared`; the result
/// goes through `RecordingLanding` into a document or opens a new one. This
/// file is the window, its rows and its phases; `+Rows.swift` is what fills
/// the popups, and `+Choices.swift` turns them into a `RecordingChoice` and
/// back;
/// `+Recording.swift` is everything from Record pressed to the recording
/// running, `+Grants.swift` the three grants a press checks first and the
/// one place System Settings is opened for them, `+Landing.swift`
/// everything from the recording's end to the note that says where it
/// went, `+Picker.swift` the window picker, `+Pause.swift` the pause
/// and the resume, the hidden recording's one door and the phases drawn
/// (R2c), `+VoiceOver.swift` the Source row "Microphone Only" (#99),
/// `+Showing.swift` `show()`, the sync timer, `setNote` and the refit,
/// `+Camera.swift` the Source row "Camera", its popup, the Format popup and
/// the "Record the camera too" box (spec §11 CAM-5, CAM-6, CAM-11),
/// `+CameraPreview.swift` the camera's live preview in `CameraPreviewWell`
/// (CAM-7), `+Devices.swift` hot-plug: the device observers and the
/// popups rebuilt when a device comes or goes (CAM-8), `+Polish.swift` the

418	        // 4. The choice; the microphone is the DEFAULT audio device.
419	        var microphoneID: String?
420	        if microphone {
421	            guard let device = AVCaptureDevice.default(for: .audio) else {
422	                throw ToolError(message: "No microphone is available.")
423	            }
424	            microphoneID = device.uniqueID
425	        }
426	        let choice = RecordingChoice(
427	            source: source, includeFrameJobWindows: includeFrameJob,
428	            microphone: microphoneID, systemAudio: systemAudio,
429	            showClicks: showClicks, rate: rate, resolution: resolution,
430	            destination: destination, folder: folder ?? RecordingFiles.folder(),
431	            camera: cameraPick?.id, cameraFormat: cameraPick?.format, enhanceMicrophone: enhance,
432	            keys: keys, cursor: cursor, autoZoom: polish.contains(.autoZoom),
433	            shortcutOverlays: polish.contains(.shortcutOverlays),
434	            speedUpTyping: polish.contains(.speedUpTyping), cameraLayout: cameraLanding.layout,
435	            cameraCutout: cameraLanding.cutout)
436	
437	        // 5. The recording: start, the span, stop — all waits on this thread.
438	        let result = try record(
439	            filter: filter, choice: choice, seconds: seconds, cameraBeside: cameraBeside)
440	
441	        // 6. A drag in the target document is waited out HERE, on this
442	        //    thread — a wait on main would hold the gesture it waits for.
443	        awaitGestureEnd(destination)
444	
445	        // 7. The landing, on main, through the door the panel does not use;
446	        //    then, with `enhance`, Enhance Voice as its own step (AU-68 (f)),
447	        //    then the polish, each command its own step (CU-101 (j)).
448	        return try landAndEnhance(result, place: place)
449	    }
450	
451	    // MARK: - The recording
452	
453	    /// Start, the span, stop. See the header for the hook and the waits. A
454	    /// filter is a screen recording, started through `start`; with none, a
455	    /// camera (`choice.source == .camera`) is started through `startCamera`
456	    /// and a voice-over through `startVoiceOver`, and the span waits first
457	    /// for their first segment's start (`awaitFirstStart`). `cameraBeside`
458	    /// sizes the stop wait for the camera's probe (CAM-10 (7)).
459	    private func record(
460	        filter: SCContentFilter?, choice: RecordingChoice, seconds: Double, cameraBeside: Bool
461	    ) throws -> RecordingResult {
462	        let recorder = ScreenRecorder.shared
463	        let started = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
464	        let startBox = AgentBox<Result<Void, Error>>()
465	        let finished = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
466	        let box = AgentBox<Result<RecordingResult, Error>>()
467	        let chrome = RecordingToolChrome()
468	        // `onFinish` runs on MAIN, once: the status item comes down before
469	        // the landing, and the box is written before the signal.
470	        let deliver: (Result<RecordingResult, Error>) -> Void = { outcome in
471	            chrome.remove()
472	            if box.value == nil { box.value = outcome }
473	            finished.signal()
474	        }
475	        let startCompletion: (Error?) -> Void = { error in
476	            startBox.value = error.map { .failure($0) } ?? .success(())
477	            started.signal()
478	        }
479	        onMain {
480	            if let filter {
481	                recorder.start(
482	                    filter: filter, choice: choice, mayAsk: false, onFinish: deliver,
483	                    completion: startCompletion)
484	            } else if choice.source == .camera {
485	                recorder.startCamera(
486	                    choice: choice, mayAsk: false, onFinish: deliver,
487	                    completion: startCompletion)
488	            } else {
489	                recorder.startVoiceOver(
490	                    choice: choice, mayAsk: false, onFinish: deliver,
491	                    completion: startCompletion)
492	            }
493	        }
494	        // The recorder's own arm timer answers first; this bound is for a
495	        // start that never answers at all.
496	        guard started.wait(timeout: .now() + ScreenRecorder.armCeiling + 5) == .success else {
497	            throw ToolError(
498	                message: "record_screen timed out waiting for the recording to start."
499	                    + Self.recordingAlertClause)
500	        }
501	        if case .failure(let error) = startBox.value ?? .success(()) {
502	            throw ToolError(message: Self.startSentence(of: error))
503	        }
504	        onMain { chrome.show(recorder) }
505	        if filter == nil { awaitFirstStart(recorder, ended: box) }
506	
507	        // The span: the recording runs on main's run loop, this thread waits,
508	        // and only `onFinish` — an external stop, a failure — wakes it early.
509	        if finished.wait(timeout: .now() + seconds) == .timedOut {
510	            // The segment count is read in the SAME hop that stops: a Resume
511	            // landing between the two would mint a segment — two probes — the
512	            // wait had not budgeted for. The item freezes first (its doc).
513	            let segments = onMain { () -> Int in
514	                chrome.freeze()
515	                let count = max(recorder.heldSegmentCount, 1)
516	                recorder.stop()
517	                return count
518	            }
519	            let ceiling = Self.stopCeiling(segments: segments, camera: cameraBeside)
520	            guard finished.wait(timeout: .now() + ceiling) == .success else {
521	                // The files the recorder still holds — one per segment, and
522	                // a camera file beside each movie that has one.
523	                var cameras: [String] = []
524	                let movies = onMain { () -> [String] in
525	                    chrome.remove()
526	                    cameras = recorder.heldCameraPaths
527	                    return recorder.heldFilePaths
528	                }
529	                throw ToolError(
530	                    message: Self.finishTimeoutSentence(
531	                        movies: movies, cameras: cameras, camera: cameraBeside,
532	                        voiceOver: choice.source == .voiceOver))
533	            }
534	        }
535	        guard let outcome = box.value else {
536	            throw ToolError(message: "The recording ended without a result.")
537	        }
538	        do {
539	            return try outcome.get()
540	        } catch {
541	            throw ToolError(message: Self.sentence(of: error))
542	        }
543	    }
544	
545	    /// SERVER THREAD. A voice-over's start completion answers BEFORE its
546	    /// writer's did-start, so a span counted from it comes out short by the
547	    /// input's start-up time (a second on a Bluetooth input); a camera's
548	    /// answers when segment 0's writer is armed, before its first buffer
549	    /// (CAM-4 point 5: the span is the picture recorded, the warm-up not in
550	    /// it). This polls `heldFirstStartedAt` through `onMain` until it lands,
551	    /// the recording has already ended (`ended` written by `onFinish`), or
552	    /// `ScreenRecorder.armCeiling` passes — past which the span runs as
553	    /// before. A screen recording's start already answers after its arm.
554	    private func awaitFirstStart(
555	        _ recorder: ScreenRecorder, ended: AgentBox<Result<RecordingResult, Error>>
556	    ) {
557	        let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(ScreenRecorder.armCeiling)
558	        while Date() < deadline {
559	            let waiting = onMain { recorder.heldFirstStartedAt == nil && ended.value == nil }
560	            guard waiting else { return }
561	            Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 0.02)
562	        }
563	    }
564	}

569	/// `record_screen`'s ARGUMENT vocabulary and the lookup the arguments meet —
570	/// the second cut off `AgentServer+Recording.swift` (R1 review; the first is
571	/// `+RecordingResult.swift`), taken when the fixes put that file at 481
572	/// lines against the 400-line cap for a new file. The seam is the sentence
573	/// its header had used to describe itself: "the wait around the recorder
574	/// and the argument vocabulary in front of it" — the wait stayed, the
575	/// vocabulary came here, and with it the shareable-content call and the
576	/// display ordering, because they are what the `display` and `window`
577	/// arguments RESOLVE against and nothing else reads them. Every function is
578	/// pure in the arguments, or a wait on one framework answer; none touches
579	/// the recorder. `private` → internal is the whole cost.
580	///
581	/// **The refusal ORDER is decided in the caller**, `recordScreen`, which
582	/// calls these in the order the header there fixes: the caller's own
583	/// mistakes, the grant, the lookup. Nothing here reads a grant.
584	extension AgentServer {
585	
586	    // MARK: - The arguments
587	
588	    /// `source`: what is recorded — the screen (the default), the
589	    /// microphone alone (the panel's Microphone Only, spec §11 recording) or
590	    /// a camera alone (spec §11 CAM-4, `+RecordingCamera.swift`).
591	    enum RecordingSourceKind: String, CaseIterable {
592	        case screen
593	        case voiceOver = "voice_over"
594	        case camera
595	    }
596	
597	    /// The arguments a voice-over refuses by name: everything that only a
598	    /// picture or the stream reads.
599	    static let voiceOverScreenOnlyArguments = [
600	        "display", "window", "system_audio", "show_clicks", "size", "include_framejob_windows",
601	        "auto_zoom", "shortcut_overlays", "speed_up_typing",
602	        "keys", "cursor",
603	    ]
604	
605	    /// `source`, default `screen`; an unknown value refused with the
606	    /// vocabulary; then the camera's argument checks (CAM-4: `camera` with
607	    /// another source, a camera's own strangers). For `voice_over`, the
608	    /// screen-only arguments the caller
609	    /// GAVE (a JSON null is not given, `scalarArg`'s rule) are refused
610	    /// together, in `voiceOverScreenOnlyArguments` order, then
611	    /// `microphone: false`.
612	    func recordingSourceKind(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> RecordingSourceKind {
613	        let kind = try enumArg(a, "source", RecordingSourceKind.self) ?? .screen
614	        try recordingCameraStrangers(a, kind: kind)
615	        guard kind == .voiceOver else { return kind }
616	        let strangers = Self.voiceOverScreenOnlyArguments.filter { a[$0] != nil && !(a[$0] is NSNull) }
617	        guard strangers.isEmpty else {
618	            throw ToolError(
619	                message: "With source voice_over, " + strangers.joined(separator: ", ")
620	                    + " cannot be given — a voice-over records the microphone alone.")
621	        }
622	        if try boolArg(a, "microphone") == false {
623	            throw ToolError(
624	                message: "With source voice_over, microphone cannot be false — a voice-over "
625	                    + "records the microphone alone.")
626	        }
627	        return kind
628	    }
629	
630	    /// `seconds`: required, 1…600. Spelled back as the caller sent it (`0`,
631	    /// not `0.0`) when it is whole.
632	    func recordingSeconds(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> Double {
633	        guard let seconds = try doubleArg(a, "seconds") else {
634	            throw ToolError(message: "Missing required argument: seconds")
635	        }
636	        guard seconds >= 1, seconds <= 600 else {
637	            let whole = seconds == seconds.rounded() && abs(seconds) < 1e15
638	            let spelled = whole ? String(Int(seconds)) : String(seconds)
639	            throw ToolError(message: "seconds must be 1…600 (got \(spelled)).")
640	        }
641	        return seconds
642	    }
643	
644	    /// `display` (an index, default 0) and `window` (a CGWindowID), at most
645	    /// one; the index meets the LIST later, once it can be asked for.
646	    func recordingSourceArguments(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> (Int, CGWindowID?) {
647	        let display = try intArg(a, "display")
648	        let window = try intArg(a, "window")
649	        guard display == nil || window == nil else {
650	            throw ToolError(
651	                message: "Pass display or window, not both — a recording is of one or the other.")
652	        }
653	        if let display, display < 0 {
654	            throw ToolError(message: "display must be 0 or more (got \(display)).")
655	        }
656	        var windowID: CGWindowID?
657	        if let window {
658	            guard window >= 0, window <= Int(CGWindowID.max) else {
659	                throw ToolError(message: "window must be a CGWindowID (got \(window)).")
660	            }
661	            windowID = CGWindowID(window)
662	        }
663	        return (display ?? 0, windowID)
664	    }
665	
666	    /// `enhance` (spec §11 AU-69 (d)), default false: true needs a microphone,
667	    /// then a clip to enhance — `place` — refused in that order.
668	    func recordingEnhance(_ a: [String: Any], microphone: Bool, place: Bool) throws -> Bool {
669	        guard try boolArg(a, "enhance") ?? false else { return false }
670	        guard microphone else {
671	            throw ToolError(
672	                message: "enhance: true enhances the microphone's clip, so it needs "
673	                    + "microphone: true (or source voice_over).")
674	        }
675	        guard place else {
676	            throw ToolError(
677	                message: "enhance: true needs place: true — with place: false the microphone "
678	                    + "lands as media with no clip to enhance.")
679	        }
680	        return true
681	    }
682	
683	    /// `size`: `nominal` (default) or `best`, `requestedFrameFormat`'s form.
684	    func recordingResolution(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> RecordingResolution {
685	        try enumArg(a, "size", RecordingResolution.self, folding: true) ?? .nominal
686	    }
687	
688	    /// `path`, the FOLDER: trimmed, tilde-expanded, and an empty or blank
689	    /// string counting as absent — `RecordingFiles.folder()` then applies —
690	    /// because `URL(fileURLWithPath: "")` is the process's working directory,
691	    /// and a recording written into whatever `cwd` the app was launched
692	    /// from is a file nobody can find.
693	    func recordingFolder(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> URL? {
694	        guard let raw = try stringArg(a, "path") else { return nil }
695	        let trimmed = raw.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
696	        guard !trimmed.isEmpty else { return nil }
697	        return URL(
698	            fileURLWithPath: (trimmed as NSString).expandingTildeInPath, isDirectory: true)
699	    }
700	
701	    /// Where the recording will land, decided BEFORE it starts. A named
702	    /// `project` goes through `target(_:)` and its refusal stands; no name
703	    /// and no document is `.newProject`; otherwise the frontmost. Main.
704	    func recordingDestination(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> RecordingDestination {
705	        if try stringArg(a, "project") != nil {
706	            return .document(recipeKey: try target(a).recipeKey)
707	        }
708	        if openProjects().isEmpty { return .newProject }
709	        return .document(recipeKey: try target(a).recipeKey)
710	    }
711	
712	    // MARK: - The content
713	
714	    /// `ScreenRecorder.shareableContent`, CALLED from this thread (the helper
715	    /// issues the framework call from a global queue and hops the completion
716	    /// to main whatever thread asks) and waited for here. Not through
717	    /// `onMain`: on a locked console the framework held the calling thread
718	    /// ~37 s before answering nothing — main's, through a hop.
719	    func shareableContent() throws -> SCShareableContent {
720	        let semaphore = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
721	        let box = AgentBox<Result<SCShareableContent, Error>>()
722	        ScreenRecorder.shareableContent { outcome in
723	            box.value = outcome
724	            semaphore.signal()
725	        }
726	        guard semaphore.wait(timeout: .now() + 20) == .success else {
727	            throw ToolError(message: "Timed out listing the shareable displays and windows.")
728	        }
729	        switch box.value {
730	        case .success(let content): return content
731	        case .failure(let error): throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
732	        case nil:
733	            throw ToolError(message: "The shareable displays and windows could not be listed.")
734	        }
735	    }
736	
737	    /// The shareable displays, MAIN first — so `display` 0 means what the
738	    /// catalog says whatever order the framework lists them in.
739	    static func orderedDisplays(_ content: SCShareableContent) -> [SCDisplay] {
740	        let main = CGMainDisplayID()
741	        return content.displays.filter { $0.displayID == main }
742	            + content.displays.filter { $0.displayID != main }
743	    }
744	
745	    /// The source the two arguments name. A window id naming nothing
746	    /// shareable is refused by `ScreenRecorder.filter(for:in:excluding:)`'s sentence.
747	    /// An EMPTY display list is a fact about the host — the console is
748	    /// locked or every display is asleep (measured: a true preflight and
749	    /// zero displays, the night the proof was written) — and is named as
750	    /// that, BEFORE the range sentence, which would otherwise read
751	    /// "display must be 0…0 (got 0)" for a caller who asked for nothing odd.
752	    func recordingSource(
753	        _ displayIndex: Int, _ windowID: CGWindowID?, in content: SCShareableContent
754	    ) throws -> RecordingSource {
755	        if let windowID { return .window(windowID) }
756	        let displays = Self.orderedDisplays(content)
757	        guard !displays.isEmpty else {
758	            throw ToolError(
759	                message: "No display is shareable right now — the console is locked or every "
760	                    + "display is asleep; nothing can be recorded until one is.")
761	        }
762	        guard displayIndex < displays.count else {
763	            throw ToolError(
764	                message: "display must be 0…\(displays.count - 1) (got \(displayIndex)); "
765	                    + "\(displays.count) display\(displays.count == 1 ? " is" : "s are") "
766	                    + "shareable.")
767	        }
768	        return .display(displays[displayIndex].displayID)
769	    }
770	}

5	/// File ▸ New Recording… (⌥⌘N) — the recorder's panel (road map 3, R1c).
6	/// One instance for the life of the process, `ExportQueueWindowController`'s
7	/// mould (`shared`, a private init, `isExcludedFromWindowsMenu`,
8	/// `isReleasedWhenClosed = false`), because a recording outlives documents
9	/// and the panel must exist with none open. The controls become one
10	/// `RecordingChoice`; Record hands it to `ScreenRecorder.shared`; the result
11	/// goes through `RecordingLanding` into a document or opens a new one. This
12	/// file is the window, its rows and its phases; `+Rows.swift` is what fills
13	/// the popups, and `+Choices.swift` turns them into a `RecordingChoice` and
14	/// back;
15	/// `+Recording.swift` is everything from Record pressed to the recording
16	/// running, `+Grants.swift` the three grants a press checks first and the
17	/// one place System Settings is opened for them, `+Landing.swift`
18	/// everything from the recording's end to the note that says where it
19	/// went, `+Picker.swift` the window picker, `+Pause.swift` the pause
20	/// and the resume, the hidden recording's one door and the phases drawn
21	/// (R2c), `+VoiceOver.swift` the Source row "Microphone Only" (#99),
22	/// `+Showing.swift` `show()`, the sync timer, `setNote` and the refit,
23	/// `+Camera.swift` the Source row "Camera", its popup, the Format popup and
24	/// the "Record the camera too" box (spec §11 CAM-5, CAM-6, CAM-11),
25	/// `+CameraPreview.swift` the camera's live preview in `CameraPreviewWell`
26	/// (CAM-7), `+Devices.swift` hot-plug: the device observers and the
27	/// popups rebuilt when a device comes or goes (CAM-8), `+Polish.swift` the
28	/// "When it lands:" boxes (road map creator-jobs CU10, spec §11 CU-102), and
29	/// `+CameraLanding.swift` the camera's Layout and cutout (CO8, spec §11 CO-82).
30	/// Fourteen files at the 400-line cap, and the crossing members are internal
31	/// for it, the tree's rule for a class split across files.
32	///
33	/// **It is an `NSPanel`, floating and NON-ACTIVATING**, and each of the four
34	/// window settings below is load-bearing. `.nonactivatingPanel` so Record,
35	/// and the countdown's Cancel, can be clicked with the application about to
36	/// be recorded still FRONTMOST — the panel is off screen once the recording
37	/// runs (below), so this is for the seconds before it, when activating
38	/// Frame Job would put its document windows over the target; `.floating` so
39	/// it stays above that thing; `hidesOnDeactivate = false`
40	/// because `NSPanel` defaults it TRUE (`PreviewWindowController` measured it)
41	/// and a recorder panel that vanished the moment the person switched to the
42	/// application they are about to record would be useless; and NO window
43	/// delegate — a delegate that answers nil for the undo manager is the trap
44	/// `PreviewWindowController` records, and here there is no document to
45	/// answer with. It persists nothing about its frame (the queue window's
46	/// posture: no autosave name, no defaults key for the harness to pin), and
47	/// centres itself once; a panel is picked up and put beside the recorded
48	/// window each time anyway. **Whatever it is refitted to stays on the
49	/// screen it is on** (`fitWindowToContent`, R1 review): the countdown
50	/// numeral grows the card 88 pt DOWNWARD — 130 with a note under it — from
51	/// a fixed top edge, and a panel parked at the bottom of a display, the
52	/// natural place for a recorder, used to put its Cancel button under the
53	/// Dock.
54	///
55	/// **Visibility during a recording** (decision 7, R2c): the panel orders
56	/// OUT at `recordingDidStart` for every source but Microphone Only and
57	/// Camera (below), and the status item is the
58	/// recording's whole chrome — Pause, Resume and Stop are its menu; File ▸
59	/// Stop Recording still stops. R1 kept a DISPLAY recording's panel up, its
60	/// filter excluding Frame Job (R0 q3), and hid only a PICKED window's; the
61	/// user asked for the dialog to go away whatever is recorded, and a panel
62	/// whose one live control was a Stop the menu bar also has earned nothing
63	/// on screen. It comes back after the landing ONLY when it was on screen
64	/// as the recording began (`showWhenLanded`, read at `recordingDidStart`)
65	/// AND the landing left a note (`revealIfNoted`, `+Landing.swift`): a stop
66	/// from the system's own indicator, a closed target, a microphone problem,
67	/// a refused resume, a failure. A clean recording lands and the panel
68	/// stays away, and a panel closed before the recording began stays closed
69	/// whatever the note; ⌥⌘N shows it again. `show()` BEEPS while
70	/// `hiddenForRecording` (R1 review) — the welcome window's button reaches
71	/// it — because a panel un-hidden into the recording would be in the file;
72	/// the quit guard goes through `revealControls()` instead (`+Pause.swift`).
73	/// **It takes key only from an active Frame Job** (spec §11, #137): shown from
74	/// the background it is ordered front without key, so Return stays with
75	/// the app in front. **A voice-over stays UP** (#99): nothing is filmed, so
76	/// the rows lock, the meter stays live, Record reads Stop with a Pause /
77	/// Resume button beside it; Close takes the panel away and the recording
78	/// carries on — the welcome button and the quit guard show the panel again,
79	/// and ⌥⌘N (File ▸ Stop Recording) and the status item stop it. **So does
80	/// a camera recording** (CAM-5), on the same terms: nothing on screen is
81	/// filmed.
82	///
83	/// Two limits of that chrome, accepted (R2 review). With the panel hidden
84	/// the status item is the ONLY Pause and Resume, and macOS drops a status
85	/// item that does not fit the menu bar — behind a notch, in a crowded bar
86	/// — so there Stop survives in the File menu and Pause and Resume do not.
87	/// And "●" and "❚❚" differ in width under `variableLength`, so the items to
88	/// the left of it shift by a few points at each pause and resume.
89	///
90	/// **Quit while recording, and the order AppKit asks in.**
91	/// `AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate` cancels a quit while
92	/// `ScreenRecorder.shared.isRecording` and calls `revealControls()` — the
93	/// status item's menu, opened, while this panel is hidden for its
94	/// recording; `show()` for any other (a tool's, which File ▸ Stop Recording
95	/// ends) — and it is a BACKSTOP: `NSDocumentController` reviews modified
96	/// documents FIRST, so the save sheet comes before the guard, and a target
97	/// document the review CLOSED lands as `.newProject` —
98	/// `RecordingLanding.resolve` looks the destination up by `recipeKey`,
99	/// never minted twice, so the miss is exact, and the landing's note says
100	/// the document was closed.
101	///
102	/// **Two Record Into rules.** The popup is built from `NSMenuItem`s carrying
103	/// each document's `recipeKey` in `representedObject` and is read from
104	/// `selectedItem`, never by index: `NSPopUpButton.addItem(withTitle:)`
105	/// REMOVES a same-titled row (phase 4's defect), and two untitled documents
106	/// read alike. And it follows the FRONT document until the person chooses a
107	/// row themselves (`chosenDestination`), re-synced by a one-second timer
108	/// while the panel is visible — rows compared before any rebuild, so a menu
109	/// the person has open is never rebuilt under the pointer — **and only while
110	/// the phase is idle** (`rebuildDestinations`, R1 review): from the press
111	/// of Record to the landing the rows are FROZEN at what the person saw when
112	/// they pressed it, whichever document comes to the front meanwhile, and
113	/// `landed()`'s own rebuild is what moves them again. The destination the
114	/// recording actually lands in was captured from the controls at the
115	/// countdown's end and cannot move either way; what the freeze buys is that
116	/// the row on screen and the destination in the choice agree.
117	///
118	/// Every choice persists under a `FrameJobRecording…` key (written on change,
119	/// read on show); the harness pins all eighteen on `FrameJobExportChoice`'s terms.
120	/// `.picked` is the one source that cannot persist — a filter is not a
121	/// value — so a reopened panel with a picked window keeps the row only while
122	/// the filter is still held; Microphone Only and Camera persist for the
123	/// session only (the camera itself is remembered, the row is not). "Record
124	/// the camera too" (CAM-11) is remembered across launches, and so is Record
125	/// shortcuts (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-62), off by default, and

378	    /// carries on — the status item and File ▸ Stop Recording can end it —

391	        recorder.discardPreparedCamera()

99	/// A recording's cursor file over MCP (road map "creator-jobs" CU5, spec §11
100	/// CU-50, CU-53): the op tool `set_media_cursor`, which mirrors the Media
101	/// tab's Cursor section ▸ Locate… and Remove (`MediaPane+Cursor.swift`), and
102	/// `get_cursor_events`, a read with no menu: the file's clicks, scrolls,
103	/// shortcuts, typing stretches and path, in media or clip time.
104	extension AgentServer {
105	
106	    // MARK: - set_media_cursor
107	
108	    /// `set_media_cursor` — Locate… and Remove. A non-null `cursor` is held
109	    /// to Locate's own check first (CU-50 (b)): the file opens through the
110	    /// core and its `movie_size` is the movie's (`cursorAttachment`, CU-34),
111	    /// and the call's `in_picture` is the file's. The path checked is the
112	    /// path stored, as given (no `~` expansion). Passing both, the op is
113	    /// sent with the caller's value as given; the core reads it strictly and
114	    /// refuses by name. An unknown media goes on to the core's own sentence;
115	    /// `null` is not checked.
116	    func setMediaCursor(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
117	        let document = try target(a)
118	        let media = try idArg(a, "media")
119	        guard let cursor = a["cursor"] else {
120	            throw ToolError(
121	                message: "Missing required argument: cursor ({path, bookmark?, in_picture} or "
122	                    + "null)")
123	        }
124	        if let object = cursor as? [String: Any],
125	            let path = object["path"] as? String, !path.isEmpty,
126	            let entry = document.project.snapshot.media(media)
127	        {
128	            let file = URL(fileURLWithPath: path)
129	            switch MediaImporter.cursorAttachment(at: file, to: MediaDescriptor(entry)) {
130	            case .failure(let problem):
131	                throw ToolError(message: problem.message)
132	            case .success(let attachment):
133	                if let asked = object["in_picture"] as? Bool,
134	                    asked != attachment.cursor.inPicture
135	                {
136	                    throw ToolError(
137	                        message: "The cursor file \(file.lastPathComponent) was not attached: "
138	                            + "its in_picture is \(attachment.cursor.inPicture) and the call "
139	                            + "says \(asked).")
140	                }
141	            }
142	        }
143	        let name = cursor is NSNull ? "Remove Cursor File" : "Locate Cursor File"
144	        return try editResult(
145	            document, name, [.setMediaCursorRaw(media: media, cursor: cursor)],
146	            ["media": Int(media)])
147	    }
