149	    // MARK: - get_cursor_events
150	
151	    /// What the first main-thread hop resolves.
152	    struct CursorEventsCall {
153	        let document: ProjectDocument
154	        let media: MediaSnapshot
155	        let clip: ClipSnapshot?
156	        let times: AnalysisClipTimes?
157	        let file: URL
158	        let request: CursorEventsAnswer.Request
159	    }
160	
161	    /// `get_cursor_events` — refused in CU-53 (g)'s order. **Runs on the
162	    /// SERVER thread** (`creatorOffMainTools`): one main hop resolves, the
163	    /// file is opened as a fresh `ReelCursor` here, and a last main hop
164	    /// computes Q, which reads `clip_state`, and the summary.
165	    func getCursorEvents(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
166	        guard !Thread.isMainThread else {
167	            throw ToolError(
168	                message: "get_cursor_events must run on the server thread — its name is "
169	                    + "missing from AgentServer.creatorOffMainTools.")
170	        }
171	        let call = try onMain { try self.resolveCursorEventsCall(a) }
172	        let track: ReelCursor
173	        let read: CursorEventsAnswer.Read

226	/// R1d): `ScreenRecorder.shared`, the object the panel drives, run for a
227	/// fixed number of seconds from the agent and landed exactly as the panel
228	/// lands — `RecordingLanding` for the ops, `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`
229	/// for a new project — so the two doors provably do one thing. This file is
230	/// the wait around the recorder and the argument vocabulary in front of it;
231	/// `AgentServer+RecordingResult.swift` is what the answer and the refusals
232	/// SAY, cut off this file at the 400-line cap, and
233	/// `AgentServer+RecordingLanding.swift` the landing, cut at camera-recording CR3-0.
234	///
235	/// **Runs on the server thread** (`AgentServer.offMainTools`), `import_media`'s
236	/// shape and never `transcribe`'s synchronous body: the recorder's every
237	/// callback lands on MAIN, so a main-thread wait would deadlock, and a
238	/// recording of up to ten minutes is not a thing the UI may freeze for. Every
239	/// document touch is an `onMain` hop; every wait is a `DispatchSemaphore`
240	/// signalled from main with an `AgentBox` carrying the answer across.
241	///
242	/// **The refusal ORDER is the contract** (`transcribe`'s rule): the caller's
243	/// own mistakes FIRST, so they stay reachable with no grant — `seconds`
244	/// missing or outside 1…600, then `source` (its value; the camera's
245	/// strangers, `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout` among them, spec §11
246	/// CO-83 (a); for `voice_over`
247	/// the screen-only arguments given, `keys`, `cursor` and the polish's three
248	/// among them, then `microphone: false`), `display` with `window`, a `rate` or `size` outside the
249	/// vocabulary, a `keys` outside its vocabulary (spec §11 CU-62), a `cursor`
250	/// outside its vocabulary (spec §11 CU-36 (e)), `enhance:
251	/// true` without a microphone and then with `place: false` (spec §11 AU-69),
252	/// `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` in that order, each
253	/// with `place: false` and the last two without `keys: "shortcuts"` (road map
254	/// creator-jobs CU10, spec §11 CU-102 (b)), a `camera_layout` outside its
255	/// vocabulary and then, with `place: false`, a `camera_layout` given and a
256	/// `camera_cutout: true` (CO8, spec §11 CO-83 (b)),
257	/// `microphone: true` (implied by a voice-over) with the Microphone grant
258	/// absent (the status WORD in the sentence), `keys: "shortcuts"` with the
259	/// Input Monitoring grant absent (CU-3's sentence, read and never
260	/// requested), and a `project` naming nothing
261	/// open, answered by `target(_:)`'s own sentence and never turned into a
262	/// fresh document. A voice-over stops there: it reads no other grant and
263	/// looks nothing up (spec §11 recording, "A voice-over is a recording with
264	/// no picture"). A camera recording (spec §11 CAM-4) then looks the camera
265	/// up — the named one, else the default, refused naming every camera present
266	/// — then its format (CAM-6), and only then the Camera grant (`+RecordingCamera.swift`); so
267	/// does a screen recording given a `camera` to record beside it (spec §11 CAM-10 (5)),
268	/// before anything screen-side. A
269	/// screen recording then reads the Screen Recording grant,
270	/// synchronously, named with the System Settings pane. Only then the
271	/// display or window lookup, which cannot be asked without the grant — a
272	/// list with NO display in it (a locked console) is named as that, not as
273	/// an index out of range. `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess` and the picker are
274	/// never called, nor is System Settings opened (decision 4): the panel is
275	/// where a person grants.
276	///
277	/// **The target is `.document(recipeKey:)`**, resolved BEFORE the recording
278	/// and looked up again AFTER it (`RecordingLanding.resolve`): a document that
279	/// closed meanwhile lands as a new project and the answer says so, as it does
280	/// for `place: false` in a new project, which still opens the document.
281	///

283	/// calls EXACTLY ONCE at conclude whoever ended the recording — this tool's
284	/// `stop()`, the menu bar's status item, the system's own indicator

286	/// failure — and never for a start that fails, whose error is the start

288	/// past the recorder's own `armCeiling`, whose timer answers first); the
289	/// span, a wait on the FINISH semaphore that `onFinish` ends early when
290	/// something else ended the recording; then, after `stop()`, the same
291	/// semaphore again, bounded at `stopCeiling(segments:camera:)` over the count

293	/// lands the result once) and in any state past idle JOINS the finishing

313	    /// `seconds` and a function of the SEGMENTS the recorder holds: its own

315	    /// sequential `MediaImporter.probe` ceilings of 30 s PER SEGMENT
316	    /// (`MediaImporter.probeTimeout`; `settle` probes each segment's movie, then
317	    /// its microphone file — n segments, 2n probes), plus a margin: 75 s

324	        ScreenRecorder.finishCeiling
325	            + (camera ? 3 : 2) * MediaImporter.probeTimeout * TimeInterval(max(segments, 1)) + 5

453	    /// Start, the span, stop. See the header for the hook and the waits. A
454	    /// filter is a screen recording, started through `start`; with none, a
455	    /// camera (`choice.source == .camera`) is started through `startCamera`
456	    /// and a voice-over through `startVoiceOver`, and the span waits first
457	    /// for their first segment's start (`awaitFirstStart`). `cameraBeside`
458	    /// sizes the stop wait for the camera's probe (CAM-10 (7)).
459	    private func record(
460	        filter: SCContentFilter?, choice: RecordingChoice, seconds: Double, cameraBeside: Bool
461	    ) throws -> RecordingResult {
462	        let recorder = ScreenRecorder.shared
463	        let started = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
464	        let startBox = AgentBox<Result<Void, Error>>()
465	        let finished = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
466	        let box = AgentBox<Result<RecordingResult, Error>>()
467	        let chrome = RecordingToolChrome()
468	        // `onFinish` runs on MAIN, once: the status item comes down before
469	        // the landing, and the box is written before the signal.
470	        let deliver: (Result<RecordingResult, Error>) -> Void = { outcome in
471	            chrome.remove()
472	            if box.value == nil { box.value = outcome }
473	            finished.signal()
474	        }
475	        let startCompletion: (Error?) -> Void = { error in
476	            startBox.value = error.map { .failure($0) } ?? .success(())
477	            started.signal()
478	        }
479	        onMain {
480	            if let filter {
481	                recorder.start(
482	                    filter: filter, choice: choice, mayAsk: false, onFinish: deliver,
483	                    completion: startCompletion)
484	            } else if choice.source == .camera {
485	                recorder.startCamera(
486	                    choice: choice, mayAsk: false, onFinish: deliver,
487	                    completion: startCompletion)
488	            } else {
489	                recorder.startVoiceOver(
490	                    choice: choice, mayAsk: false, onFinish: deliver,
491	                    completion: startCompletion)
492	            }
493	        }
494	        // The recorder's own arm timer answers first; this bound is for a
495	        // start that never answers at all.
496	        guard started.wait(timeout: .now() + ScreenRecorder.armCeiling + 5) == .success else {
497	            throw ToolError(
498	                message: "record_screen timed out waiting for the recording to start."
499	                    + Self.recordingAlertClause)
500	        }
501	        if case .failure(let error) = startBox.value ?? .success(()) {
502	            throw ToolError(message: Self.startSentence(of: error))
503	        }
504	        onMain { chrome.show(recorder) }
505	        if filter == nil { awaitFirstStart(recorder, ended: box) }
506	
507	        // The span: the recording runs on main's run loop, this thread waits,
508	        // and only `onFinish` — an external stop, a failure — wakes it early.
509	        if finished.wait(timeout: .now() + seconds) == .timedOut {
510	            // The segment count is read in the SAME hop that stops: a Resume
511	            // landing between the two would mint a segment — two probes — the
512	            // wait had not budgeted for. The item freezes first (its doc).
513	            let segments = onMain { () -> Int in
514	                chrome.freeze()
515	                let count = max(recorder.heldSegmentCount, 1)
516	                recorder.stop()
517	                return count
518	            }
519	            let ceiling = Self.stopCeiling(segments: segments, camera: cameraBeside)
520	            guard finished.wait(timeout: .now() + ceiling) == .success else {
521	                // The files the recorder still holds — one per segment, and
522	                // a camera file beside each movie that has one.
523	                var cameras: [String] = []
524	                let movies = onMain { () -> [String] in
525	                    chrome.remove()
526	                    cameras = recorder.heldCameraPaths
527	                    return recorder.heldFilePaths
528	                }
529	                throw ToolError(
530	                    message: Self.finishTimeoutSentence(
531	                        movies: movies, cameras: cameras, camera: cameraBeside,
532	                        voiceOver: choice.source == .voiceOver))
533	            }
534	        }
535	        guard let outcome = box.value else {
536	            throw ToolError(message: "The recording ended without a result.")
537	        }
538	        do {
539	            return try outcome.get()
540	        } catch {
541	            throw ToolError(message: Self.sentence(of: error))
542	        }
543	    }

545	    /// SERVER THREAD. A voice-over's start completion answers BEFORE its
546	    /// writer's did-start, so a span counted from it comes out short by the
547	    /// input's start-up time (a second on a Bluetooth input); a camera's
548	    /// answers when segment 0's writer is armed, before its first buffer
549	    /// (CAM-4 point 5: the span is the picture recorded, the warm-up not in
550	    /// it). This polls `heldFirstStartedAt` through `onMain` until it lands,
551	    /// the recording has already ended (`ended` written by `onFinish`), or
552	    /// `ScreenRecorder.armCeiling` passes — past which the span runs as
553	    /// before. A screen recording's start already answers after its arm.
554	    private func awaitFirstStart(
555	        _ recorder: ScreenRecorder, ended: AgentBox<Result<RecordingResult, Error>>
556	    ) {
557	        let deadline = Date().addingTimeInterval(ScreenRecorder.armCeiling)
558	        while Date() < deadline {
559	            let waiting = onMain { recorder.heldFirstStartedAt == nil && ended.value == nil }
560	            guard waiting else { return }
561	            Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 0.02)
562	        }
563	    }

649	        guard display == nil || window == nil else {
650	            throw ToolError(

653	        if let display, display < 0 {
654	            throw ToolError(message: "display must be 0 or more (got \(display)).")
655	        }

657	        if let window {
658	            guard window >= 0, window <= Int(CGWindowID.max) else {
659	                throw ToolError(message: "window must be a CGWindowID (got \(window)).")

689	    /// string counting as absent — `RecordingFiles.folder()` then applies —
690	    /// because `URL(fileURLWithPath: "")` is the process's working directory,
691	    /// and a recording written into whatever `cwd` the app was launched
692	    /// from is a file nobody can find.
693	    func recordingFolder(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> URL? {
694	        guard let raw = try stringArg(a, "path") else { return nil }
695	        let trimmed = raw.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)

703	    /// and no document is `.newProject`; otherwise the frontmost. Main.
704	    func recordingDestination(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> RecordingDestination {
705	        if try stringArg(a, "project") != nil {
706	            return .document(recipeKey: try target(a).recipeKey)

712	    // MARK: - The content
713	
714	    /// `ScreenRecorder.shareableContent`, CALLED from this thread (the helper
715	    /// issues the framework call from a global queue and hops the completion
716	    /// to main whatever thread asks) and waited for here. Not through
717	    /// `onMain`: on a locked console the framework held the calling thread
718	    /// ~37 s before answering nothing — main's, through a hop.
719	    func shareableContent() throws -> SCShareableContent {
720	        let semaphore = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
721	        let box = AgentBox<Result<SCShareableContent, Error>>()
722	        ScreenRecorder.shareableContent { outcome in
723	            box.value = outcome
724	            semaphore.signal()
725	        }
726	        guard semaphore.wait(timeout: .now() + 20) == .success else {
727	            throw ToolError(message: "Timed out listing the shareable displays and windows.")
728	        }
729	        switch box.value {
730	        case .success(let content): return content
731	        case .failure(let error): throw ToolError(message: error.localizedDescription)
732	        case nil:
733	            throw ToolError(message: "The shareable displays and windows could not be listed.")
734	        }
735	    }
736	
737	    /// The shareable displays, MAIN first — so `display` 0 means what the
738	    /// catalog says whatever order the framework lists them in.
739	    static func orderedDisplays(_ content: SCShareableContent) -> [SCDisplay] {
740	        let main = CGMainDisplayID()
741	        return content.displays.filter { $0.displayID == main }
742	            + content.displays.filter { $0.displayID != main }
743	    }
744	
745	    /// The source the two arguments name. A window id naming nothing
746	    /// shareable is refused by `ScreenRecorder.filter(for:in:excluding:)`'s sentence.
747	    /// An EMPTY display list is a fact about the host — the console is
748	    /// locked or every display is asleep (measured: a true preflight and
749	    /// zero displays, the night the proof was written) — and is named as
750	    /// that, BEFORE the range sentence, which would otherwise read
751	    /// "display must be 0…0 (got 0)" for a caller who asked for nothing odd.
752	    func recordingSource(
753	        _ displayIndex: Int, _ windowID: CGWindowID?, in content: SCShareableContent
754	    ) throws -> RecordingSource {
755	        if let windowID { return .window(windowID) }
756	        let displays = Self.orderedDisplays(content)
757	        guard !displays.isEmpty else {
758	            throw ToolError(
759	                message: "No display is shareable right now — the console is locked or every "
760	                    + "display is asleep; nothing can be recorded until one is.")
761	        }
762	        guard displayIndex < displays.count else {
763	            throw ToolError(
764	                message: "display must be 0…\(displays.count - 1) (got \(displayIndex)); "
765	                    + "\(displays.count) display\(displays.count == 1 ? " is" : "s are") "
766	                    + "shareable.")
767	        }
768	        return .display(displays[displayIndex].displayID)
769	    }

5	/// File ▸ New Recording… (⌥⌘N) — the recorder's panel (road map 3, R1c).
6	/// One instance for the life of the process, `ExportQueueWindowController`'s
7	/// mould (`shared`, a private init, `isExcludedFromWindowsMenu`,
8	/// `isReleasedWhenClosed = false`), because a recording outlives documents
9	/// and the panel must exist with none open. The controls become one
10	/// `RecordingChoice`; Record hands it to `ScreenRecorder.shared`; the result
11	/// goes through `RecordingLanding` into a document or opens a new one. This
12	/// file is the window, its rows and its phases; `+Rows.swift` is what fills
13	/// the popups, and `+Choices.swift` turns them into a `RecordingChoice` and
14	/// back;
15	/// `+Recording.swift` is everything from Record pressed to the recording
16	/// running, `+Grants.swift` the three grants a press checks first and the
17	/// one place System Settings is opened for them, `+Landing.swift`
18	/// everything from the recording's end to the note that says where it
19	/// went, `+Picker.swift` the window picker, `+Pause.swift` the pause
20	/// and the resume, the hidden recording's one door and the phases drawn
21	/// (R2c), `+VoiceOver.swift` the Source row "Microphone Only" (#99),
22	/// `+Showing.swift` `show()`, the sync timer, `setNote` and the refit,
23	/// `+Camera.swift` the Source row "Camera", its popup, the Format popup and
24	/// the "Record the camera too" box (spec §11 CAM-5, CAM-6, CAM-11),
25	/// `+CameraPreview.swift` the camera's live preview in `CameraPreviewWell`
26	/// (CAM-7), `+Devices.swift` hot-plug: the device observers and the
27	/// popups rebuilt when a device comes or goes (CAM-8), `+Polish.swift` the
28	/// "When it lands:" boxes (road map creator-jobs CU10, spec §11 CU-102), and
29	/// `+CameraLanding.swift` the camera's Layout and cutout (CO8, spec §11 CO-82).
30	/// Fourteen files at the 400-line cap, and the crossing members are internal
31	/// for it, the tree's rule for a class split across files.
32	///
33	/// **It is an `NSPanel`, floating and NON-ACTIVATING**, and each of the four
34	/// window settings below is load-bearing. `.nonactivatingPanel` so Record,
35	/// and the countdown's Cancel, can be clicked with the application about to
36	/// be recorded still FRONTMOST — the panel is off screen once the recording
37	/// runs (below), so this is for the seconds before it, when activating
38	/// Frame Job would put its document windows over the target; `.floating` so
39	/// it stays above that thing; `hidesOnDeactivate = false`
40	/// because `NSPanel` defaults it TRUE (`PreviewWindowController` measured it)
41	/// and a recorder panel that vanished the moment the person switched to the
42	/// application they are about to record would be useless; and NO window
43	/// delegate — a delegate that answers nil for the undo manager is the trap
44	/// `PreviewWindowController` records, and here there is no document to
45	/// answer with. It persists nothing about its frame (the queue window's
46	/// posture: no autosave name, no defaults key for the harness to pin), and
47	/// centres itself once; a panel is picked up and put beside the recorded
48	/// window each time anyway. **Whatever it is refitted to stays on the
49	/// screen it is on** (`fitWindowToContent`, R1 review): the countdown
50	/// numeral grows the card 88 pt DOWNWARD — 130 with a note under it — from
51	/// a fixed top edge, and a panel parked at the bottom of a display, the
52	/// natural place for a recorder, used to put its Cancel button under the
53	/// Dock.
54	///
55	/// **Visibility during a recording** (decision 7, R2c): the panel orders
56	/// OUT at `recordingDidStart` for every source but Microphone Only and
57	/// Camera (below), and the status item is the
58	/// recording's whole chrome — Pause, Resume and Stop are its menu; File ▸
59	/// Stop Recording still stops. R1 kept a DISPLAY recording's panel up, its
60	/// filter excluding Frame Job (R0 q3), and hid only a PICKED window's; the
61	/// user asked for the dialog to go away whatever is recorded, and a panel
62	/// whose one live control was a Stop the menu bar also has earned nothing
63	/// on screen. It comes back after the landing ONLY when it was on screen
64	/// as the recording began (`showWhenLanded`, read at `recordingDidStart`)
65	/// AND the landing left a note (`revealIfNoted`, `+Landing.swift`): a stop
66	/// from the system's own indicator, a closed target, a microphone problem,
67	/// a refused resume, a failure. A clean recording lands and the panel
68	/// stays away, and a panel closed before the recording began stays closed
69	/// whatever the note; ⌥⌘N shows it again. `show()` BEEPS while
70	/// `hiddenForRecording` (R1 review) — the welcome window's button reaches
71	/// it — because a panel un-hidden into the recording would be in the file;
72	/// the quit guard goes through `revealControls()` instead (`+Pause.swift`).
73	/// **It takes key only from an active Frame Job** (spec §11, #137): shown from
74	/// the background it is ordered front without key, so Return stays with
75	/// the app in front. **A voice-over stays UP** (#99): nothing is filmed, so
76	/// the rows lock, the meter stays live, Record reads Stop with a Pause /
77	/// Resume button beside it; Close takes the panel away and the recording
78	/// carries on — the welcome button and the quit guard show the panel again,
79	/// and ⌥⌘N (File ▸ Stop Recording) and the status item stop it. **So does
80	/// a camera recording** (CAM-5), on the same terms: nothing on screen is
81	/// filmed.
82	///
83	/// Two limits of that chrome, accepted (R2 review). With the panel hidden
84	/// the status item is the ONLY Pause and Resume, and macOS drops a status
85	/// item that does not fit the menu bar — behind a notch, in a crowded bar
86	/// — so there Stop survives in the File menu and Pause and Resume do not.
87	/// And "●" and "❚❚" differ in width under `variableLength`, so the items to
88	/// the left of it shift by a few points at each pause and resume.
89	///
90	/// **Quit while recording, and the order AppKit asks in.**
91	/// `AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate` cancels a quit while
92	/// `ScreenRecorder.shared.isRecording` and calls `revealControls()` — the
93	/// status item's menu, opened, while this panel is hidden for its
94	/// recording; `show()` for any other (a tool's, which File ▸ Stop Recording
95	/// ends) — and it is a BACKSTOP: `NSDocumentController` reviews modified
96	/// documents FIRST, so the save sheet comes before the guard, and a target
97	/// document the review CLOSED lands as `.newProject` —
98	/// `RecordingLanding.resolve` looks the destination up by `recipeKey`,
99	/// never minted twice, so the miss is exact, and the landing's note says
100	/// the document was closed.
101	///
102	/// **Two Record Into rules.** The popup is built from `NSMenuItem`s carrying
103	/// each document's `recipeKey` in `representedObject` and is read from
104	/// `selectedItem`, never by index: `NSPopUpButton.addItem(withTitle:)`
105	/// REMOVES a same-titled row (phase 4's defect), and two untitled documents
106	/// read alike. And it follows the FRONT document until the person chooses a
107	/// row themselves (`chosenDestination`), re-synced by a one-second timer
108	/// while the panel is visible — rows compared before any rebuild, so a menu
109	/// the person has open is never rebuilt under the pointer — **and only while
110	/// the phase is idle** (`rebuildDestinations`, R1 review): from the press
111	/// of Record to the landing the rows are FROZEN at what the person saw when
112	/// they pressed it, whichever document comes to the front meanwhile, and
113	/// `landed()`'s own rebuild is what moves them again. The destination the
114	/// recording actually lands in was captured from the controls at the
115	/// countdown's end and cannot move either way; what the freeze buys is that
116	/// the row on screen and the destination in the choice agree.
117	///
118	/// Every choice persists under a `FrameJobRecording…` key (written on change,
119	/// read on show); the harness pins all eighteen on `FrameJobExportChoice`'s terms.
120	/// `.picked` is the one source that cannot persist — a filter is not a
121	/// value — so a reopened panel with a picked window keeps the row only while

353	        if let sender = sender as? NSPopUpButton, sender === cameraPopup { rebuildCameraFormats() }
354	        if let sender = sender as? NSPopUpButton, sender === cursorPopup {
355	            cursorChosen = RecordingCursor(
356	                rawValue: cursorPopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String ?? "")
357	        }
358	        persistChoices()
359	        refreshSizeNote()
360	        syncControlsEnabled()
361	        syncCameraPreview()
362	    }

368	    /// A countdown must not go on in a panel nobody can see: closing cancels
369	    /// it, and a microphone or camera the countdown prepared is let go with it — said
370	    /// again here rather than left to `cancelCountdown`, because a panel
371	    /// closed during the microphone PROMPT (before any countdown) may also
372	    /// hold one, and an input left open past the panel is the leak the
373	    /// discard exists to close (R1 review). A close while `.starting` is a
374	    /// Stop (R2 review) — the attempt abandoned before `launch`, the
375	    /// recording stopped after it, `stopRecording`'s own two arms — because
376	    /// a start that ran on behind a closed panel would read `showWhenLanded`
377	    /// false and land every later note where nobody sees it. A RECORDING
378	    /// carries on — the status item and File ▸ Stop Recording can end it —
379	    /// and the sync timer stops until the next `show()`. `panelClosing` is
380	    /// set FIRST, so the phase change below steps the preview to off and
381	    /// never builds a capture (CAM-7 (5)), the device observers go (CAM-8 (1)),
382	    /// and the well is emptied last.
383	    @objc private func panelWillClose(_ note: Notification) {
384	        panelClosing = true
385	        switch phase {
386	        case .countdown: cancelCountdown()
387	        case .starting: stopRecording()
388	        default: break
389	        }
390	        recorder.discardPreparedMicrophone()
391	        recorder.discardPreparedCamera()
392	        stopObservingDevices()
393	        syncTimer?.invalidate()
394	        syncTimer = nil
395	        cameraPreview.showMessage(nil)
396	    }
397	}

602	    /// "New Project" first, then every open document by `displayName` with
603	    /// its `recipeKey` in `representedObject`. The selection is the person's
604	    /// own choice while its document is still open, else the front document,
605	    /// else New Project.
606	    ///
607	    /// **Idle only** (R1 review). The rows used to follow the front document
608	    /// through a recording, so a person who pressed Record over "Untitled 2"
609	    /// and then clicked into "Untitled 3" to record it watched the row change
610	    /// to a document the recording was never going to land in — the choice
611	    /// was captured at the countdown's end. The guard is HERE rather than in
612	    /// the sync timer alone because the timer is not the only caller:
613	    /// `show()`, which the quit guard runs during a recording, rebuilds too.
614	    /// `landed()` sets the phase idle before its own rebuild, which is what
615	    /// moves the rows again.
616	    func rebuildDestinations() {
617	        guard phase == .idle else { return }
618	        let rows = Self.destinationRows()
619	        let listed = destinationPopup.itemArray.dropFirst().map { item in
620	            (item.title, (item.representedObject as? NSNumber)?.intValue ?? 0)
621	        }
622	        if destinationPopup.numberOfItems == 0 || !listed.elementsEqual(rows, by: { $0 == $1 }) {
623	            destinationPopup.removeAllItems()
624	            destinationPopup.menu?.addItem(
625	                NSMenuItem(title: "New Project", action: nil, keyEquivalent: ""))
626	            for (title, key) in rows {
627	                let item = NSMenuItem(title: title, action: nil, keyEquivalent: "")
628	                item.representedObject = NSNumber(value: key)
629	                destinationPopup.menu?.addItem(item)
630	            }
631	        }
632	        var wanted: Int?
633	        switch chosenDestination {
634	        case .some(.document(let key)) where rows.contains(where: { $0.1 == key }):
635	            wanted = key
636	        case .some(.newProject):
637	            wanted = nil
638	        default:
639	            chosenDestination = nil
640	            wanted = Self.frontDocument()?.recipeKey
641	        }
642	        let index =
643	            wanted.flatMap { key in
644	                destinationPopup.itemArray.firstIndex {
645	                    ($0.representedObject as? NSNumber)?.intValue == key
646	                }
647	            } ?? 0
648	        if destinationPopup.indexOfSelectedItem != index { destinationPopup.selectItem(at: index) }
649	    }

651	    static func destinationRows() -> [(String, Int)] {
652	        NSDocumentController.shared.documents.compactMap { $0 as? ProjectDocument }.map {
653	            ($0.displayName ?? "Untitled", $0.recipeKey)
654	        }

660	        if let current = NSDocumentController.shared.currentDocument as? ProjectDocument {
661	            return current

666	    static func displayID(of screen: NSScreen) -> CGDirectDisplayID {
667	        let key = NSDeviceDescriptionKey("NSScreenNumber")
668	        return (screen.deviceDescription[key] as? NSNumber)?.uint32Value ?? CGMainDisplayID()
669	    }

671	    var selectedDisplayID: CGDirectDisplayID {
672	        (sourcePopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? NSNumber)?.uint32Value
673	            ?? CGMainDisplayID()
674	    }

676	    var selectedScreen: NSScreen? {
677	        guard sourcePopup.selectedItem?.tag != Self.windowTag, !voiceOverSelected, !cameraSelected
678	        else { return nil }
679	        let id = selectedDisplayID

687	            } ?? 0

693	            id.flatMap { wanted in

703	/// The recorder panel's choice: how the controls become one
704	/// `RecordingChoice`, how that choice is written to and read back from
705	/// `UserDefaults`, and the size note beside it. A pure move out of
706	/// `RecorderPanelController+Rows.swift` under road map "creator-jobs"
707	/// CU0a's toll U3.
708	extension RecorderPanelController {
709	    // MARK: - The choice, persisted and restored
710	
711	    /// The controls as one value. `.picked` only while the picker's filter
712	    /// is held; a "Window…" row with no filter (the picker was cancelled and
713	    /// the row not reselected) falls back to the main display. `camera` is
714	    /// the Camera popup's id while a camera is wanted (Source Camera, or the
715	    /// box beside a screen source: CAM-11 (3)), and nil otherwise;
716	    /// `cameraFormat` the Format popup's spelling beside it, nil for Best.
717	    func currentChoice() -> RecordingChoice {
718	        var choice = RecordingChoice()
719	        if voiceOverSelected {
720	            choice.source = .voiceOver
721	        } else if cameraSelected {
722	            choice.source = .camera
723	        } else if sourcePopup.selectedItem?.tag == Self.windowTag, pickedFilter != nil {
724	            choice.source = .picked
725	        } else {
726	            choice.source = .display(selectedDisplayID)
727	        }
728	        if cameraWanted {
729	            choice.camera = selectedCameraID
730	            choice.cameraFormat = selectedCameraFormat
731	        }
732	        choice.includeFrameJobWindows = includeFrameJobCheckbox.state == .on
733	        choice.microphone = microphonePopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String
734	        choice.enhanceMicrophone = enhanceMicrophoneCheckbox.state == .on && choice.microphone != nil
735	        choice.systemAudio = systemAudioSwitch.state == .on
736	        choice.showClicks = showClicksSwitch.state == .on
737	        // CU-62: shortcuts only with a screen source; off for Microphone Only and Camera.
738	        choice.keys =
739	            recordShortcutsCheckbox.state == .on && !voiceOverSelected && !cameraSelected
740	            ? .shortcuts : .off
741	        // CU-36: the person's pick, nil for the source's default; none without a screen source.
742	        choice.cursor = voiceOverSelected || cameraSelected ? nil : cursorChosen
743	        choice.rate = Self.rates.contains(ratePopup.selectedTag()) ? ratePopup.selectedTag() : 60
744	        choice.resolution =
745	            RecordingResolution(rawValue: sizePopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String ?? "")
746	            ?? .nominal
747	        if let key = destinationPopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? NSNumber {
748	            choice.destination = .document(recipeKey: key.intValue)
749	        } else {
750	            choice.destination = .newProject
751	        }
752	        applyPolish(to: &choice)
753	        applyCameraLanding(to: &choice)
754	        return choice
755	    }
756	
757	    /// Writes every control but the destination (a `recipeKey` is minted per
758	    /// process) and a picked window (a filter is not a value). The display
759	    /// key is left alone while the Window row, Microphone Only or Camera (the
760	    /// two session-only rows) is selected. The camera key, and the format
761	    /// key beside it (`""` for Best), are written only while the Camera popup
762	    /// names one, so "None connected" forgets nothing. The box's key is written
763	    /// on every change (CAM-11 (2)).
764	    func persistChoices() {
765	        let defaults = UserDefaults.standard
766	        if sourcePopup.selectedItem?.tag != Self.windowTag, !voiceOverSelected, !cameraSelected {
767	            defaults.set(Int(selectedDisplayID), forKey: Self.displayKey)
768	        }
769	        defaults.set(
770	            microphonePopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String ?? "",
771	            forKey: Self.microphoneKey)
772	        if let camera = selectedCameraID {
773	            defaults.set(camera, forKey: Self.cameraKey)
774	            defaults.set(selectedCameraFormat ?? "", forKey: Self.cameraFormatKey)
775	        }
776	        defaults.set(systemAudioSwitch.state == .on, forKey: Self.systemAudioKey)
777	        defaults.set(showClicksSwitch.state == .on, forKey: Self.showClicksKey)
778	        defaults.set(
779	            includeFrameJobCheckbox.state == .on, forKey: Self.includeFrameJobWindowsKey)
780	        defaults.set(cameraBesideCheckbox.state == .on, forKey: Self.cameraBesideKey)
781	        defaults.set(enhanceMicrophoneCheckbox.state == .on, forKey: Self.enhanceMicrophoneKey)
782	        defaults.set(recordShortcutsCheckbox.state == .on, forKey: Self.keysKey)
783	        // CU-36 (d): the pick, never the row shown; `""` follows the source.
784	        defaults.set(cursorChosen?.rawValue ?? "", forKey: Self.cursorKey)
785	        defaults.set(currentChoice().rate, forKey: Self.rateKey)
786	        defaults.set(currentChoice().resolution.rawValue, forKey: Self.sizeKey)
787	        persistPolish(defaults)
788	        persistCameraLanding(defaults)
789	    }
790	
791	    /// The stored choices, each falling back to `RecordingChoice`'s default
792	    /// for an absent or stale value: a display no longer attached is the
793	    /// main one, a microphone no longer connected is Off, a camera no longer
794	    /// connected is the default camera, system audio is ON
795	    /// when nothing is stored (`bool(forKey:)` of an absent key is false, so
796	    /// the absence is tested by name).
797	    func restoreChoices() {
798	        let defaults = UserDefaults.standard
799	        if pickedFilter == nil, !voiceOverSelected, !cameraSelected {
800	            let stored = defaults.integer(forKey: Self.displayKey)
801	            selectDisplay(stored > 0 ? CGDirectDisplayID(clamping: stored) : CGMainDisplayID())
802	        }
803	        let mic = defaults.string(forKey: Self.microphoneKey) ?? ""
804	        selectMicrophone(mic.isEmpty ? nil : mic)
805	        let camera = defaults.string(forKey: Self.cameraKey) ?? ""
806	        selectCamera(camera.isEmpty ? nil : camera)
807	        let systemAudio =
808	            defaults.object(forKey: Self.systemAudioKey) == nil
809	            ? RecordingChoice().systemAudio : defaults.bool(forKey: Self.systemAudioKey)
810	        systemAudioSwitch.state = systemAudio ? .on : .off
811	        showClicksSwitch.state = defaults.bool(forKey: Self.showClicksKey) ? .on : .off
812	        includeFrameJobCheckbox.state =
813	            defaults.bool(forKey: Self.includeFrameJobWindowsKey) ? .on : .off
814	        cameraBesideCheckbox.state = defaults.bool(forKey: Self.cameraBesideKey) ? .on : .off
815	        enhanceMicrophoneCheckbox.state =
816	            defaults.bool(forKey: Self.enhanceMicrophoneKey) ? .on : .off
817	        recordShortcutsCheckbox.state = defaults.bool(forKey: Self.keysKey) ? .on : .off
818	        cursorChosen = RecordingCursor(rawValue: defaults.string(forKey: Self.cursorKey) ?? "")
819	        let rate = defaults.integer(forKey: Self.rateKey)
820	        _ = ratePopup.selectItem(withTag: Self.rates.contains(rate) ? rate : RecordingChoice().rate)
821	        let size = defaults.string(forKey: Self.sizeKey) ?? ""
822	        let resolution = RecordingResolution(rawValue: size) ?? RecordingChoice().resolution
823	        sizePopup.selectItem(at: RecordingResolution.allCases.firstIndex(of: resolution) ?? 0)
824	        restorePolish(defaults)
825	        restoreCameraLanding(defaults)
826	    }
827	
828	    /// The Cursor popup shows the person's pick, else the screen source's
829	    /// default: Separate for every screen source (spec §11 CU-36, amended at
830	    /// CU0d). Left as it is for Microphone Only and Camera, whose row is
831	    /// greyed with its value kept.
832	    func syncCursorPopup() {
833	        guard !voiceOverSelected, !cameraSelected else { return }
834	        let shown = cursorChosen ?? .defaultFor(currentChoice().source)
835	        if let item = cursorPopup.itemArray.first(where: {
836	            $0.representedObject as? String == shown.rawValue
837	        }) {
838	            cursorPopup.select(item)
839	        }
840	    }

842	    /// `1728×1117 points · 3456×2234 pixels` for the chosen display; a picked
843	    /// window records at its own size, which the panel cannot know; a
844	    /// voice-over has no picture; a camera records at its best format. The
845	    /// Cursor popup is synced FIRST, before the three early returns, so the
846	    /// Window row (no `selectedScreen`) follows its source too.
847	    func refreshSizeNote() {
848	        syncCursorPopup()
849	        if voiceOverSelected {
850	            sizeNote.stringValue = Self.voiceOverSizeNote
851	            return
852	        }
853	        if cameraSelected {
854	            sizeNote.stringValue = selectedCameraSizeNote
855	            return
856	        }
857	        guard let screen = selectedScreen else {
858	            sizeNote.stringValue = "the picked window's own size"
859	            return
860	        }
861	        let size = screen.frame.size
862	        let scale = screen.backingScaleFactor
863	        sizeNote.stringValue =
864	            "\(Int(size.width))×\(Int(size.height)) points · "
865	            + "\(Int((size.width * scale).rounded()))×\(Int((size.height * scale).rounded())) pixels"

3	/// Pause and resume from the panel's side, the one door into a hidden
4	/// recording's controls, and the phases drawn (road map 3, R2c) —
5	/// `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s sixth file, NEW rather than cut for its
6	/// first two members: they are the whole of what the panel adds for a pause,
7	/// and `+Recording.swift` and the base file were both within a dozen lines
8	/// of the 400-line cap when R2 began. `syncPhase` and `refreshStatusLabel`
9	/// then MOVED here from the base file when the R2 review's fixes took it
10	/// over the cap — the base file's toll, paid along the line the footnote
11	/// draws: its `.paused` and `.stopping` arms are what the pause added, and
12	/// `syncPhase` is its one caller besides the tick.
13	///
14	/// **Neither pause member is reachable from the panel's own controls** but
15	/// in a voice-over, whose panel stays up with a Pause / Resume button
16	/// (`+VoiceOver.swift`). The panel is off screen for every other recording
17	/// (decision 7), so Pause Recording
18	/// and Resume Recording are rows of the status item's menu, which calls
19	/// these through the closures `recordingDidStart` hands it, and File ▸
20	/// Pause/Resume Recording (`AppDelegate+Recording.swift`), the second door,
21	/// which calls them for the panel's own recording (#98). The panel's
22	/// phase — `.recording ⇄ .paused` — follows the recorder's own `pause()` /
23	/// `resume()` (`ScreenRecorder+Pause.swift`), which are synchronous and
24	/// throw. The phase moves only AFTER the call returns
25	/// without throwing, so the panel never claims a state the recorder
26	/// refused: a pause that could not close the segment's file leaves the
27	/// recorder `.recording` and the panel with it, and a resume whose output
28	/// could not be added leaves both `.paused`.
29	///
30	/// **The two refusals are answered differently, on purpose.** A refused
31	/// pause BEEPS: the recorder is still recording, nothing was lost, and the
32	/// panel is hidden, so a note there would be read by nobody until the
33	/// landing, by which time it would be stale. A refused resume keeps the
34	/// recorder's sentence as `resumeProblem` and stays paused: the stream still
35	/// captures but no file is taking it, so what the person does next — try
36	/// again, or stop and land what was recorded — depends on the sentence, and
37	/// the landing's reveal (`revealIfNoted`, `+Landing.swift`) brings the
38	/// panel back with that sentence in its note when they stop. The sentence
39	/// is STATE and never text read back off the label (R2 review): the live
40	/// note is rebuilt from `[microphoneProblem, resumeProblem]` at every tick
41	/// (`syncMicrophoneNote`, over `liveNote` below), so a microphone
42	/// did-finish landing late cannot wipe it and a retried resume replaces it
43	/// rather than appending a second copy; and `landingNote` takes it as an
44	/// argument, so the landing's note carries it where the first shape — each
45	/// end replacing the label whole — dropped it, and the reveal showed
46	/// nothing. A resume that LANDS clears it: a sentence about a refusal the
47	/// person has since got past would bring the panel back with nothing true
48	/// to say.
49	///
50	/// A Stop while paused (`stopRecording`, `record(_:)`, File ▸ Stop
51	/// Recording) goes to `recorder.stop()` exactly as one while recording
52	/// does — the recorder's `.paused` arm takes the same finishing path with
53	/// the segment's output already closed — and the status item comes down at
54	/// `recordingEnded` as ever. The tick runs through `.paused` (`armTick`):
55	/// the meter poll is a no-op there, the recorder having silenced the bar at
56	/// the pause, and `elapsed` is frozen, so the footnote and the item hold
57	/// still on their own.
58	extension RecorderPanelController {
59	    // MARK: - Pause and resume
60	
61	    /// The status item's Pause Recording, and File ▸ Pause Recording's for
62	    /// the panel's own recording. `.recording` → `.paused`; any
63	    /// other phase beeps — the row was clicked in the moment between a Stop
64	    /// and the item coming down — and so does any throw, `.alreadyPaused`
65	    /// among them (the header).
66	    func pauseRecording() {
67	        guard phase == .recording else {
68	            NSSound.beep()
69	            return
70	        }
71	        do {
72	            try recorder.pause()
73	            phase = .paused
74	        } catch {
75	            NSSound.beep()
76	        }
77	    }
78	
79	    /// The status item's Resume Recording, and File ▸ Resume Recording's.
80	    /// `.paused` → `.recording`, with
81	    /// the refused-resume sentence cleared; any other phase beeps. A throw
82	    /// leaves the phase paused and keeps the recorder's sentence as
83	    /// `resumeProblem`, REPLACING an earlier one, redrawn into the note at
84	    /// once rather than at the tick's next turn (the header).
85	    func resumeRecording() {
86	        guard phase == .paused else {
87	            NSSound.beep()
88	            return
89	        }
90	        do {
91	            try recorder.resume()
92	            resumeProblem = nil
93	            phase = .recording
94	        } catch {
95	            resumeProblem = error.localizedDescription
96	            syncMicrophoneNote()
97	        }
98	    }
99	
100	    /// The live note's two parts, in order: the microphone's sentence, with
101	    /// the fact that the picture is still recording (a silent meter alone
102	    /// reads as a broken recording), then a refused resume's; empty with
103	    /// neither. Pure, so a probe can pin the composition without a recorder.
104	    static func liveNote(microphoneProblem: String?, resumeProblem: String?) -> String {
105	        var sentences: [String] = []
106	        if let microphoneProblem {
107	            sentences.append(
108	                "The microphone stopped: \(microphoneProblem) The picture is still recording.")
109	        }
110	        if let resumeProblem { sentences.append(resumeProblem) }
111	        return sentences.joined(separator: " ")
112	    }
113	
114	    // MARK: - The hidden recording's one door
115	
116	    /// The quit guard's call (`AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate`).
117	    /// While this panel is hidden for its recording `show()` can only beep,
118	    /// and a beep tells a person who paused and forgot nothing — so the
119	    /// status item's menu is opened instead, Pause or Resume and Stop put
120	    /// in front of them (`RecorderStatusItem.openMenu`); the beep is kept
121	    /// for the one case with no item to open. Any other recording — a
122	    /// tool's, which File ▸ Stop Recording ends — shows the panel as before.
123	    func revealControls() {
124	        guard hiddenForRecording else {
125	            show()
126	            return
127	        }
128	        if statusItem?.openMenu() != true { NSSound.beep() }
129	    }
130	
131	    // MARK: - The phases, drawn
132	
133	    /// Draws the phase: the button's title and enabled state, the controls
134	    /// locked while anything is in flight, the countdown numeral, the
135	    /// footnote, the camera preview (CAM-7), and the window refitted to
136	    /// whatever appeared or went.
137	    func syncPhase() {
138	        syncControlsEnabled()
139	        syncPauseButton()
140	        var countdown: String?
141	        switch phase {
142	        case .idle:
143	            recordButton.title = "Record"
144	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
145	        case .countdown(let remaining):
146	            recordButton.title = "Cancel"
147	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
148	            countdown = "\(remaining)"
149	        case .starting:
150	            recordButton.title = "Starting…"
151	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
152	        case .recording, .paused:
153	            recordButton.title = "Stop"
154	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
155	        case .stopping:
156	            recordButton.title = "Stopping…"
157	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
158	        case .landing:
159	            recordButton.title = "Adding…"
160	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
161	        }
162	        recordButton.invalidateIntrinsicContentSize()
163	        countdownLabel.stringValue = countdown ?? ""
164	        countdownLabel.isHidden = countdown == nil
165	        refreshStatusLabel()
166	        syncCameraPreview()
167	        fitWindowToContent()
168	    }
169	
170	    /// The footnote: the folder while idle, the coral dot and the elapsed
171	    /// time while recording, the pause glyph and the frozen time while
172	    /// paused — faint, because the dot's colour means "capturing" — and
173	    /// through `.stopping` whichever of those two it last showed, left
174	    /// UNTOUCHED (R2 review): the phase no longer says whether the Stop
175	    /// came from paused, `elapsed` is frozen at the stop call, and
176	    /// redrawing the arm as recording brought the coral dot back over a
177	    /// finish that captures nothing. The status item keeps its mark the
178	    /// same way (`RecorderStatusItem.freeze`, called by `stopRecording`).
179	    func refreshStatusLabel() {
180	        switch phase {
181	        case .recording:
182	            statusLabel.stringValue = "● " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)
183	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.meterClip
184	        case .paused:
185	            statusLabel.stringValue =
186	                RecorderStatusItem.pauseGlyph + " " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)
187	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint

189	            break
190	        default:
191	            statusLabel.stringValue =

213	    /// capture that failed (or a build that threw) is let go first, so the

215	    /// are added before that sync, which applies a change made while the
216	    /// panel was closed (CAM-8 (1)).
217	    func show() {

220	            return
221	        }

248	    /// steps again (CAM-7 (5)).
249	    private func armSyncTimer() {
250	        guard syncTimer == nil else { return }
251	        syncTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { [weak self] timer in
252	            guard let self else {
253	                timer.invalidate()
254	                return
255	            }
256	            guard self.window?.isVisible == true else { return }

279	    /// programmatically, on screen or off — which is why the call is
280	    /// explicit.
281	    func fitWindowToContent() {
282	        guard let window else { return }

315	    var requestScreen: () -> Void
316	    var screenAsked: () -> Bool
317	    var rememberScreenAsked: () -> Void

319	    var requestMicrophone: (@escaping () -> Void) -> Void

322	    var cameraStatus: () -> AVAuthorizationStatus

363	/// recording) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s seventh file, cut out of
364	/// `+Recording.swift` when the press learned to open System Settings.
365	///
366	/// **The grants are asked for HERE and nowhere else, and UNCONDITIONALLY**
367	/// (decision 4: the TOOL never asks — it reads the status and refuses by
368	/// name — because a system prompt needs a person in front of it; the panel
369	/// asks, because a press of Record IS that person, exactly as the transcribe
370	/// sheet's Start is). **This is also the only place System Settings is
371	/// opened for them**, and the tool never opens it. Screen Recording is
372	/// asked with `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` on the FIRST press that finds
373	/// it absent — the system prompt appears once per app, not per launch — and
374	/// the ask is remembered in `FrameJobScreenRecordingAsked`; every later press
375	/// opens the Screen & System Audio Recording pane and the note says so.
376	/// `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` returns false at once on a first ask, so
377	/// the refusal sentence is shown either way and the person presses Record
378	/// again once the grant is on. The flag is read and written only in a
379	/// launchd-owned launch: a shell-launched press always asks and never
380	/// remembers, because TCC attributes that prompt to the terminal (R0 q1).
381	/// The microphone is asked only when one is chosen, from `.notDetermined`,
382	/// and the countdown starts from the answer; `.denied` and `.restricted`
383	/// open the Microphone pane and stop there, and a prompt's answer never
384	/// opens it. Both readings happen BEFORE the countdown, so a countdown never
385	/// ends in a prompt. An earlier draft gated both asks on a `canAsk` (since
386	/// deleted with the speech grant) — false for a scripted agent launch —
387	/// and the R1 review measured what that cost: under that flag the refusal
388	/// note told the person to press the button they had just pressed, and a
389	/// `notDetermined` microphone could never be granted from anywhere.
390	/// `canAsk` is the tool's rule about a prompt nobody would see; it does not
391	/// apply to a button somebody clicked. **The Camera grant** (CR1c, spec §11
392	/// CAM-5) is the third, read only for Source Camera, whose press never reads
393	/// Screen Recording: the microphone's steps, through its own pane
394	/// (`Privacy_Camera`), and its prompt's answer RE-READS the grant before the
395	/// microphone and the countdown, so a refused prompt stops there. **Input
396	/// Monitoring** (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-3, CU-62) is the
397	/// fourth, read only when Record shortcuts is on with a screen source, after
398	/// Screen Recording and before the Camera and the Microphone. Its step is
399	/// Screen Recording's table, remembered in `FrameJobInputMonitoringAsked`;
400	/// because no prompt shows and Frame Job is not listed until a person adds
401	/// it (CU0b), an ask ALSO opens the Input Monitoring pane, and the note says
402	/// to add Frame Job with + (`inputMonitoringNote(opened:)`).
403	extension RecorderPanelController {
404	    /// The doors every grant call goes through; a probe replaces it.
405	    static var grantDoors = RecorderGrantDoors.live
406	
407	    /// A system prompt, or System Settings, is about to come up in ANOTHER
408	    /// process at normal window level, and a `.floating` panel sits over
409	    /// every normal window on the screen: the person found the Screen
410	    /// Recording prompt hidden behind the panel until they dragged it away
411	    /// (2026-09-28). So the panel steps down to `.normal` first, and
412	    /// `floatAgain` puts it back on the next press that goes on, or on
413	    /// `show()`.
414	    func stepAsideForSystemUI() { window?.level = .normal }
415	    func floatAgain() { window?.level = .floating }
416	
417	    /// Screen Recording, for a press: true to go on; false with the note
418	    /// set, and the press ends. `screenStep` is the one decision point.
419	    func checkScreenRecordingGrant() -> Bool {
420	        floatAgain()
421	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
422	        let owned = doors.launchedByLaunchd()
423	        let step = RecordingGrant.screenStep(
424	            granted: doors.screenGranted(), asked: doors.screenAsked(), launchedByLaunchd: owned)
425	        switch step {
426	        case .proceed:
427	            return true
428	        case .ask:
429	            if owned { doors.rememberScreenAsked() }
430	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
431	            doors.requestScreen()
432	            setNote(RecordingGrant.screenRecordingRefusal)
433	            return false
434	        case .openPane:
435	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
436	            let opened = RecordingGrant.screenRecordingPaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
437	            setNote(
438	                opened ? RecordingGrant.screenRecordingOpenedNote : RecordingGrant.screenRecordingRefusal)
439	            return false
440	        }
441	    }

444	    /// off (it is `.off` for a voice-over and a camera) or granted; false with
445	    /// the note set, and the press ends. `inputMonitoringStep` decides.
446	    func checkInputMonitoringGrant() -> Bool {
447	        guard currentChoice().keys == .shortcuts else { return true }
448	        floatAgain()
449	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
450	        let owned = doors.launchedByLaunchd()
451	        let step = RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringStep(
452	            granted: doors.inputMonitoringGranted(), asked: doors.inputMonitoringAsked(),
453	            launchedByLaunchd: owned)
454	        switch step {
455	        case .proceed:
456	            return true
457	        case .ask:
458	            if owned { doors.rememberInputMonitoringAsked() }
459	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
460	            doors.requestInputMonitoring()
461	            let opened = RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringPaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
462	            setNote(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringNote(opened: opened))
463	            return false
464	        case .openPane:
465	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
466	            let opened = RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringPaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
467	            setNote(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringNote(opened: opened))
468	            return false
469	        }
470	    }
471	
472	    /// The microphone, for a press: true to go on (none chosen, or
473	    /// authorized); false when it asked (the answer continues the press) or
474	    /// opened its pane.
475	    func checkMicrophoneGrant() -> Bool {
476	        guard currentChoice().microphone != nil else { return true }
477	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
478	        let status = doors.microphoneStatus()
479	        switch RecordingGrant.microphoneStep(status) {
480	        case .proceed:
481	            return true
482	        case .ask:
483	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
484	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
485	            doors.requestMicrophone { [weak self] in self?.microphoneAnswered() }
486	            return false
487	        case .openPane:
488	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
489	            let opened = RecordingGrant.microphonePaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
490	            setNote(
491	                opened
492	                    ? RecordingGrant.microphoneOpenedNote(status)
493	                    : RecordingGrant.microphoneRefusal(status))
494	            return false
495	        }
496	    }
497	
498	    /// The prompt's answer. The button comes back either way; the countdown
499	    /// begins only in an idle panel that is still ON SCREEN (R1 review) — a
500	    /// panel closed during the prompt must not count down where nobody can
501	    /// cancel it, and `panelWillClose` cannot cancel a countdown that has not
502	    /// begun. It never opens System Settings.
503	    private func microphoneAnswered() {
504	        recordButton.isEnabled = true
505	        guard phase == .idle, window?.isVisible == true else { return }
506	        let status = Self.grantDoors.microphoneStatus()
507	        guard status == .authorized else {
508	            setNote(RecordingGrant.microphoneRefusal(status))
509	            return
510	        }
511	        setNote("")
512	        floatAgain()
513	        beginCountdown()
514	    }

516	    /// The camera, for a press with Source Camera: true to go on
517	    /// (authorized); false when it asked (the answer continues the press) or
518	    /// opened its pane — `checkMicrophoneGrant`'s three arms.
519	    func checkCameraGrant() -> Bool {
520	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
521	        let status = doors.cameraStatus()
522	        switch RecordingGrant.cameraStep(status) {
523	        case .proceed:
524	            return true
525	        case .ask:
526	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
527	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
528	            doors.requestCamera { [weak self] in self?.cameraAnswered() }
529	            return false
530	        case .openPane:
531	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
532	            let opened = RecordingGrant.cameraPaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
533	            setNote(
534	                opened
535	                    ? RecordingGrant.cameraOpenedNote(status)
536	                    : RecordingGrant.cameraRefusal(status))
537	            return false
538	        }
539	    }

541	    /// The camera prompt's answer, `microphoneAnswered`'s rule: the button
542	    /// comes back either way, and the press goes on only in an idle panel
543	    /// still on screen. The grant is READ AGAIN first — anything but
544	    /// authorized stops with the refusal, no microphone prompt and no
545	    /// countdown — then the microphone's grant, then the countdown.
546	    private func cameraAnswered() {
547	        recordButton.isEnabled = true
548	        guard phase == .idle, window?.isVisible == true else { return }
549	        let status = Self.grantDoors.cameraStatus()
550	        guard status == .authorized else {
551	            setNote(RecordingGrant.cameraRefusal(status))
552	            return
553	        }
554	        setNote("")
555	        floatAgain()
556	        guard checkMicrophoneGrant() else { return }

558	    }

200	/// the three arguments `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` and their
201	/// refusals, and the tool door's follow-up after `land` and any Enhance Voice — the panel's
202	/// "When it lands:" boxes without the panel. Every command is its tool's own body
203	/// (`autoZoom(document:clips:settings:)` and the two beside it) at the tools' defaults, since a
204	/// tool reads no `UserDefaults`, each its own undo step.

206	
207	    /// The three booleans (default false), in the order auto_zoom, shortcut_overlays,
208	    /// speed_up_typing, each refused without `place` and the last two without `keys:
209	    /// "shortcuts"` (CU-102 (b)); read after `enhance`, before any grant. With voice_over or
210	    /// camera they never reach here: the source's stranger lists refuse them by name.
211	    func recordingPolish(_ a: [String: Any], place: Bool, keys: RecordingKeys) throws
212	        -> [RecordingPolish.Command]
213	    {
214	        var asked: [RecordingPolish.Command] = []
215	        for command in RecordingPolish.Command.allCases {
216	            guard try boolArg(a, command.rawValue) ?? false else { continue }
217	            if !place { throw ToolError(message: Self.polishNeedsPlace(command)) }
218	            if command != .autoZoom, keys != .shortcuts {
219	                throw ToolError(message: Self.polishNeedsKeys(command))
220	            }
221	            asked.append(command)
222	        }
223	        return asked
224	    }

227	    static func polishNeedsPlace(_ command: RecordingPolish.Command) -> String {
228	        switch command {
229	        case .autoZoom:
230	            return "auto_zoom: true plans on the landed screen clips, so it needs place: true."
231	        case .shortcutOverlays:
232	            return "shortcut_overlays: true places overlays over the landed screen clips, so it "
233	                + "needs place: true."
234	        case .speedUpTyping:
235	            return "speed_up_typing: true speeds up the landed screen clips' typing, so it needs "
236	                + "place: true."
237	        }
238	    }

241	    static func polishNeedsKeys(_ command: RecordingPolish.Command) -> String {
242	        let what = command == .speedUpTyping ? "typing to speed up" : "shortcut to show"
243	        return "\(command.rawValue): true needs keys: \"shortcuts\" — without it the cursor file "
244	            + "records no \(what)."
245	    }

247	    /// SERVER THREAD. CU-101 (j): for each command the choice asks for, in order, `decide`
248	    /// polled through `onMain` every `RecordingPolish.checkInterval`, then the tool's body; its
249	    /// answer object under the command's name, or a sentence under `<name>_error`. On `.drop`,
250	    /// `.giveUp` or the call's cancel, every command not yet run gets its sentence. The cursor
251	    /// files are read here, once, for the speed-up's readiness; a read that fails counts as
252	    /// ready, so the body says why.
253	    func polishLanded(
254	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument, into fields: inout [String: Any]
255	    ) {
256	        var remaining = RecordingPolish.commands(of: result.choice)
257	        guard !remaining.isEmpty else { return }
258	        let stop = AgentLane.shared.callCancel
259	        let paths = RecordingPolish.screenPaths(of: result)
260	        let scope = onMain { document.scope }
261	        var tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor]?
262	        var started = Date()
263	        func fail(_ sentence: (RecordingPolish.Command) -> String) {
264	            for command in remaining { fields[command.rawValue + "_error"] = sentence(command) }
265	            remaining = []
266	        }
267	        while let command = remaining.first {
268	            if stop?.isCancelled == true {
269	                fail(RecordingPolish.stoppedSentence)
270	                break
271	            }
272	            if command == .speedUpTyping, tracks == nil {
273	                let files = onMain { () -> [UInt32: URL] in
274	                    let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
275	                    let clips = RecordingPolish.screenClips(paths, in: document)
276	                    return (try? AutoZoom.cursorFiles(
277	                        clips.compactMap { snapshot.clip($0) }, in: snapshot)) ?? [:]
278	                }
279	                tracks = (try? AutoZoom.readTracks(files)) ?? [:]
280	            }
281	            let held = tracks ?? [:]
282	            let step = onMain { () -> RecordingPolish.Step in
283	                let clips = RecordingPolish.screenClips(paths, in: document)
284	                let ready =
285	                    !clips.isEmpty
286	                    && RecordingPolish.isReady(
287	                        command, clips: clips, tracks: held, speedUp: SpeedUpTypingSettings(),
288	                        in: document)
289	                return RecordingPolish.decide(
290	                    command: command, clips: clips,
291	                    enhancing: RecordingEnhance.isPending(document), ready: ready,
292	                    busy: RecordingEnhance.isBusy(document, scope: scope),
293	                    elapsed: Date().timeIntervalSince(started))
294	            }
295	            switch step {
296	            case .wait:
297	                Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: RecordingPolish.checkInterval)
298	            case .drop:
299	                fail(RecordingPolish.noScreenSentence)
300	            case .giveUp:
301	                fail { RecordingPolish.notReadySentence($0, tool: true) }
302	            case .run(let ran, let clips):
303	                do {
304	                    let answer = try polish(ran, document: document, clips: clips)
305	                    fields[ran.rawValue] = Self.resultObject(answer) ?? answer
306	                } catch let error as ToolError {
307	                    fields[ran.rawValue + "_error"] = error.message
308	                } catch {
309	                    fields[ran.rawValue + "_error"] = error.localizedDescription
310	                }
311	                remaining.removeFirst()
312	                started = Date()
313	            }
314	        }
315	        onMain { RecordingPolish.forgetWait(document) }
316	    }
317	
318	    /// One command through its tool's body at the tools' defaults. SERVER THREAD.
319	    private func polish(
320	        _ command: RecordingPolish.Command, document: ProjectDocument, clips: [UInt32]
321	    ) throws -> String {
322	        switch command {
323	        case .autoZoom:
324	            return try autoZoom(document: document, clips: clips, settings: AutoZoomSettings())
325	        case .shortcutOverlays:
326	            return try addShortcutOverlays(
327	                document: document, clips: clips, settings: ShortcutOverlaySettings())
328	        case .speedUpTyping:
329	            return try speedUpTyping(
330	                document: document, clips: clips, settings: SpeedUpTypingSettings())
331	        }
332	    }

336	/// `record_screen`'s RESULT shaping and its SENTENCES — what the answer says
337	/// about the files and the ids they landed as, and what a refusal says once
338	/// a file is on disk — cut out of `AgentServer+Recording.swift` when that
339	/// file stood at 397 lines against app/CLAUDE.md's 400-line cap for a new
340	/// file, with the R1 review's fixes still to land on it. The seam is the one
341	/// the file already had: `record_screen`'s waits and its argument vocabulary
342	/// stay there; the pure functions from a `RecordingResult` (and a document,
343	/// or an error) to result fields and sentences are here. Every member is
344	/// `static` and reads nothing off the server, which is what made them the
345	/// cut: the other side keeps the semaphores and the `onMain` hops, this side
346	/// keeps what a probe could call with no server at all. `private` →
347	/// internal is the whole cost, because a `private` extension member reaches
348	/// only its own file. The SENTENCES moved on to
349	/// `AgentServer+RecordingSentences.swift` at camera-recording CR3-0.

351	/// **Road map 3, R2d — a recording is a SEQUENCE of files** (decision 6): a
352	/// `RecordingResult` carries `segments`, one per stretch between a start or
353	/// resume and a pause or the stop, and there is deliberately no
354	/// `result.micDescriptor` or `result.micOffset` any more — those are a
355	/// segment's, and this file used to read both off the result. So the answer
356	/// grew two keys that are ALWAYS present, `pauses` and `segments`, and every

390	        var media: UInt32?
391	        var clip: UInt32?
392	        var micMedia: UInt32?
393	        var micClip: UInt32?
394	        var cameraMedia: UInt32?
395	        var cameraClip: UInt32?

402	            self.clip = clip
403	            self.micMedia = micMedia

410	    /// What the files are, and — through `ids`, one entry per segment in

412	    /// top-level keys are the FIRST segment's: `path`, `width`, `height`,
413	    /// `fps`, `has_audio`, `audio_tracks` (what the MOVIE holds, 1 with

415	    /// `mic_path` and `mic_duration`, never a second track of this one),
416	    /// `mic_offset` — ALWAYS present, 0 for a segment with no microphone,
417	    /// because the key is a measurement and not a flag: `mic_path` is what

421	    /// no file holds them.
422	    /// `mic_problem` is every segment's sentence joined
423	    /// (`RecordingResult.micProblem`), present when any segment's microphone

461	        if !result.unreadable.isEmpty {
462	            fields["unreadable"] = result.unreadable.enumerated().map { i, left -> [String: Any] in

465	                    "reason": left.error.localizedDescription,

467	                if let mic = left.micDescriptor {
468	                    entry["mic_path"] = mic.path
469	                    entry["mic_duration"] = mic.duration

471	                let known = i < leftOutIds.count ? leftOutIds[i] : nil

477	        fields.merge(idFields(ids.first)) { _, new in new }

489	    /// the segment has a camera file, `camera_problem` and `camera_note`
490	    /// when set, and `camera_media` and `camera_clip` when known.
491	    static func segmentFields(
492	        _ segment: RecordingSegment, ids: RecordingSegmentIds? = nil
493	    ) -> [String: Any] {
494	        let movie = segment.descriptor

496	            "path": movie.path, "duration": movie.duration, "width": movie.width,
497	            "height": movie.height, "fps": [movie.fps.num, movie.fps.den],
498	            "started_at": startedAtFormatter.string(from: segment.startedAt),
499	            "mic_offset": segment.micOffset,

502	            fields["mic_path"] = mic.path
503	            fields["mic_duration"] = mic.duration
504	        }
505	        if let problem = segment.micProblem { fields["mic_problem"] = problem }
506	        if let camera = segment.cameraDescriptor {
507	            fields["camera_path"] = camera.path
508	            fields["camera_duration"] = camera.duration
509	            fields["camera_offset"] = segment.cameraOffset
510	        }
511	        if let problem = segment.cameraProblem { fields["camera_problem"] = problem }
512	        if let note = segment.cameraNote { fields["camera_note"] = note }
513	        if let id = ids?.cameraMedia { fields["camera_media"] = Int(id) }
514	        if let id = ids?.cameraClip { fields["camera_clip"] = Int(id) }
515	        // The segment's cursor file beside its movie (spec §11 CU-18).
516	        if let url = segment.cursorURL { fields["cursor_path"] = url.path }

518	            fields["cursor_image"] = image.rawValue

527	    /// there was no spelling to match; UTC because the file's own name
528	    /// (`RecordingFiles.stem`) is already the local-time reading of the same
529	    /// instant and a second local spelling would say nothing new, and the
530	    /// fraction because the segments' offsets are measured in milliseconds.
531	    static let startedAtFormatter: ISO8601DateFormatter = {
532	        let formatter = ISO8601DateFormatter()
533	        formatter.formatOptions = [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds]
534	        formatter.timeZone = TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0)
535	        return formatter
536	    }()

538	    private static func idFields(_ ids: RecordingSegmentIds?) -> [String: Any] {
539	        var fields: [String: Any] = [:]
540	        if let id = ids?.media { fields["media"] = Int(id) }
541	        if let id = ids?.clip { fields["clip"] = Int(id) }
542	        if let id = ids?.micMedia { fields["mic_media"] = Int(id) }
543	        if let id = ids?.micClip { fields["mic_clip"] = Int(id) }
544	        return fields
545	    }

547	    static func stopReasonName(_ reason: StopReason) -> String {
548	        switch reason {
549	        case .stopped: return "stopped"
550	        case .userStopped: return "user_stopped"
551	        case .systemStopped: return "system_stopped"
552	        }
553	    }
554	
555	    /// The `note` clause for a result some segment's microphone did not
556	    /// land for — the pictures are in the project and the answer must say
557	    /// what is missing. Over the JOINED problems, whose sentences name the
558	    /// segment's file when one was left behind. A voice-over has no picture:
559	    /// its problem — a microphone that stopped on its own — is said verbatim.
560	    static func microphoneNote(_ result: RecordingResult) -> String? {
561	        if result.isVoiceOver { return result.micProblem }
562	        return result.micProblem.map {
563	            "The picture landed without its microphone — the microphone file could not be "
564	                + "used: " + $0
565	        }
566	    }
