568	    /// The result's own `note` clauses, in order: the segments left out as
569	    /// unreadable (#97), the left-out voices that landed (#181 item 2), the
570	    /// microphone's, then a camera's `problem` and `note`, verbatim (CAM-4),
571	    /// then every segment's camera sentences beside the screen
572	    /// (`cameraSegmentsNote`, CAM-10 (6)). Both doors append these after their
573	    /// own, on a landing that succeeded only.
574	    static func resultNotes(_ result: RecordingResult) -> [String] {
575	        [
576	            result.unreadableNote, result.leftOutVoiceNote, microphoneNote(result),
577	            result.camera?.problem, result.camera?.note,
578	            result.cameraSegmentsNote,
579	            // Every segment's cursor problem (spec §11 CU-18), last.
580	            result.cursorSegmentsNote,
581	        ].compactMap { $0 }
582	    }
583	
584	    /// The ids a new project holds for every segment's files, read off its
585	    /// snapshot by path, SEGMENT BY SEGMENT — `untitled(around:)` placed
586	    /// them (the first picture as the document, the rest through
587	    /// `remainderPlacement`), so nothing here predicted an id, and a file
588	    /// the remainder landed as media alone (its sentence in the landing's
589	    /// `notes`) answers a `media` and no `clip`, which is the truth. A new
590	    /// project has no nest, so its top-level clips are the only clips there
591	    /// are.
592	    static func newProjectIds(
593	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument
594	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
595	        let snapshot = document.project.snapshot
596	        return result.segments.map { segment in
597	            let media = landedMedia(for: segment.descriptor.path, in: snapshot)
598	            let micMedia = segment.micDescriptor.flatMap { landedMedia(for: $0.path, in: snapshot) }
599	            let cameraMedia = segment.cameraDescriptor.flatMap {
600	                landedMedia(for: $0.path, in: snapshot)
601	            }
602	            return RecordingSegmentIds(
603	                media: media, clip: media.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) },
604	                micMedia: micMedia, micClip: micMedia.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) },
605	                cameraMedia: cameraMedia,
606	                cameraClip: cameraMedia.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) })
607	        }
608	    }
609	
610	    /// The ids a DOCUMENT landing gives every segment — the placement's own
611	    /// four lists, the ids it predicted off the purely-applied trial (R1's
612	    /// contract: `next_id` before each op that mints) and the ones the panel
613	    /// selects, so the tool reports what the panel highlights. All four
614	    /// lists have ONE entry per segment, in order, nil where nothing was
615	    /// minted (`Placement`'s doc), so every one is indexed by SEGMENT and
616	    /// none is consumed by an iterator — the first shape here walked the two
617	    /// `mic…` lists as "segments with a microphone file" were met, and a
618	    /// voice that minted no clip then shifted every later segment's ids by
619	    /// one. Read BEFORE the commit, as R1 read the singulars, which is what
620	    /// lets `land()` keep `editResult`'s tail.
621	    static func documentIds(
622	        _ result: RecordingResult, placement: RecordingLanding.Placement
623	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
624	        func entry(_ list: [UInt32?], _ k: Int) -> UInt32? { k < list.count ? list[k] : nil }
625	        return result.segments.indices.map { k in
626	            RecordingSegmentIds(
627	                media: k < placement.mediaIds.count ? placement.mediaIds[k] : nil,
628	                clip: entry(placement.clipIds, k), micMedia: entry(placement.micMediaIds, k),
629	                micClip: entry(placement.micClipIds, k),
630	                cameraMedia: entry(placement.cameraMediaIds, k),
631	                cameraClip: entry(placement.cameraClipIds, k))
632	        }
633	    }
634	
635	    /// The ids a DOCUMENT landing gives each left-out segment's voice (#181
636	    /// item 2): the placement's two left-out lists, one entry per
637	    /// `result.unreadable`, `micMedia` and `micClip` only.
638	    static func documentLeftOutIds(
639	        _ result: RecordingResult, placement: RecordingLanding.Placement
640	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
641	        func entry(_ list: [UInt32?], _ i: Int) -> UInt32? { i < list.count ? list[i] : nil }
642	        return result.unreadable.indices.map { i in
643	            RecordingSegmentIds(
644	                micMedia: entry(placement.leftOutMicMediaIds, i),
645	                micClip: entry(placement.leftOutMicClipIds, i))
646	        }
647	    }
648	
649	    /// The ids a NEW project holds for each left-out segment's voice, read
650	    /// off its snapshot by trimmed path as `newProjectIds` reads the
651	    /// segments': a voice before the first segment is media with no clip.
652	    static func newProjectLeftOutIds(
653	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument
654	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
655	        let snapshot = document.project.snapshot
656	        return result.unreadable.map { left in
657	            let micMedia = left.micDescriptor.flatMap { landedMedia(for: $0.path, in: snapshot) }
658	            return RecordingSegmentIds(
659	                micMedia: micMedia, micClip: micMedia.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) })
660	        }
661	    }
662	
663	    /// The media entry for `path`, matched TRIMMED because that is what the
664	    /// core stored (`RecordingLanding.addMedia`'s rule).
665	    private static func landedMedia(for path: String, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> UInt32? {
666	        let trimmed = path.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
667	        return snapshot.media.first(where: { $0.path == trimmed })?.id
668	    }
669	
670	    /// The first top-level clip whose source is `media`.
671	    private static func landedClip(of media: UInt32, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> UInt32? {
672	        snapshot.clips.first { clip in
673	            if case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source { return id == media }
674	            return false
675	        }?.id
676	    }
677	}

680	/// `record_screen`'s SENTENCES (camera-recording CR3-0): an error's sentence,
681	/// the start's and the finish's timeout sentences with the alert clause they
682	/// share, and `savedButNotAdded`, a failure after the files are on disk. A
683	/// pure move out of `AgentServer+RecordingResult.swift` at the 400-line cap,
684	/// landed alone before camera + screen grows the result; nothing changed,
685	/// and `isStartTimeout` stays `private`, because only `startSentence` calls
686	/// it. Every member is `static` and reads nothing off the server, the rule
687	/// the result file was cut by.
688	extension AgentServer {
689	    // MARK: - The sentences
690	
691	    /// An error's sentence — a `ToolError`'s `localizedDescription` is generic.
692	    static func sentence(of error: any Error) -> String {
693	        (error as? ToolError)?.message ?? error.localizedDescription
694	    }
695	
696	    /// The clause both of the tool's timeout sentences end with, and the
697	    /// recorder's own arm timeout gets it too: macOS 15 periodically puts up
698	    /// a consent alert — whether to keep letting Frame Job bypass the system
699	    /// window picker — which is a prompt neither `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess`
700	    /// (still true) nor this tool can see, and a capture waiting behind it
701	    /// looks exactly like a recorder that hung.
702	    static let recordingAlertClause =
703	        " A system alert about screen recording may be waiting on the screen — macOS "
704	        + "periodically asks whether to keep allowing Frame Job to record, and neither the "
705	        + "preflight nor this tool can see that prompt; answer it and call again."
706	
707	    /// The start's failure as the caller reads it: the recorder's sentence,
708	    /// plus the alert clause when the recorder's own arm ceiling is what
709	    /// answered (`.startTimedOut`, bare or wrapped in `.filesKept`).
710	    static func startSentence(of error: any Error) -> String {
711	        sentence(of: error) + (isStartTimeout(error) ? recordingAlertClause : "")
712	    }
713	
714	    private static func isStartTimeout(_ error: any Error) -> Bool {
715	        guard let failure = error as? RecorderError else { return false }
716	        switch failure {
717	        case .startTimedOut: return true
718	        case .filesKept(let inner, _, _): return isStartTimeout(inner)
719	        default: return false
720	        }
721	    }
722	
723	    /// The sentence for a `stop()` that did not conclude within
724	    /// `stopCeiling(segments:camera:)`: it names every movie the recorder still
725	    /// holds — one per segment, the recording may finish on its own after
726	    /// the tool has answered, and a person can then import them — and the
727	    /// alert clause. Empty means the recorder no longer holds a session at
728	    /// all. The seconds it spells are the ceiling over `movies.count`, which
729	    /// is the number the wait used: the same count while the session is
730	    /// held (a stop removes no segment), and the one-segment number — the
731	    /// wait's own `?? 1` — when the recorder had let the session go. A
732	    /// voice-over's files are named "file", not "movie". `cameras` are the
733	    /// camera files beside a screen's movies (spec §11 CAM-10 (7)), named
734	    /// after them. `camera` is the wait's own `cameraBeside`, so the ceiling
735	    /// spelled is the one the wait used — with the camera's probe whenever a
736	    /// camera was asked for beside the screen, even when no camera file is
737	    /// held (CAM-11 (7)).
738	    static func finishTimeoutSentence(
739	        movies: [String], cameras: [String] = [], camera: Bool = false, voiceOver: Bool = false
740	    ) -> String {
741	        let noun = voiceOver ? "file" : "movie"
742	        let where_: String
743	        switch movies.count {
744	        case 0:
745	            where_ =
746	                "The recorder no longer holds the session, so the recording may already have "
747	                + "finished without answering."
748	        case 1:
749	            where_ = "The recording may still finish on its own; its \(noun) is at \(movies[0])."
750	        default:
751	            where_ =
752	                "The recording may still finish on its own; its \(noun)s are at "
753	                + movies.joined(separator: ", ") + "."
754	        }
755	        let besideClause: String
756	        switch cameras.count {
757	        case 0: besideClause = ""
758	        case 1: besideClause = " Its camera file is at \(cameras[0])."
759	        default: besideClause = " Its camera files are at " + cameras.joined(separator: ", ") + "."
760	        }
761	        let ceiling = stopCeiling(segments: movies.count, camera: camera)
762	        return "record_screen asked the recorder to stop and it did not finish within "
763	            + "\(Int(ceiling)) s. " + where_ + besideClause + recordingAlertClause
764	    }
765	
766	    /// A failure AFTER the recording landed on disk, as a `ToolError` naming
767	    /// the file(s): the placement's trial, the commit and the untitled
768	    /// document are the three throw sites, and every one of them is reached
769	    /// with the footage already written. The files are
770	    /// `RecordingResult.filesClause` — every segment's movie comma-joined,
771	    /// then every microphone file that landed — the one spelling the panel's
772	    /// note uses too; with one segment the sentence is byte for byte R1's,
773	    /// which `tools/proof/recording_proof.py` matches by shape. A segment
774	    /// left out as unreadable (#97) is named after it, its files too.
775	    static func savedButNotAdded(_ result: RecordingResult, _ error: any Error) -> ToolError {
776	        ToolError(
777	            message: "The recording was saved at \(result.filesClause) but could not "
778	                + "be added: " + sentence(of: error)
779	                + (result.unreadableNote.map { " " + $0 } ?? ""))
780	    }
781	}

784	/// `record_screen`'s LANDING (camera-recording CR3-0): `awaitGestureEnd`, the
785	/// wait for a target document's drag to end, and `land`, the two doors a
786	/// finished recording takes — a document through `editResult`, a new project
787	/// through `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`. A pure move out of
788	/// `AgentServer+Recording.swift` at the 400-line cap, landed alone before
789	/// camera + screen grows the tool; nothing in either body changed, and
790	/// `private` → internal is the whole cost, because a `private` extension
791	/// member reaches only its own file. What the answer and its refusals say is
792	/// `AgentServer+RecordingResult.swift` and `+RecordingSentences.swift`.
793	extension AgentServer {
794	    // MARK: - The landing
795	
796	    /// SERVER THREAD. A target document mid-drag is not committed over the
797	    /// gesture's base handle (`RecordingLanding.placement` refuses by name);
798	    /// the panel retries from a half-second timer bounded at forty tries,
799	    /// and this polls `isLiveEditing` through `onMain` at that interval and
800	    /// bound BY NAME, so the two doors cannot drift. A gesture outlasting
801	    /// the bound still reaches `placement`'s refusal, which names the file;
802	    /// a `.newProject` target or a closed document has nothing to wait for.
803	    func awaitGestureEnd(_ destination: RecordingDestination) {
804	        for _ in 0..<RecorderPanelController.landingRetryLimit {
805	            let dragging = onMain { () -> Bool in
806	                guard case .document(let document) = RecordingLanding.resolve(destination)
807	                else { return false }
808	                return document.isLiveEditing
809	            }
810	            guard dragging else { return }
811	            Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: RecorderPanelController.landingRetryInterval)
812	        }
813	    }
814	
815	    /// MAIN. The two doors: a document through `editResult` (one undo step,
816	    /// the `created` ids, the scope landing); a new project through
817	    /// `ProjectDocument.untitled(around:)`, which does everything. Every
818	    /// throw past this point is `savedButNotAdded`'s: every segment's files
819	    /// exist. The result is `recordingFields` over the segments plus the ids
820	    /// each door knows them by (the placement's lists, predicted before the
821	    /// commit; the new project's snapshot, read by path), and `note` is the
822	    /// door's sentences in order: `place: false`, a closed target, what the
823	    /// landing could NOT place (each naming its file), then `resultNotes(result)`.
824	    /// Answers the document it landed in beside the answer, for
825	    /// `landAndEnhance`.
826	    func land(_ result: RecordingResult, place: Bool) throws
827	        -> (answer: String, document: ProjectDocument)
828	    {
829	        var fields: [String: Any]
830	        var notes: [String] = []
831	        switch RecordingLanding.resolve(result.choice.destination) {
832	        case .document(let document):
833	            let placement: RecordingLanding.Placement
834	            do {
835	                placement = try RecordingLanding.placement(result, in: document, place: place)
836	            } catch {
837	                throw Self.savedButNotAdded(result, error)
838	            }
839	            fields = Self.recordingFields(
840	                result, ids: Self.documentIds(result, placement: placement),
841	                leftOutIds: Self.documentLeftOutIds(result, placement: placement))
842	            fields["landed"] = "document"
843	            if !place {
844	                notes.append(
845	                    "The recording is in the project's media list but not on the timeline — "
846	                        + "place it with add_clip {track, media, at}.")
847	            }
848	            notes.append(contentsOf: placement.notes)
849	            notes.append(contentsOf: Self.resultNotes(result))
850	            if !notes.isEmpty { fields["note"] = notes.joined(separator: " ") }
851	            let answer: String
852	            do {
853	                answer = try editResult(document, RecordingLanding.actionName, placement.ops, fields)
854	            } catch {
855	                throw Self.savedButNotAdded(result, error)
856	            }
857	            // `editResult` commits and does not build caches; `importMedia`
858	            // calls this after its own commit for the same reason.
859	            document.generateCaches()
860	            return (answer, document)
861	        case .newProject:
862	            let document: ProjectDocument
863	            var landingNotes: [String] = []
864	            do {
865	                let landing = try ProjectDocument.untitled(around: result)
866	                document = landing.document
867	                landingNotes = landing.notes
868	            } catch {
869	                throw Self.savedButNotAdded(result, error)
870	            }
871	            fields = Self.recordingFields(
872	                result, ids: Self.newProjectIds(result, in: document),
873	                leftOutIds: Self.newProjectLeftOutIds(result, in: document))
874	            fields["landed"] = "new_project"
875	            if result.choice.destination != .newProject {
876	                notes.append(
877	                    "The target document closed while the recording ran, so it opened as a "
878	                        + "new project instead.")
879	            }
880	            if !place {
881	                notes.append(
882	                    "place: false has no meaning for a new project — the "
883	                        + (result.isVoiceOver ? "voice-over" : "picture") + " IS the "
884	                        + "document, so its clips are on the timeline, one per segment and "
885	                        + "the first at 0.")
886	            }
887	            notes.append(contentsOf: landingNotes)
888	            notes.append(contentsOf: Self.resultNotes(result))
889	            if !notes.isEmpty { fields["note"] = notes.joined(separator: " ") }
890	            fields["ok"] = true
891	            fields["project"] = summary(document)
892	            return (try jsonResult(fields), document)
893	        }
894	    }
895	
896	    /// SERVER THREAD. `land` on main, and in the same hop, when the choice
897	    /// asks for it, Remove Background over the camera clips as its own step
898	    /// (road map creator-jobs CO8, spec §11 CO-81, `camera_cutout` or
899	    /// `camera_cutout_error`); then, when the choice asks for it,
900	    /// Enhance Voice over the recording's voice clips as its own step (spec
901	    /// §11 AU-68 (f)): `decide` polled through `onMain` every
902	    /// `RecordingEnhance.checkInterval`, then `enhance_voice`'s own body at
903	    /// its default target (a tool reads no `UserDefaults`); then, when it asks
904	    /// for any, the polish on landing (road map creator-jobs CU10, spec §11
905	    /// CU-101 (j), `polishLanded`). The answer is `land`'s with `enhance`
906	    /// (that body's answer) or `enhance_error`, the polish's answers or
907	    /// `…_error` sentences, and `project` read again, last, when any ran.
908	    func landAndEnhance(_ result: RecordingResult, place: Bool) throws -> String {
909	        let stop = AgentLane.shared.callCancel
910	        let (answer, document, cutout) = try onMain {
911	            () throws -> (String, ProjectDocument, [UInt32]) in
912	            let (answer, document) = try self.land(result, place: place)
913	            // CO-81: Remove Background, its own step, before Enhance Voice and the polish.
914	            return (answer, document, RecordingCutout.apply(result, in: document))
915	        }
916	        let polish = !RecordingPolish.commands(of: result.choice).isEmpty
917	        let wantsCutout = result.choice.cameraCutout
918	        guard result.choice.enhanceMicrophone || polish || wantsCutout else { return answer }
919	        var fields = Self.resultObject(answer) ?? [:]
920	        if wantsCutout {
921	            if cutout.isEmpty {
922	                fields["camera_cutout_error"] = RecordingCutout.noCameraSentence
923	            } else {
924	                fields["camera_cutout"] = ["clips": cutout]
925	            }
926	        }
927	        if result.choice.enhanceMicrophone {
928	            try enhanceLanded(result, in: document, stop: stop, into: &fields)
929	        }
930	        if polish { polishLanded(result, in: document, into: &fields) }
931	        fields["project"] = onMain { self.summary(document) }
932	        return try jsonResult(fields)
933	    }
934	
935	    /// SERVER THREAD. AU-68 (f)'s wait and Enhance Voice, its answer or
936	    /// `enhance_error` written into `fields`.
937	    private func enhanceLanded(
938	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument, stop: AgentCallCancel?,
939	        into fields: inout [String: Any]
940	    ) throws {
941	        let (clips, scope) = onMain {
942	            (RecordingEnhance.voiceClips(of: result, in: document), document.scope)
943	        }
944	        let started = Date()
945	        var step = RecordingEnhance.Step.wait
946	        while step == .wait, stop?.isCancelled != true {
947	            step = onMain { () -> RecordingEnhance.Step in
948	                let present = RecordingEnhance.present(clips, in: document)
949	                return RecordingEnhance.decide(
950	                    clips: present, analysed: RecordingEnhance.isAnalysed(present, in: document),
951	                    busy: RecordingEnhance.isBusy(document, scope: scope),
952	                    elapsed: Date().timeIntervalSince(started))
953	            }
954	            if step == .wait { Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: RecordingEnhance.checkInterval) }
955	        }
956	        switch step {
957	        case .enhance(let ids):
958	            do {
959	                let enhanced = try enhanceVoice(
960	                    document: document, clips: ids, targetLUFS: AudioNormalize.defaultTargetLUFS)
961	                fields["enhance"] = Self.resultObject(enhanced) ?? enhanced
962	            } catch let error as ToolError {
963	                fields["enhance_error"] = error.message
964	            }
965	        case .drop:
966	            fields["enhance_error"] = RecordingEnhance.noVoiceSentence
967	        case .giveUp:
968	            fields["enhance_error"] = RecordingEnhance.notReadyToolSentence
969	        case .wait:
970	            fields["enhance_error"] =
971	                "record_screen was stopped while the microphone's sound was being analysed, so "
972	                + "Enhance Voice did not run."
973	        }
974	    }
975	
976	    /// The object a `jsonResult` envelope's text holds, nil for anything else.
977	    static func resultObject(_ envelope: String) -> [String: Any]? {
978	        guard
979	            let call = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(envelope.utf8)))
980	                as? [String: Any],
981	            let content = call["content"] as? [[String: Any]],
982	            let text = content.first?["text"] as? String
983	        else { return nil }
984	        return (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: Data(text.utf8))) as? [String: Any]
985	    }
986	}

21	/// which calls them for the panel's own recording (#98). The panel's
22	/// phase — `.recording ⇄ .paused` — follows the recorder's own `pause()` /
23	/// `resume()` (`ScreenRecorder+Pause.swift`), which are synchronous and
24	/// throw. The phase moves only AFTER the call returns
25	/// without throwing, so the panel never claims a state the recorder
26	/// refused: a pause that could not close the segment's file leaves the
27	/// recorder `.recording` and the panel with it, and a resume whose output
28	/// could not be added leaves both `.paused`.
29	///
30	/// **The two refusals are answered differently, on purpose.** A refused
31	/// pause BEEPS: the recorder is still recording, nothing was lost, and the
32	/// panel is hidden, so a note there would be read by nobody until the
33	/// landing, by which time it would be stale. A refused resume keeps the
34	/// recorder's sentence as `resumeProblem` and stays paused: the stream still
35	/// captures but no file is taking it, so what the person does next — try
36	/// again, or stop and land what was recorded — depends on the sentence, and
37	/// the landing's reveal (`revealIfNoted`, `+Landing.swift`) brings the
38	/// panel back with that sentence in its note when they stop. The sentence
39	/// is STATE and never text read back off the label (R2 review): the live
40	/// note is rebuilt from `[microphoneProblem, resumeProblem]` at every tick
41	/// (`syncMicrophoneNote`, over `liveNote` below), so a microphone
42	/// did-finish landing late cannot wipe it and a retried resume replaces it
43	/// rather than appending a second copy; and `landingNote` takes it as an
44	/// argument, so the landing's note carries it where the first shape — each
45	/// end replacing the label whole — dropped it, and the reveal showed
46	/// nothing. A resume that LANDS clears it: a sentence about a refusal the
47	/// person has since got past would bring the panel back with nothing true
48	/// to say.
49	///
50	/// A Stop while paused (`stopRecording`, `record(_:)`, File ▸ Stop
51	/// Recording) goes to `recorder.stop()` exactly as one while recording
52	/// does — the recorder's `.paused` arm takes the same finishing path with
53	/// the segment's output already closed — and the status item comes down at
54	/// `recordingEnded` as ever. The tick runs through `.paused` (`armTick`):
55	/// the meter poll is a no-op there, the recorder having silenced the bar at
56	/// the pause, and `elapsed` is frozen, so the footnote and the item hold
57	/// still on their own.
58	extension RecorderPanelController {
59	    // MARK: - Pause and resume
60	
61	    /// The status item's Pause Recording, and File ▸ Pause Recording's for
62	    /// the panel's own recording. `.recording` → `.paused`; any
63	    /// other phase beeps — the row was clicked in the moment between a Stop
64	    /// and the item coming down — and so does any throw, `.alreadyPaused`
65	    /// among them (the header).
66	    func pauseRecording() {
67	        guard phase == .recording else {
68	            NSSound.beep()
69	            return
70	        }
71	        do {
72	            try recorder.pause()
73	            phase = .paused
74	        } catch {
75	            NSSound.beep()
76	        }
77	    }
78	
79	    /// The status item's Resume Recording, and File ▸ Resume Recording's.
80	    /// `.paused` → `.recording`, with
81	    /// the refused-resume sentence cleared; any other phase beeps. A throw
82	    /// leaves the phase paused and keeps the recorder's sentence as
83	    /// `resumeProblem`, REPLACING an earlier one, redrawn into the note at
84	    /// once rather than at the tick's next turn (the header).
85	    func resumeRecording() {
86	        guard phase == .paused else {
87	            NSSound.beep()
88	            return
89	        }
90	        do {
91	            try recorder.resume()
92	            resumeProblem = nil
93	            phase = .recording
94	        } catch {
95	            resumeProblem = error.localizedDescription
96	            syncMicrophoneNote()
97	        }
98	    }
99	
100	    /// The live note's two parts, in order: the microphone's sentence, with
101	    /// the fact that the picture is still recording (a silent meter alone
102	    /// reads as a broken recording), then a refused resume's; empty with
103	    /// neither. Pure, so a probe can pin the composition without a recorder.
104	    static func liveNote(microphoneProblem: String?, resumeProblem: String?) -> String {
105	        var sentences: [String] = []
106	        if let microphoneProblem {
107	            sentences.append(
108	                "The microphone stopped: \(microphoneProblem) The picture is still recording.")
109	        }
110	        if let resumeProblem { sentences.append(resumeProblem) }
111	        return sentences.joined(separator: " ")
112	    }

114	    // MARK: - The hidden recording's one door
115	
116	    /// The quit guard's call (`AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate`).
117	    /// While this panel is hidden for its recording `show()` can only beep,
118	    /// and a beep tells a person who paused and forgot nothing — so the
119	    /// status item's menu is opened instead, Pause or Resume and Stop put
120	    /// in front of them (`RecorderStatusItem.openMenu`); the beep is kept
121	    /// for the one case with no item to open. Any other recording — a
122	    /// tool's, which File ▸ Stop Recording ends — shows the panel as before.
123	    func revealControls() {
124	        guard hiddenForRecording else {
125	            show()
126	            return
127	        }
128	        if statusItem?.openMenu() != true { NSSound.beep() }
129	    }

131	    // MARK: - The phases, drawn
132	
133	    /// Draws the phase: the button's title and enabled state, the controls
134	    /// locked while anything is in flight, the countdown numeral, the
135	    /// footnote, the camera preview (CAM-7), and the window refitted to
136	    /// whatever appeared or went.
137	    func syncPhase() {
138	        syncControlsEnabled()
139	        syncPauseButton()
140	        var countdown: String?
141	        switch phase {
142	        case .idle:
143	            recordButton.title = "Record"
144	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
145	        case .countdown(let remaining):
146	            recordButton.title = "Cancel"
147	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
148	            countdown = "\(remaining)"
149	        case .starting:
150	            recordButton.title = "Starting…"
151	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
152	        case .recording, .paused:
153	            recordButton.title = "Stop"
154	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
155	        case .stopping:
156	            recordButton.title = "Stopping…"
157	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
158	        case .landing:
159	            recordButton.title = "Adding…"
160	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
161	        }
162	        recordButton.invalidateIntrinsicContentSize()
163	        countdownLabel.stringValue = countdown ?? ""
164	        countdownLabel.isHidden = countdown == nil
165	        refreshStatusLabel()
166	        syncCameraPreview()
167	        fitWindowToContent()

169	
170	    /// The footnote: the folder while idle, the coral dot and the elapsed
171	    /// time while recording, the pause glyph and the frozen time while
172	    /// paused — faint, because the dot's colour means "capturing" — and
173	    /// through `.stopping` whichever of those two it last showed, left
174	    /// UNTOUCHED (R2 review): the phase no longer says whether the Stop
175	    /// came from paused, `elapsed` is frozen at the stop call, and
176	    /// redrawing the arm as recording brought the coral dot back over a
177	    /// finish that captures nothing. The status item keeps its mark the
178	    /// same way (`RecorderStatusItem.freeze`, called by `stopRecording`).
179	    func refreshStatusLabel() {
180	        switch phase {
181	        case .recording:
182	            statusLabel.stringValue = "● " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)
183	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.meterClip
184	        case .paused:
185	            statusLabel.stringValue =
186	                RecorderStatusItem.pauseGlyph + " " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)
187	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
188	        case .stopping:
189	            break
190	        default:
191	            statusLabel.stringValue =
192	                "saved in " + (RecordingFiles.folder().path as NSString).abbreviatingWithTildeInPath
193	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
194	        }
195	    }

200	/// rows current while it is up, `setNote` and the refit that keeps the card on
201	/// its screen — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s ninth file. A pure move out
202	/// of the base file, which stood at 399 lines against the 400-line cap a
203	/// Camera source would have grown: camera recording's CR1-0, paid first and
204	/// alone. Its `// MARK: - Showing` came here whole, bodies untouched;
205	/// `armSyncTimer` stays private, since its one caller, `show()`, moved with it.

211	    /// type doc): the welcome window's button is the caller that would
212	    /// otherwise un-hide it into the recording. Shown while idle, a prepared
213	    /// capture that failed (or a build that threw) is let go first, so the
214	    /// preview's sync tries again (spec §11 CAM-7 (5)). The device observers
215	    /// are added before that sync, which applies a change made while the
216	    /// panel was closed (CAM-8 (1)).
217	    func show() {
218	        guard !hiddenForRecording else {
219	            NSSound.beep()
220	            return
221	        }
222	        panelClosing = false
223	        if phase == .idle {
224	            rebuildSources()
225	            rebuildMicrophones()
226	            rebuildCameras()
227	            restoreChoices()
228	            if recorder.state == .idle, previewFailure != nil { recorder.discardPreparedCamera() }
229	        }
230	        rebuildDestinations()
231	        refreshSizeNote()
232	        fitWindowToContent()
233	        floatAgain()
234	        if NSApp.isActive {
235	            showWindow(nil)

238	            window?.orderFrontRegardless()

241	        observeDevices()

245	    /// One second, while the panel is up: the Record Into rows follow the
246	    /// documents that open and close and the one in front — while idle,
247	    /// which `rebuildDestinations` itself decides — and the camera preview
248	    /// steps again (CAM-7 (5)).
249	    private func armSyncTimer() {
250	        guard syncTimer == nil else { return }
251	        syncTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { [weak self] timer in
252	            guard let self else {
253	                timer.invalidate()
254	                return

262	    // `syncPhase()` and `refreshStatusLabel()` — the phases drawn — are
263	    // `+Pause.swift`'s since the R2 review, the base file's toll.
264	
265	    func setNote(_ text: String) {
266	        noteLabel.stringValue = text
267	        noteLabel.isHidden = text.isEmpty
268	        fitWindowToContent()
269	    }

271	    /// The window takes the card's fitting size, keeping its TOP-LEFT where
272	    /// it was — `setContentSize` would keep the bottom-left and walk the
273	    /// title bar up the screen every time the note appeared — and then
274	    /// CONSTRAINED to its screen (`window.screen`, else the main one), so a
275	    /// panel whose bottom edge sits near the Dock is pushed up when the
276	    /// countdown grows it rather than growing under the Dock (R1 review;
277	    /// measured, the numeral adds 88 pt below the rows and a note 42 more).
278	    /// `setFrame` itself constrains nothing — a window can be put anywhere
279	    /// programmatically, on screen or off — which is why the call is
280	    /// explicit.
281	    func fitWindowToContent() {
282	        guard let window else { return }
283	        card.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
284	        let content = NSRect(origin: .zero, size: card.fittingSize)
285	        var frame = window.frameRect(forContentRect: content)
286	        let current = window.frame
287	        frame.origin = NSPoint(x: current.minX, y: current.maxY - frame.height)
288	        let screen = window.screen ?? NSScreen.main ?? NSScreen.screens.first
289	        frame = window.constrainFrameRect(frame, to: screen)
290	        window.setFrame(frame, display: window.isVisible)
291	    }

296	/// The calls a press of Record makes about the four grants, as values a
297	/// probe can replace: the reads, the four system prompts, the two remembered
298	/// "asked" flags and the one opener of System Settings. `live` is the app's;
299	/// `tools/proof/recording_probe.py` puts a sealed spy in
300	/// `RecorderPanelController.grantDoors` before any mode runs, so no probe
301	/// can prompt, open Settings or touch the key. Input Monitoring's four
302	/// (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-62) come last and default INERT —
303	/// never granted, never asking, never remembering — so a probe that fills
304	/// only the first ten compiles unchanged and can never prompt.
305	struct RecorderGrantDoors {
306	    /// Whether the panel has put up the Screen Recording prompt once
307	    /// (spec §11 recording). Written only by a launchd-owned press.
308	    static let screenRecordingAskedKey = "FrameJobScreenRecordingAsked"
309	    /// Whether the panel has asked for Input Monitoring once (spec §11 CU-3,
310	    /// CU-62). Written only by a launchd-owned press.
311	    static let inputMonitoringAskedKey = "FrameJobInputMonitoringAsked"
312	
313	    var screenGranted: () -> Bool
314	    var launchedByLaunchd: () -> Bool
315	    var requestScreen: () -> Void
316	    var screenAsked: () -> Bool
317	    var rememberScreenAsked: () -> Void
318	    var microphoneStatus: () -> AVAuthorizationStatus
319	    var requestMicrophone: (@escaping () -> Void) -> Void
320	    var openSettings: (URL) -> Bool
321	    /// The Camera grant (CR1c, spec §11 CAM-5), asked only for Source Camera.
322	    var cameraStatus: () -> AVAuthorizationStatus
323	    var requestCamera: (@escaping () -> Void) -> Void
324	    /// Input Monitoring (CU-62), read only with Record shortcuts on.
325	    var inputMonitoringGranted: () -> Bool = { false }
326	    var requestInputMonitoring: () -> Void = {}
327	    var inputMonitoringAsked: () -> Bool = { false }
328	    var rememberInputMonitoringAsked: () -> Void = {}
329	
330	    static var live: RecorderGrantDoors {
331	        RecorderGrantDoors(
332	            screenGranted: { RecordingGrant.screenRecordingGranted },
333	            launchedByLaunchd: { RecordingGrant.launchedByLaunchd },
334	            requestScreen: { _ = CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess() },
335	            screenAsked: { UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: screenRecordingAskedKey) },
336	            rememberScreenAsked: { UserDefaults.standard.set(true, forKey: screenRecordingAskedKey) },
337	            microphoneStatus: { RecordingGrant.microphoneStatus },
338	            requestMicrophone: { answered in
339	                // The framework does not say which queue it answers on, so
340	                // the answer hops to main.
341	                AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess(for: .audio) { _ in
342	                    DispatchQueue.main.async { answered() }
343	                }
344	            },
345	            openSettings: { url in NSWorkspace.shared.open(url) },
346	            cameraStatus: { RecordingGrant.cameraStatus },
347	            requestCamera: { answered in
348	                // As the microphone's: the answer hops to main.
349	                AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess(for: .video) { _ in
350	                    DispatchQueue.main.async { answered() }
351	                }
352	            },
353	            inputMonitoringGranted: { RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringGranted },
354	            requestInputMonitoring: { _ = CGRequestListenEventAccess() },
355	            inputMonitoringAsked: { UserDefaults.standard.bool(forKey: inputMonitoringAskedKey) },
356	            rememberInputMonitoringAsked: {
357	                UserDefaults.standard.set(true, forKey: inputMonitoringAskedKey)
358	            })
359	    }

362	/// The grants, for the recorder panel (road map 3, R1c; spec §11
363	/// recording) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s seventh file, cut out of
364	/// `+Recording.swift` when the press learned to open System Settings.
365	///
366	/// **The grants are asked for HERE and nowhere else, and UNCONDITIONALLY**
367	/// (decision 4: the TOOL never asks — it reads the status and refuses by
368	/// name — because a system prompt needs a person in front of it; the panel
369	/// asks, because a press of Record IS that person, exactly as the transcribe
370	/// sheet's Start is). **This is also the only place System Settings is
371	/// opened for them**, and the tool never opens it. Screen Recording is
372	/// asked with `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` on the FIRST press that finds
373	/// it absent — the system prompt appears once per app, not per launch — and
374	/// the ask is remembered in `FrameJobScreenRecordingAsked`; every later press
375	/// opens the Screen & System Audio Recording pane and the note says so.
376	/// `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` returns false at once on a first ask, so
377	/// the refusal sentence is shown either way and the person presses Record
378	/// again once the grant is on. The flag is read and written only in a
379	/// launchd-owned launch: a shell-launched press always asks and never
380	/// remembers, because TCC attributes that prompt to the terminal (R0 q1).
381	/// The microphone is asked only when one is chosen, from `.notDetermined`,
382	/// and the countdown starts from the answer; `.denied` and `.restricted`
383	/// open the Microphone pane and stop there, and a prompt's answer never
384	/// opens it. Both readings happen BEFORE the countdown, so a countdown never
385	/// ends in a prompt. An earlier draft gated both asks on a `canAsk` (since
386	/// deleted with the speech grant) — false for a scripted agent launch —
387	/// and the R1 review measured what that cost: under that flag the refusal
388	/// note told the person to press the button they had just pressed, and a
389	/// `notDetermined` microphone could never be granted from anywhere.
390	/// `canAsk` is the tool's rule about a prompt nobody would see; it does not
391	/// apply to a button somebody clicked. **The Camera grant** (CR1c, spec §11
392	/// CAM-5) is the third, read only for Source Camera, whose press never reads
393	/// Screen Recording: the microphone's steps, through its own pane
394	/// (`Privacy_Camera`), and its prompt's answer RE-READS the grant before the
395	/// microphone and the countdown, so a refused prompt stops there. **Input
396	/// Monitoring** (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-3, CU-62) is the
397	/// fourth, read only when Record shortcuts is on with a screen source, after
398	/// Screen Recording and before the Camera and the Microphone. Its step is
399	/// Screen Recording's table, remembered in `FrameJobInputMonitoringAsked`;
400	/// because no prompt shows and Frame Job is not listed until a person adds
401	/// it (CU0b), an ask ALSO opens the Input Monitoring pane, and the note says
402	/// to add Frame Job with + (`inputMonitoringNote(opened:)`).
403	extension RecorderPanelController {
404	    /// The doors every grant call goes through; a probe replaces it.
405	    static var grantDoors = RecorderGrantDoors.live
406	
407	    /// A system prompt, or System Settings, is about to come up in ANOTHER
408	    /// process at normal window level, and a `.floating` panel sits over
409	    /// every normal window on the screen: the person found the Screen
410	    /// Recording prompt hidden behind the panel until they dragged it away
411	    /// (2026-09-28). So the panel steps down to `.normal` first, and
412	    /// `floatAgain` puts it back on the next press that goes on, or on
413	    /// `show()`.
414	    func stepAsideForSystemUI() { window?.level = .normal }
415	    func floatAgain() { window?.level = .floating }

417	    /// Screen Recording, for a press: true to go on; false with the note
418	    /// set, and the press ends. `screenStep` is the one decision point.
419	    func checkScreenRecordingGrant() -> Bool {
420	        floatAgain()
421	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
422	        let owned = doors.launchedByLaunchd()
423	        let step = RecordingGrant.screenStep(
424	            granted: doors.screenGranted(), asked: doors.screenAsked(), launchedByLaunchd: owned)
425	        switch step {
426	        case .proceed:
427	            return true
428	        case .ask:
429	            if owned { doors.rememberScreenAsked() }
430	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
431	            doors.requestScreen()
432	            setNote(RecordingGrant.screenRecordingRefusal)
433	            return false
434	        case .openPane:
435	            stepAsideForSystemUI()
436	            let opened = RecordingGrant.screenRecordingPaneURL.map(doors.openSettings) ?? false
437	            setNote(
438	                opened ? RecordingGrant.screenRecordingOpenedNote : RecordingGrant.screenRecordingRefusal)
439	            return false
440	        }

445	    /// the note set, and the press ends. `inputMonitoringStep` decides.

447	        guard currentChoice().keys == .shortcuts else { return true }
448	        floatAgain()
449	        let doors = Self.grantDoors
450	        let owned = doors.launchedByLaunchd()
451	        let step = RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringStep(

462	            setNote(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringNote(opened: opened))

464	        case .openPane:
465	            stepAsideForSystemUI()

467	            setNote(RecordingGrant.inputMonitoringNote(opened: opened))
468	            return false
469	        }
470	    }

473	    /// authorized); false when it asked (the answer continues the press) or
474	    /// opened its pane.

30	    /// The arguments a camera recording refuses by name (CAM-4 point 3),
31	    /// in the order the refusal lists them: everything only a screen's
32	    /// picture or stream reads, and `rate` — a camera records at its own
33	    /// format's rate.
34	    static let cameraRefusedArguments = [
35	        "display", "window", "system_audio", "show_clicks", "size", "include_framejob_windows",
36	        "keys", "cursor", "auto_zoom", "shortcut_overlays", "speed_up_typing", "camera_layout",
37	        "camera_cutout", "rate",

40	    /// `camera` (CAM-4 point 1): a device's `uniqueID` or name, trimmed; nil
41	    /// when absent, a JSON null, or blank — absent takes the default camera.
42	    /// A value that is not a string is `stringArg`'s refusal.
43	    func recordingCameraArgument(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String? {
44	        guard let raw = try stringArg(a, "camera") else { return nil }
45	        let trimmed = raw.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
46	        return trimmed.isEmpty ? nil : trimmed
47	    }

49	    /// `camera_format` (CAM-6 (6)): trimmed; nil when absent, a JSON null,
50	    /// or blank — absent is Best. A value that is not a string is
51	    /// `stringArg`'s refusal.
52	    func recordingCameraFormatArgument(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String? {
53	        guard let raw = try stringArg(a, "camera_format") else { return nil }
54	        let trimmed = raw.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
55	        return trimmed.isEmpty ? nil : trimmed

58	    /// CAM-4 points 2 and 3 with CAM-6 (6), as CAM-10 (5) amends them,
59	    /// called by `recordingSourceKind` right after `source`'s value: with
60	    /// source `voice_over`, the given ones of `camera`, `camera_format`,
61	    /// `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout` (CO-83 (a)) are refused together

63	    /// `camera_format`, `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout` given without
64	    /// `camera` is refused (a camera beside the screen is named by
65	    /// `camera`); with `camera`, the given ones of
66	    /// `cameraRefusedArguments` (a JSON null is not given, `scalarArg`'s
67	    /// rule) are refused together, in that order.
68	    func recordingCameraStrangers(_ a: [String: Any], kind: RecordingSourceKind) throws {
69	        let camera = try recordingCameraArgument(a)
70	        let format = try recordingCameraFormatArgument(a)
71	        // CO-83 (a): the landing's two, given when present and not a JSON null.
72	        let landing = ["camera_layout", "camera_cutout"].filter {
73	            a[$0] != nil && !(a[$0] is NSNull)
74	        }
75	        let given =
76	            [("camera", camera), ("camera_format", format)].filter { $0.1 != nil }.map(\.0)
77	            + landing
78	        guard kind != .voiceOver || given.isEmpty else {
79	            throw ToolError(
80	                message: "With source voice_over, " + given.joined(separator: ", ")
81	                    + " cannot be given — a voice-over records the microphone alone.")
82	        }
83	        let beside = (format != nil ? ["camera_format"] : []) + landing
84	        if kind == .screen, camera == nil, let first = beside.first {
85	            throw ToolError(
86	                message: "With source screen, \(first) needs camera — name the camera to "
87	                    + "record beside the screen.")
88	        }
89	        guard kind == .camera else { return }
90	        let strangers = Self.cameraRefusedArguments.filter { a[$0] != nil && !(a[$0] is NSNull) }
91	        guard strangers.isEmpty else {
92	            throw ToolError(
93	                message: "With source camera, " + strangers.joined(separator: ", ")
94	                    + " cannot be given — a camera recording records the camera alone, at the "
95	                    + "camera's own format.")
96	        }

101	    /// with the vocabulary), then with `place: false` a given layout and a true cutout, each in

109	        let cutout = try boolArg(a, "camera_cutout") ?? false

123	    /// CAM-3 (7) then (8), pure: the camera `wanted` names
124	    /// (`CameraDevices.match`), or the default (`CameraDevices.defaultIndex`)
125	    /// when it is nil — "No camera is connected." when none is, a sentence
126	    /// naming every camera present when the name or id is unknown — then

128	    /// is Best, else `CameraDevices.formatMatch`, a miss refused naming the
129	    /// camera's formats), and only then the grant, `status`, refused by
130	    /// `RecordingGrant.cameraRefusal` unless `.authorized`.
131	    static func recordingCameraPick(
132	        _ wanted: String?, format wantedFormat: String?, in cameras: [CameraDeviceFacts],
133	        preferredID: String?, status: AVAuthorizationStatus
134	    ) throws -> CameraPick {
135	        let index: Int?
136	        if let wanted {
137	            index = CameraDevices.match(wanted, in: cameras)
138	        } else {
139	            index = CameraDevices.defaultIndex(in: cameras, preferredID: preferredID)
140	        }
141	        guard let index else {
142	            throw ToolError(
143	                message: wanted.map { CameraDevices.noSuchCameraSentence($0, cameras: cameras) }
144	                    ?? CameraDevices.noCameraSentence)
145	        }
146	        var format: String?
147	        if let wantedFormat, wantedFormat.caseInsensitiveCompare("best") != .orderedSame {
148	            format = CameraDevices.formatMatch(wantedFormat, in: cameras[index].formats)
149	            guard format != nil else {
150	                throw ToolError(
151	                    message: CameraDevices.noSuchFormatSentence(
152	                        wantedFormat, camera: cameras[index]))
153	            }
154	        }
155	        guard status == .authorized else {
156	            throw ToolError(message: RecordingGrant.cameraRefusal(status))
157	        }
158	        return CameraPick(id: cameras[index].uniqueID, format: format)
159	    }

168	        return try onMain {

171	                in: CameraDevices.connected().map(CameraDevices.facts(of:)),
172	                preferredID: AVCaptureDevice.systemPreferredCamera?.uniqueID,

247	    /// SERVER THREAD. CU-101 (j): for each command the choice asks for, in order, `decide`
248	    /// polled through `onMain` every `RecordingPolish.checkInterval`, then the tool's body; its
249	    /// answer object under the command's name, or a sentence under `<name>_error`. On `.drop`,
250	    /// `.giveUp` or the call's cancel, every command not yet run gets its sentence. The cursor
251	    /// files are read here, once, for the speed-up's readiness; a read that fails counts as
252	    /// ready, so the body says why.
253	    func polishLanded(
254	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument, into fields: inout [String: Any]
255	    ) {
256	        var remaining = RecordingPolish.commands(of: result.choice)
257	        guard !remaining.isEmpty else { return }
258	        let stop = AgentLane.shared.callCancel
259	        let paths = RecordingPolish.screenPaths(of: result)
260	        let scope = onMain { document.scope }
261	        var tracks: [UInt32: ReelCursor]?
262	        var started = Date()
263	        func fail(_ sentence: (RecordingPolish.Command) -> String) {
264	            for command in remaining { fields[command.rawValue + "_error"] = sentence(command) }
265	            remaining = []
266	        }
267	        while let command = remaining.first {
268	            if stop?.isCancelled == true {
269	                fail(RecordingPolish.stoppedSentence)
270	                break
271	            }
272	            if command == .speedUpTyping, tracks == nil {
273	                let files = onMain { () -> [UInt32: URL] in
274	                    let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
275	                    let clips = RecordingPolish.screenClips(paths, in: document)
276	                    return (try? AutoZoom.cursorFiles(
277	                        clips.compactMap { snapshot.clip($0) }, in: snapshot)) ?? [:]
278	                }
279	                tracks = (try? AutoZoom.readTracks(files)) ?? [:]
280	            }
281	            let held = tracks ?? [:]
282	            let step = onMain { () -> RecordingPolish.Step in
283	                let clips = RecordingPolish.screenClips(paths, in: document)
284	                let ready =
285	                    !clips.isEmpty
286	                    && RecordingPolish.isReady(
287	                        command, clips: clips, tracks: held, speedUp: SpeedUpTypingSettings(),
288	                        in: document)
289	                return RecordingPolish.decide(
290	                    command: command, clips: clips,
291	                    enhancing: RecordingEnhance.isPending(document), ready: ready,
292	                    busy: RecordingEnhance.isBusy(document, scope: scope),
293	                    elapsed: Date().timeIntervalSince(started))
294	            }
295	            switch step {
296	            case .wait:
297	                Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: RecordingPolish.checkInterval)
298	            case .drop:
299	                fail(RecordingPolish.noScreenSentence)
300	            case .giveUp:
301	                fail { RecordingPolish.notReadySentence($0, tool: true) }
302	            case .run(let ran, let clips):
303	                do {
304	                    let answer = try polish(ran, document: document, clips: clips)
305	                    fields[ran.rawValue] = Self.resultObject(answer) ?? answer
306	                } catch let error as ToolError {
307	                    fields[ran.rawValue + "_error"] = error.message
308	                } catch {
309	                    fields[ran.rawValue + "_error"] = error.localizedDescription
310	                }
311	                remaining.removeFirst()
312	                started = Date()
313	            }
314	        }
315	        onMain { RecordingPolish.forgetWait(document) }
316	    }
317	
318	    /// One command through its tool's body at the tools' defaults. SERVER THREAD.
319	    private func polish(
320	        _ command: RecordingPolish.Command, document: ProjectDocument, clips: [UInt32]
321	    ) throws -> String {
322	        switch command {
323	        case .autoZoom:
324	            return try autoZoom(document: document, clips: clips, settings: AutoZoomSettings())
325	        case .shortcutOverlays:
326	            return try addShortcutOverlays(
327	                document: document, clips: clips, settings: ShortcutOverlaySettings())
328	        case .speedUpTyping:
329	            return try speedUpTyping(
330	                document: document, clips: clips, settings: SpeedUpTypingSettings())
331	        }
332	    }
333	}

336	/// `record_screen`'s RESULT shaping and its SENTENCES — what the answer says
337	/// about the files and the ids they landed as, and what a refusal says once
338	/// a file is on disk — cut out of `AgentServer+Recording.swift` when that
339	/// file stood at 397 lines against app/CLAUDE.md's 400-line cap for a new
340	/// file, with the R1 review's fixes still to land on it. The seam is the one
341	/// the file already had: `record_screen`'s waits and its argument vocabulary
342	/// stay there; the pure functions from a `RecordingResult` (and a document,
343	/// or an error) to result fields and sentences are here. Every member is
344	/// `static` and reads nothing off the server, which is what made them the
345	/// cut: the other side keeps the semaphores and the `onMain` hops, this side
346	/// keeps what a probe could call with no server at all. `private` →
347	/// internal is the whole cost, because a `private` extension member reaches
348	/// only its own file. The SENTENCES moved on to
349	/// `AgentServer+RecordingSentences.swift` at camera-recording CR3-0.
350	///
351	/// **Road map 3, R2d — a recording is a SEQUENCE of files** (decision 6): a
352	/// `RecordingResult` carries `segments`, one per stretch between a start or
353	/// resume and a pause or the stop, and there is deliberately no
354	/// `result.micDescriptor` or `result.micOffset` any more — those are a
355	/// segment's, and this file used to read both off the result. So the answer
356	/// grew two keys that are ALWAYS present, `pauses` and `segments`, and every
357	/// top-level key keeps its R1 meaning for the FIRST segment — the recording's
358	/// file, the one a new project is addressed by — except `duration`, which is
359	/// the TOTAL recorded and for an unpaused recording is the number it always
360	/// was. The ids are carried per segment as `RecordingSegmentIds`, ONE shape
361	/// for both doors, filled by `newProjectIds` (every file looked up by path
362	/// on the document `untitled(around:)` built) and `documentIds` (the
363	/// placement's four lists, each indexed by SEGMENT — one entry per segment
364	/// since the R2 review, nil where nothing was minted — the ids it predicted
365	/// and the panel selects), so `recordingFields` derives the top-level four
366	/// from the first entry and no caller writes an id key by hand. Each entry
367	/// of `segments` also carries its own `width`, `height` and `fps`, because
368	/// on a variable-rate file `fps` genuinely differs from segment to segment.
369	///
370	/// **A failure after the recording was written names the file** (R1 review):
371	/// the recorder's own `.filesKept` already does that for a failure INSIDE
372	/// the recorder, and `savedButNotAdded` is the same rule for the three
373	/// places the TOOL can fail after a clean result — the placement's trial,
374	/// the commit, and the untitled document — because a caller told only "a
375	/// drag is in progress" has no way to find the footage that exists. The
376	/// files are spelled by `RecordingResult.filesClause`, the ONE spelling the
377	/// panel's note shares: every movie comma-joined, then every microphone file
378	/// that landed; the one-segment sentence is byte for byte R1's.
379	extension AgentServer {
380	
381	    // MARK: - The result
382	
383	    /// The ids ONE segment's files landed as, each nil until known: a
384	    /// `place: false` landing mints no clip, a segment whose microphone
385	    /// failed has no `micMedia`, and a result built before any landing
386	    /// (a probe's, or a throw's) has none of the four. `cameraMedia` and
387	    /// `cameraClip` are a camera beside the screen's (spec §11 CAM-10 (6)),
388	    /// written per segment only, never at the top level.
389	    struct RecordingSegmentIds {
390	        var media: UInt32?
391	        var clip: UInt32?
392	        var micMedia: UInt32?
393	        var micClip: UInt32?
394	        var cameraMedia: UInt32?
395	        var cameraClip: UInt32?
396	
397	        init(
398	            media: UInt32? = nil, clip: UInt32? = nil, micMedia: UInt32? = nil,
399	            micClip: UInt32? = nil, cameraMedia: UInt32? = nil, cameraClip: UInt32? = nil
400	        ) {
401	            self.media = media
402	            self.clip = clip
403	            self.micMedia = micMedia
404	            self.micClip = micClip
405	            self.cameraMedia = cameraMedia
406	            self.cameraClip = cameraClip
407	        }
408	    }
409	
410	    /// What the files are, and — through `ids`, one entry per segment in
411	    /// order, absent entries reading as unknown — where they landed. The
412	    /// top-level keys are the FIRST segment's: `path`, `width`, `height`,
413	    /// `fps`, `has_audio`, `audio_tracks` (what the MOVIE holds, 1 with
414	    /// system audio, else 0: the microphone is a second file, reported as
415	    /// `mic_path` and `mic_duration`, never a second track of this one),
416	    /// `mic_offset` — ALWAYS present, 0 for a segment with no microphone,
417	    /// because the key is a measurement and not a flag: `mic_path` is what
418	    /// says whether a file landed — and `media` / `clip` / `mic_media` /
419	    /// `mic_clip` from `ids.first`. `duration` is the SUM of every
420	    /// segment's — the total recorded, the paused stretches excluded because
421	    /// no file holds them.
422	    /// `mic_problem` is every segment's sentence joined
423	    /// (`RecordingResult.micProblem`), present when any segment's microphone
424	    /// was asked for and did not land — which is why, unlike R1, it can
425	    /// stand beside a `mic_path`: a second segment's failure leaves the
426	    /// first's file in place. `pauses` and `segments` are always present;
427	    /// `segments` has exactly one entry for a recording never paused.
428	    /// `unreadable` (#97) is present only when a segment was LEFT OUT because
429	    /// its movie would not probe, or its writer failed after it closed (#181):
430	    /// one entry per such segment, in order, with its movie's `path`, the
431	    /// `kept_files` still on disk and the `reason` — and, when its
432	    /// microphone file read (#181 item 2), `mic_path` and `mic_duration`,
433	    /// with `mic_media` and `mic_clip` from `leftOutIds` (one entry per
434	    /// left-out segment) when known. `camera` (spec §11 CAM-4) is present
435	    /// exactly when the result has one (`cameraFields`).
436	    static func recordingFields(
437	        _ result: RecordingResult, ids: [RecordingSegmentIds] = [],
438	        leftOutIds: [RecordingSegmentIds] = []
439	    ) -> [String: Any] {
440	        let first = result.segments[0]
441	        let movie = first.descriptor
442	        let total = result.segments.reduce(Ticks(0)) { $0 + $1.descriptor.duration }
443	        let segments = result.segments.enumerated().map { index, segment in
444	            segmentFields(segment, ids: index < ids.count ? ids[index] : nil)
445	        }
446	        var fields: [String: Any] = [
447	            "path": movie.path, "duration": total, "width": movie.width,
448	            "height": movie.height, "fps": [movie.fps.num, movie.fps.den],
449	            "has_audio": movie.hasAudio, "audio_tracks": movie.hasAudio ? 1 : 0,
450	            "mic_offset": first.micOffset, "stopped_by": stopReasonName(result.stoppedBy),
451	            "pauses": result.pauses, "segments": segments,
452	        ]
453	        if let mic = first.micDescriptor {
454	            fields["mic_path"] = mic.path
455	            fields["mic_duration"] = mic.duration
456	        }
457	        if let problem = result.micProblem { fields["mic_problem"] = problem }
458	        if let camera = result.camera {
459	            fields["camera"] = cameraFields(camera, id: result.choice.camera)
460	        }
461	        if !result.unreadable.isEmpty {
462	            fields["unreadable"] = result.unreadable.enumerated().map { i, left -> [String: Any] in
463	                var entry: [String: Any] = [
464	                    "path": left.moviePath, "kept_files": left.keptFiles,
465	                    "reason": left.error.localizedDescription,
466	                ]
467	                if let mic = left.micDescriptor {
468	                    entry["mic_path"] = mic.path
469	                    entry["mic_duration"] = mic.duration
470	                }
471	                let known = i < leftOutIds.count ? leftOutIds[i] : nil
472	                if let id = known?.micMedia { entry["mic_media"] = Int(id) }
473	                if let id = known?.micClip { entry["mic_clip"] = Int(id) }
474	                return entry
475	            }
476	        }
477	        fields.merge(idFields(ids.first)) { _, new in new }
478	        return fields
479	    }
480	
481	    /// One entry of `segments`: `path`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps`
482	    /// (this FILE's, which on a variable-rate recording differs per segment
483	    /// — the top level's is the first segment's) and `started_at` (the
484	    /// screen's did-start, `startedAtFormatter`'s spelling), then `mic_path`,
485	    /// `mic_duration`, `mic_offset` (always, 0 with no microphone) and
486	    /// `mic_problem` on the top level's terms for THIS segment's files, and
487	    /// the four ids when known. A camera beside the screen (spec §11 CAM-10
488	    /// (6)) adds `camera_path`, `camera_duration` and `camera_offset` when
489	    /// the segment has a camera file, `camera_problem` and `camera_note`
490	    /// when set, and `camera_media` and `camera_clip` when known.
491	    static func segmentFields(
492	        _ segment: RecordingSegment, ids: RecordingSegmentIds? = nil
493	    ) -> [String: Any] {
494	        let movie = segment.descriptor
495	        var fields: [String: Any] = [
496	            "path": movie.path, "duration": movie.duration, "width": movie.width,
497	            "height": movie.height, "fps": [movie.fps.num, movie.fps.den],
498	            "started_at": startedAtFormatter.string(from: segment.startedAt),
499	            "mic_offset": segment.micOffset,
500	        ]
501	        if let mic = segment.micDescriptor {
502	            fields["mic_path"] = mic.path
503	            fields["mic_duration"] = mic.duration
504	        }
505	        if let problem = segment.micProblem { fields["mic_problem"] = problem }
506	        if let camera = segment.cameraDescriptor {
507	            fields["camera_path"] = camera.path
508	            fields["camera_duration"] = camera.duration
509	            fields["camera_offset"] = segment.cameraOffset
510	        }
511	        if let problem = segment.cameraProblem { fields["camera_problem"] = problem }
512	        if let note = segment.cameraNote { fields["camera_note"] = note }
513	        if let id = ids?.cameraMedia { fields["camera_media"] = Int(id) }
514	        if let id = ids?.cameraClip { fields["camera_clip"] = Int(id) }
515	        // The segment's cursor file beside its movie (spec §11 CU-18).
516	        if let url = segment.cursorURL { fields["cursor_path"] = url.path }
517	        if segment.cursorURL != nil, let image = segment.cursorImage {
518	            fields["cursor_image"] = image.rawValue
519	        }
520	        if let problem = segment.cursorProblem { fields["cursor_problem"] = problem }
521	        fields.merge(idFields(ids)) { _, new in new }
522	        return fields
523	    }
524	
525	    /// `started_at`'s spelling: ISO 8601 in UTC to the millisecond
526	    /// (`2026-09-12T13:04:22.417Z`). The server reports no other date, so
527	    /// there was no spelling to match; UTC because the file's own name
528	    /// (`RecordingFiles.stem`) is already the local-time reading of the same
529	    /// instant and a second local spelling would say nothing new, and the
530	    /// fraction because the segments' offsets are measured in milliseconds.
531	    static let startedAtFormatter: ISO8601DateFormatter = {
532	        let formatter = ISO8601DateFormatter()
533	        formatter.formatOptions = [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds]
534	        formatter.timeZone = TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0)
535	        return formatter
536	    }()
537	
538	    private static func idFields(_ ids: RecordingSegmentIds?) -> [String: Any] {
539	        var fields: [String: Any] = [:]
540	        if let id = ids?.media { fields["media"] = Int(id) }
541	        if let id = ids?.clip { fields["clip"] = Int(id) }
542	        if let id = ids?.micMedia { fields["mic_media"] = Int(id) }
543	        if let id = ids?.micClip { fields["mic_clip"] = Int(id) }
544	        return fields
545	    }
546	
547	    static func stopReasonName(_ reason: StopReason) -> String {
548	        switch reason {
549	        case .stopped: return "stopped"
550	        case .userStopped: return "user_stopped"
551	        case .systemStopped: return "system_stopped"
552	        }
553	    }
554	
555	    /// The `note` clause for a result some segment's microphone did not
556	    /// land for — the pictures are in the project and the answer must say
557	    /// what is missing. Over the JOINED problems, whose sentences name the
558	    /// segment's file when one was left behind. A voice-over has no picture:
559	    /// its problem — a microphone that stopped on its own — is said verbatim.
560	    static func microphoneNote(_ result: RecordingResult) -> String? {
561	        if result.isVoiceOver { return result.micProblem }
562	        return result.micProblem.map {
563	            "The picture landed without its microphone — the microphone file could not be "
564	                + "used: " + $0
565	        }
566	    }
567	
568	    /// The result's own `note` clauses, in order: the segments left out as
569	    /// unreadable (#97), the left-out voices that landed (#181 item 2), the
570	    /// microphone's, then a camera's `problem` and `note`, verbatim (CAM-4),
571	    /// then every segment's camera sentences beside the screen
572	    /// (`cameraSegmentsNote`, CAM-10 (6)). Both doors append these after their
573	    /// own, on a landing that succeeded only.
574	    static func resultNotes(_ result: RecordingResult) -> [String] {
575	        [
576	            result.unreadableNote, result.leftOutVoiceNote, microphoneNote(result),
577	            result.camera?.problem, result.camera?.note,
578	            result.cameraSegmentsNote,
579	            // Every segment's cursor problem (spec §11 CU-18), last.
580	            result.cursorSegmentsNote,
581	        ].compactMap { $0 }
582	    }
583	
584	    /// The ids a new project holds for every segment's files, read off its
585	    /// snapshot by path, SEGMENT BY SEGMENT — `untitled(around:)` placed
586	    /// them (the first picture as the document, the rest through
587	    /// `remainderPlacement`), so nothing here predicted an id, and a file
588	    /// the remainder landed as media alone (its sentence in the landing's
589	    /// `notes`) answers a `media` and no `clip`, which is the truth. A new
590	    /// project has no nest, so its top-level clips are the only clips there
591	    /// are.
592	    static func newProjectIds(
593	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument
594	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
595	        let snapshot = document.project.snapshot
596	        return result.segments.map { segment in
597	            let media = landedMedia(for: segment.descriptor.path, in: snapshot)
598	            let micMedia = segment.micDescriptor.flatMap { landedMedia(for: $0.path, in: snapshot) }
599	            let cameraMedia = segment.cameraDescriptor.flatMap {
600	                landedMedia(for: $0.path, in: snapshot)
601	            }
602	            return RecordingSegmentIds(
603	                media: media, clip: media.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) },
604	                micMedia: micMedia, micClip: micMedia.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) },
605	                cameraMedia: cameraMedia,
606	                cameraClip: cameraMedia.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) })
607	        }
608	    }
609	
610	    /// The ids a DOCUMENT landing gives every segment — the placement's own
611	    /// four lists, the ids it predicted off the purely-applied trial (R1's
612	    /// contract: `next_id` before each op that mints) and the ones the panel
613	    /// selects, so the tool reports what the panel highlights. All four
614	    /// lists have ONE entry per segment, in order, nil where nothing was
615	    /// minted (`Placement`'s doc), so every one is indexed by SEGMENT and
616	    /// none is consumed by an iterator — the first shape here walked the two
617	    /// `mic…` lists as "segments with a microphone file" were met, and a
618	    /// voice that minted no clip then shifted every later segment's ids by
619	    /// one. Read BEFORE the commit, as R1 read the singulars, which is what
620	    /// lets `land()` keep `editResult`'s tail.
621	    static func documentIds(
622	        _ result: RecordingResult, placement: RecordingLanding.Placement
623	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
624	        func entry(_ list: [UInt32?], _ k: Int) -> UInt32? { k < list.count ? list[k] : nil }
625	        return result.segments.indices.map { k in
626	            RecordingSegmentIds(
627	                media: k < placement.mediaIds.count ? placement.mediaIds[k] : nil,
628	                clip: entry(placement.clipIds, k), micMedia: entry(placement.micMediaIds, k),
629	                micClip: entry(placement.micClipIds, k),
630	                cameraMedia: entry(placement.cameraMediaIds, k),
631	                cameraClip: entry(placement.cameraClipIds, k))
632	        }
633	    }
634	
635	    /// The ids a DOCUMENT landing gives each left-out segment's voice (#181
636	    /// item 2): the placement's two left-out lists, one entry per
637	    /// `result.unreadable`, `micMedia` and `micClip` only.
638	    static func documentLeftOutIds(
639	        _ result: RecordingResult, placement: RecordingLanding.Placement
640	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
641	        func entry(_ list: [UInt32?], _ i: Int) -> UInt32? { i < list.count ? list[i] : nil }
642	        return result.unreadable.indices.map { i in
643	            RecordingSegmentIds(
644	                micMedia: entry(placement.leftOutMicMediaIds, i),
645	                micClip: entry(placement.leftOutMicClipIds, i))
646	        }
647	    }
648	
649	    /// The ids a NEW project holds for each left-out segment's voice, read
650	    /// off its snapshot by trimmed path as `newProjectIds` reads the
651	    /// segments': a voice before the first segment is media with no clip.
652	    static func newProjectLeftOutIds(
653	        _ result: RecordingResult, in document: ProjectDocument
654	    ) -> [RecordingSegmentIds] {
655	        let snapshot = document.project.snapshot
656	        return result.unreadable.map { left in
657	            let micMedia = left.micDescriptor.flatMap { landedMedia(for: $0.path, in: snapshot) }
658	            return RecordingSegmentIds(
659	                micMedia: micMedia, micClip: micMedia.flatMap { landedClip(of: $0, in: snapshot) })
660	        }
661	    }
662	
663	    /// The media entry for `path`, matched TRIMMED because that is what the
664	    /// core stored (`RecordingLanding.addMedia`'s rule).
665	    private static func landedMedia(for path: String, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> UInt32? {
666	        let trimmed = path.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
667	        return snapshot.media.first(where: { $0.path == trimmed })?.id
668	    }
669	
670	    /// The first top-level clip whose source is `media`.
671	    private static func landedClip(of media: UInt32, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> UInt32? {
672	        snapshot.clips.first { clip in
673	            if case .media(let id, _, _) = clip.source { return id == media }
674	            return false
675	        }?.id
676	    }
677	}
